en: In the former Forno del Pane: Italian art from post-war to today and the largest public collection in the world dedicated to Giorgio Morandi.

Trapanese's agricultural municipality, between rural bays and countryside towards Segesta, with the Scorace Wood (Arcudaci), 750 hectares of greenery with views of the Gulf of Castellammare, and the Municipal Villa with the sculptures of Salvatore Galante.
The symbol of the village, with a view of the valley.
Etruscan tombs and paths in the green.

Borgo where the Enza valley opens onto the plain, already inhabited in the Etruscan age (Servirola) and the land of the Canossa; the medieval nucleus brings together the Rocca, today the town hall with the Museum of Resistance    \Salvo D'Acquisto, and the Church of the Castle with a fresco of Niccolò dell'Abate.
Among the most beautiful beaches in Calabria, with views of the Aeolian Islands.

Born from a missionary exhibition of the Franciscan friars of Trentino, it occupies three rooms on the ground floor of the convent-sanctuary with objects brought by the missions: from China paintings, embroidery on silk, paintings on rice paper and statuettes of divinity above all seven-nineteenth century; from the pre-incaic Andes finds in stone and ceramics, incaic images and Bolivian handicrafts; some windows on Africa. Opening on request.

Città sull'Adige, piazzaforte veneziana redesigned by Michele Sanmicheli since 1525 and then fortress of the Austrian Quadrilatero; it remains the fifteenth-century torrione, the marching lions and sections of walls, while the house-museum of the Fondazione Fioroni and the Archaeological Environmental Center tell Risorgimento and prehistory of the plain. Here Antonio Salieri was born in 1750.
For the little ones.

About 2,300 hectares between Guiglia, Marano sul Panaro and Zocca, with more than 100 km of trails in 12 itineraries for hiking, horse riding or mountain biking; there are the Sasso di Sant'Andrea and the Bosco delle Tane, chestnut groves with sandstone. The protected area recognised by the European Union is home to more than 80 species of birds, including the pilgrim hawk, and more than 40 mammals.
Long and quiet beach with the shade of the pine forest.
A high medieval church with Romanesque bell tower in the heart of the village.

Opened in 1994 at the former elementary school in Zorge, it recalls the mining history of the area, which ended in 1980 with the closure of the mines. On the ground floor the mining section, from the time of Leonardo da Vinci to the twentieth century, with original tools and the life-size reconstruction of the entrance of a gallery; on the first floor more than 2,000 minerals and 450 fossils of the Val Brembana and the world, including galena, staggered and local wulfenite and a showcase of fluorescent minerals; on the second floor multimedia and teaching materials.

Ancient citrus greenhouse (lemons, mandarin, bergamotti) at the port of Tignale, restored in 1985 and used as a museum, where the phases of the ancient cultivation are observed; since 2012 it is part of the Ecomuseum of the Limonaie del Garda. Guided tours only on request for groups of at least 10 people.

Village of huts around a nuraghe with tholos complex of which the central tower remains visible, in the Litterai district; among the huts the house of bread is paved circular environment with seats and bathtub, today attributed to a cult of the waters. The excavations have returned bronzes, basins for fusion and a statue of chief tribe.

Tomb of a powerful Etruscan family of the 6th century BC along the Via Clodia: the mound called "Grande Ruota" is 28 metres in diameter excavated in the tuff, with rooms connected by air wells, and downstream a cylindrical altar with traces of orientalizing frieze in the middle of a sort of rock theatre. Last dirt track, free access.

About 5 km of fine sandy beach with numerous establishments and a pedestrian promenade of palm trees imported from the Canaries in the early twentieth century; on viale Colombo, born in 1890 as Viale Marino, the Liberty villas. The bike path, about 20 km in all, connects San Benedetto del Tronto to the south and Cupra Marittima and Pedaso to the north.
The abandoned village on the lake peninsula.
The blue majolica that made Laterza famous.
The symbol of the city and the Rubicone.
Gardens and panorama at the entrance of the city.
Lava rock coves.
Low-altitude beech.

In a nineteenth-century manor house in the center of the village exhibits the finds of the park of Monte Luna and Santu Teru: amphorae, jugs, dishes, ointments and skylights, coins, Egyptian taste objects, Greek imports and center-italic (IV-III century BC), gold and silver jewels with scarab rings, pendants, necklaces, diadems and numerous amulets. It documents the continuity of population of the territory from the recent Neolithic to the Middle Ages, with the Nuragic finds of about Nuraxi of Sisini and of the nuraghi Simieri and Mount Uda, and has an ethnographic section. The famous bronzetto "miles cornutus" was found near the village in 1841, and is instead the National Archaeological Museum of Cagliari.
Church mentioned from 1300 and house of the fifteenth century in the Lavino valley.
The church that dominates the country.
Civic museum that preserves important archaeological finds and a collection defined among the most significant in Italy; it is part of the city museum circuit with the church of Sant'Antonio Abate.
The house of the patron and father-in-law of Verdi: in the hall, seat of the Philharmonic, the young composer performed for the first time in 1830; piano, portraits and letters autographs.
Contemporary art in the name of Pino Pascali.
Verdi's theater, backstage.

The historic centre preserves the medieval structure: St. Nicholas Square with the 18th-century staircase in curved brackets and the church of St. Nicholas, rebuilt in the eighteenth century on medieval foundations, the Renaissance Palazzo Borghese and Palazzo Crescenzi, dating back to the year 1000 and now home of the Municipal Library. From the village the view opens onto the plain of the Tiber.

In the Friulian plain, Aiello del Friuli preserves the largest ethnographic collection of the region, the Museum of peasant civilization of the Imperial Friuli, and is known for the numerous sundials painted on the walls of houses and public buildings; it is also a stop of the Celestial Way between Aquileia and Cormòns.
Tower of 1321, today library, and the gate to the castle of 1403.

Parish church built on a project by Aniello Francia and completed in 1838, on a hill in the middle of the hamlet, in the hilly area of Val del Fino. It has a single rectangular nave marked by Ionian binated pilasters on three spans, with the central covered by a lower dome on plumes; the neoclassical brick façade is crowned by a large triangular tympanum with denticles and has triglyphs in the stripe marchepiano.
The story of the alum that gave the country its name.

Garibaldi settled in Caprera in 1856 and since 1866 built the White House in granite and plaster, with eight communicating rooms, including the bedroom with the deathbed: the clock is stopped at 18.21 on June 2nd 1882. In the courtyard the wooden house, the iron house, the crusher, oven, stable, mill and the Clelia's pino planted in 1867; a path leads to the granite tomb of the general in the family grave. Open Monday to Saturday 8.30-19.30 (last entry 18.30).

The tower is today a multifunctional cultural centre with a permanent exhibition dedicated to actor Nino Manfredi, born in Castro dei Volsci in 1921; the visit is on reservation. Near Piazza IV Novembre there is a monument to the actor and a bas-relief of Umberto Cufrini realized for the centenary of the birth.

Itinerary on trails and mule tracks that retrace the last three stages of the return of the Valdese from exile in Switzerland in 1689, through the Valdese valleys, with also naturalistic and landscape value; touches Massello with the museum of Balsiglia, Prali and Salza di Pinerolo. Trail card and GPS track downloadable from the site of the Ecomuseo.
The Cremonese baroque.

Founded by the Benedictines in the first half of the 10th century (first definite news in 984) between the Via Salaria and Velino, it depended directly on the Holy See; burned during the Norman invasion, it was rebuilt by the abbot Sinibaldo and consecrated in 1179, and was abandoned at the end of the 18th century. It preserves the fortified structure with quadrangular wall and Romanesque elements, and in the center an imposing bell tower used as a sighting tower, with sculptures of a human head, an abbot with miter and pastoral and a lion head.
Permanent collection of more than 100 sculptor's works including sketches, paintings, bronzes, juta works and silkscreens.
The necropolis of the Peucezi.
Sacred art a stone's throw from the Fontana Maggiore.

In the fortress are located the historical and multimedia Museum of Bartolomeo d'Alviano and the captains of Ventura Umbria, the Museum of peasant civilization and the Centre of Faunistic Documentation of the Oasis of Alviano.

The massif above Temple, 1362 meters high, on the border with the Logudoro: CAI paths and bike paths, and on clear days the view arrives at Tavolara, at the lake of Coghinas, at the Maddalena and at the Asinara. In the gorge of the Rio Pisciaroni small waterfalls and granite tanks.

The castle, built by the Angioini after 1231 and renovated in the sixteenth century by Evangelista Menga for Pirro Castriota, was restored in 1911 by architect Adolfo Avena; it dominates the village and has been restored to the sixteenth-century forms.
The 17th century church was built by the congregation of the same name by vote of the population against the plague.
Fortress of the beginning of the fourth century BC wanted by Dionysius I on the Epipolis plateau, about 8 km from the center: defensive moats and ruins on 1.5 hectares overlooking the city.
The last medieval door of the village.
Rebuilt since 1746 after the earthquake and restored in the twentieth century, it has the bell tower unusually located on the back.
Numerous sundials placed by a group of enthusiasts on the walls of houses and public buildings of the village; the last Sunday of May the sundial Festival brings exhibitions, music and shows.
A Guido Reni on Via Emilia.
Schellino's neo-Gothic and Einaudi's tomb.
Frescoes of the fourteenth century rediscovered by chance.
Roman captains walled up in the houses.

Massif in the center of Umbria, about 45 km long, with grassy ridges, holm oaks, forre, dolines and caves; there live the butterfly Charaxes jasius and the Rosalia alpina, raptors, peaks and roe deer. The Martani Trekking, created in the mid-eighties by the Region, is a double ring path between ridges, woods, medieval villages and historical roads, for hikers, knights and mountain bikes.

Restoration center on the large square where the works saved from churches and collapsed buildings are recovered: here the organ of the church of Suffragio and several large canvases now at the museum Floriana Switzerland; the restorer Stefania Zucconi welcomes visitors.

Well-preserved structure and several times transformed, probably of Longobard origin; devastated by the Saracens, it was rebuilt by the Normans. Families such as the Gesualdo, the Filangieri, the Ludovisi and the Carafa stayed there.
Building erected in 1577, today seat of cultural initiatives.
A Romanesque crucifix of the thirteenth century.
The Chianti Rufina in his castle.
A rare memory on the sea.
The "sea" of the Florentines.
A theatre born in a greenhouse.

Borgo del Fermano where he was born in 1894 and died in 1958 the painter Osvaldo Licini: on the square dedicated to him the eighteenth-century house where he lived and the Center studies with drawings and writings; in the village the parish church of San Vito Martire, the walls of the Three-Fourteenth century and views from the hills to the sea to the Sibillini.
A fresco attributed to Pinturicchio.
The port can be reached by a daily shuttle or by a path that goes down to the lake; it has an equipped beach, a bar, an area for animals and you practice windsurfing, kayaking and sailing.
MiC card (updated 2020) says it is closed every day and run by volunteers; re-arranged in the MUD in June 2026, unpublished times

Built in the fourteenth century as a fortification to defend Milan, with a square plan with four corner towers: the north-west one is in ruins and the south-east one is the only one still standing. Terracotta walls and wooden beams roof; the east side, the most visited, shows visconteee mullioned windows, ancient battlements and the Visconteo biscion over the original entrance. Beatrice of Tenda, the second wife of Philip Maria Visconti, was beheaded in her walls, falsely accused of adultery.
Natural area of great biodiversity between Ligurian hills and Tuscan plains at the Magra Mouths; cormorants, seagulls and the kingfisher, symbol of the park.

15th century fortress built by the Venetians on the right bank of the Isonzo against Turkish invasions, to whose walls Leonardo da Vinci would have contributed; along the perimeter you can see six towers and two gates, Porta Nuova and Porta del Soccorso. Inside the walls the castle, whose core is the Palazzo del Capitano, the fifteenth-century Venetian House of Provveditori and streets porticoed with traditional coffee.
An agricultural village in Lombardy remained almost intact.
Free dunes and the sea.
A water sculpture in the square.

Under the old town there are caves dug into the tuff, on several levels and connected to each other, dating back to the Byzantine era and used in time as a refuge and cellar; today there matures the podolic caciocavallo, aged in cave for at least two years.
Andersen's bay.
History of the peaks and panoramic terrace.
The entrance door to the Stelvio Trentino Park.
Ionian sea and pine forest just a stone's throw from the ravines.

Houses leaning along narrow alleys that go up towards the area of the ancient Baronial Palace, today disappeared; around the village remain walls, water pipes and rustic villas of Roman age. Along the streets you will find the works of the local sculptor Andrea Gandini, who carves the folds of the tree trunks, including a trunk depicting Lenola with its perched houses.
The most famous mountain road in Italy.
The rooms where the only Piedmontese pope was born.
The historic residence of the lords of Pozzallo.
A surprising architecture.

Residence of the fourteenth century, the smallest of the three Orsini properties in the village, with an internal cloister in common with the Oratory of the Most Holy Stimmates; above the entrance the rose of the Orsini, inside a more elaborate coat of arms above the door of the loggia, travertine windows with stone seats and, in the basement, a preserved stone mill.
A Gonzaghesca villa of the school of Giulio Romano.

Called the "pearl of Gargano," Vieste combines a medieval old town with a castle and cathedral to a coast of high cliffs, sea caves and beaches like the Scialara, where stands the monolith of Pizzomunno, symbol of the city. In the village there is also a museum with thousands of shells from all over the world.
From the thirteenth century the political center of the city, with the public Palace of 1281 in white marble and red terracotta and the baroque equestrian statues of the Farnese by Francesco Mochi.
The districts of a country rebuilt after earthquakes.

In Muliparte, it is located on the site of the ancient castle and includes the oratory of San Giuseppe, with an eighteenth-century facade. Free visit on the first Monday of the month, with reservation required.
In Stolvizza, tools and photographs of the ancient craft of the Knife.
The Roman glass is the highlight.
The sixteenth-century church was built with the contribution of the Caccia family, whose design the Vignola had worked; in the central aisle an artistic pulpit with the coat of arms of the family.
A toast on the bridge.

Last village of Stroppo on the road to Elva, with a profile suspended in the sky which is a symbolic image of the Maira Valley. Ancient settlement: there was found a bronze bracelet from the IX-VIII century BC, today at the Civic Museum of Cuneo. To see the church of San Martino rebuilt in 1699, an ancient windmill with circular tower, the stone arch in the center, oven, washbasins and fountains; from the mule tracks start excursions to the high mountain.
The Castle, in the historic center behind the town hall square, restored and can be visited during the exhibitions or by appointment.
The museum with the Deposition from the Cross of Rosso Fiorentino (1521), masterpiece of Mannerism.
Treasury Museum by appointment, on offer: +39 329 4929871

On the remains of the Roman center of Forum Cassii, stop of the Via Francigena: in 1145 entrusted to the Order Gerosolimitano as a hospice for pilgrims, then the Knights of Malta. It preserves a great Crucifixion of the 11th-XII century, apsidal frescoes of the 12th century and a Madonna enthroned attributed to the young Masaccio (1423).

The hunting palace of the Savoys at the gates of Turin: the Baroque palace with the Gardens, the ancient village designed by Amedeo di Castellamonte and the Park La Mandria with the Castle of Vittorio Emanuele II.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Arnone, former prison of the city: Italian art from the sixteenth to the twentieth century with attention to the South, with works by Mattia Preti, Sebastiano Conca, Corrado Giaquinto, Luca Giordano and Umberto Boccioni.

Founded by the knight Attilio Benetti, to whom some ammonites and fossils are dedicated, it traces the evolution of life in the geological eras: a large collection of ammonites, remains of marine reptiles of tropical seabeds that were once Lessinia, dinosaur footprints and a skeleton complete with cave bear more than 3 meters high. From 15 June to the beginning of September open every day except Monday 9.30-12.30 and 15-18; in the rest of the year Saturday, Sunday and holidays 10-12 and 14.30-16.30; closed from mid-January to mid-March.
The Gonzaga coat of arms on Fancelli's building.
Access allowed only at organised events
With a fresco by Gregorio De Ferrari.
The monument to the Master is located at the entrance of the hospital of Villanova, which Verdi wanted to donate to the village.
€5, children up to 14 years free

The church of San Nicolò in Valdurna contains frescoes from the 15th century; sacred art also in the churches of Maria Assunta and San Cipriano in Sarentino, San Valentino al Gentersberg and San Giovanni nel Bosco near Pennes.
To be checked: same times as the Civic Museums
The sanctuary reached on foot.
Where the Grossetans meet.
Route on the history of printing, from lead characters to cast iron presses to the internet.
The Franciscan memory in the heart of the city.

Country on the eastern branch of Lake Como at the foot of the Grigne, known for the Civic Museum Setificio Monti, with one of the largest silk torcitoi operating in Europe; among the villages Borbino, Linzanico and Crebbio and, in the mountains, the Cascata del Cenghen.
The widest view of Italy.
The great armory of Trapp accounts.
The Samnite warriors of Aufidena and their suitcases.
Columbus' youth.
One of the classic Sibillini walks.
A high medieval church with pieces of the Roman city.
Small jewel designed by Borgese in 1750, with frescoes, decorations and well preserved stuccoes.

The city of San Francesco and Santa Chiara on Mount Subasio, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2000: the Basilica frescoed by Cimabue, Giotto, Lorenzetti and Simone Martini, the Temple of Minerva and the Franciscan places outside the walls.

Squares, fountains and districts with shops, cafes and buildings linked to Ladin culture; in Piaz de Ramon, Piaz de Sotegrava and Piazzatta Perla Alpina are held the Fairy Markets (edition 2026 from November 28 to January 6), with the pedestrian center in the late afternoon.
Basilica minor since 1949, houses the tombs of two popes, Clement IV and Hadrian V; the Romanesque portal has tortile columns and the bell tower sails a bell of 1259.

Waterfall about 97 meters high in the Gruppo di Tessa Nature Park, considered one of the most spectacular in the Alps: the water of the Zielbach river falls from a rock wall, fed by a steep gorge about 8 km long. The maximum flow rate is from May to July, with the snow melting; a marked path leads to a panoramic platform.
€13, reduced €11
A Gothic façade survived the earthquake.

On the hill of San Pancrazio, where a fortified building has been documented since 1107, the owner Gaetano Bonoris rebuilt his residence in neo-Gothic style since 1890, on the model of the medieval village of Turin of 1884 (inspired by the castles of Fénis and Issogne): project by Antonio Tagliaferri, completed with Carlo Melchiotti; frescoes by Giuseppe Rollini (1898-1900) in the chapel and baronale salon, furnishings by the Arboletti brothers, park redesigned in 1901 by Giuseppe Roda. Municipal since 1996. Open from April to October with guided tours on weekends; admission fee.

Borgo della Langa Astigiana, birthplace of Augusto Monti, dominated by the castle born as a Benedictine monastery in the 11th century, now town hall and seat of the Gipsoteca Edoardo Rubino; at its feet the medieval bridge with donkey back on the Bormida and, on the hills, the path to the Bricco del Moro.

Between Busso and Baranello, one of the richest centers of the Sanniti Pentri: a stone belt of about 3 km contains about 50 hectares and the peaks of 968 and 997 m, with three doors visible to oblique corridor (two excavated). The excavations have found homes, including the LN
The rascards.
The stone living room of the village.
closed for maintenance and refurbishing with reopening announced for September 22, 2026; until the full reopening ticket reduced to €2,50; closed on Mondays
access only by reservation (0833 555819, museum@comune.ugento.le.it) according to the Municipality
The medieval heart of the city.

Museum workshop hosted in the State Middle School Perlasca, exhibits the terracotta objects used by the Fermano families until the 1960s and the potter's instruments; next to there is a laboratory to experiment with the techniques of processing. During the school year, the students visit it, during the summer months visitors are accompanied by a tour operator.
The crucifix that spoke to Don Camillo.

The medieval nucleus on the top of the hills, called Terra, is the labyrinth of alleys, whitewashed houses and stairs that gave Ostuni the name of "white city." Of the original fifteen Aragonese towers, eight remain, which dominate the streets of the center.
Conciliar Church in the center of the village, inaugurated in 1971, realized by Francesco Vacchini on a project by Antonio Nervi. Open every day 8-12 and 15-19.
Elegant church with a high porch and statues outside and precious interior decorations, in a country rich in religious buildings and monuments.
A Guercino in the center of Pescara.
Inaugurated at the end of 2005 near the Tophet, in four rooms it tells the civilizations of the island and the findings of the necropolis and the Tophet of Sulky, with the model of the ancient port.
The new chessboard town built from the end of the nineteenth century on the floor of Davide Conversano, along Via D'Aquino and Via Di Palma, with Palazzo Amelio.
From the village to the panoramic summit between Piedmont and Liguria.

Born in 2000 to preserve the materials of Lachera, the late winter carnival that combines dance and theatre, with characters like Laché and Trapulin, music for violin and organ and a legend of revolt against the ius primae noctis. It exhibits costumes and masks of the Lachera and of Italian and European festivals, with temporary exhibitions in an ethnographic key; the archive has kept photos since 1909 and nineteenth-century scores.
The Mysteries of Antonio Russo.
The oldest fortress in Elba.
A Renaissance castle at the sea.
The city's collections.
Set up in the former spinning mill for which the country was known; it is visited by appointment and is indicated as accessible to people with disabilities.

Set up on the lakefront in the building of the Visitor Centre, it reconstructs a fishing house of the early twentieth century with objects donated by the Lesinesi and an ancient sandal, telling the lagoon culture of the Capitana, between land and water.
The treasures of the sanctuary of Juno Sospita.
One of the oldest churches in the Lattari Mountains.
Four museums in one building.
Museum of Humour in Art housed in Palazzo Sangallo, unique in Italy.

Set up on about 260 square meters in the catacombs of the Temple of San Cono, in four sections: wooden and majolica sculptures of the majolica that were active in Naso from the fifteenth to the seventeenth century; vestments, a bronze bell and objects of the confraternities; paintings and stone works, including the table "Madonna" with dormant Child, dating from the first decades of the sixteenth century, the circle of Joos van Cleve, and two ovals attributed to Olivio Sozzi; liturgical silvers and ex-vote. Open Monday 9-13, the other days 9-13 and 15-18.

Symbol of the village, in the historic center of the Piaz at the foot of the mountain: the nucleus is a tower of the fifteenth century, then incorporated in the baronial palace flanked by two ornamental towers; in the panoramic garden the church of Sant'Apollonia of the sixteenth century. Over the centuries, it has hosted noble houses and bishop-principles; today it is part of the Tamanini family and it welcomes events, weddings and art exhibitions.
A legendary climb of cycling.
Baroque Salento next to a medieval cemetery.
The Phoenician Punic sanctuary of the city.

In the protected area of Monteferrato Mount Javello, about 900 meters, is the highest point, with beech woods and a partisan command in the Second World War; near the Ebani, born from the reforestation of Giuseppe Vaj in the early nineteenth century, and the monumental cork on the road to Migliana. In Schignano the visitor center, the church of San Martino and the scenic road of 1967 towards Vaiano.

The house where the composer was born on February 29, 1792, bought by the Municipality in 1892 and national monument since 1904: prints, engravings, lithographs and portraits related to the life and works of Rossini.

City on the Dora Riparia linked to Alessandro Cruto, inventor of the carbon filament bulb: its opificio of 1885 hosts the eco-museum "Dream of light"; to see also the parish church of San Martino, Santa Maria del Ponte overlooking the river and the forest of the Ghiaro.
The place of Raphael's Marriage.
Gorge between limestone and Dolomite walls, natural monument, with the sanctuary of the patron; legend has it that the rock has opened for a miracle of St. George bishop of Suelli.

The capital of Carnia in the plain of But and Tagliamento, Tolmezzo has its heart in Piazza XX Settembre with the eighteenth-century Cathedral of San Martino; at Palazzo Campeis is the Carnic Museum of the Arts and Popular Traditions, one of the most important ethnographic museums in Europe, and above the city the fifteenth-century Tower Picotta offers views of the valley.
The garden of a traveler over a Roman theatre.
the MiC card shows the museum times in the text but indicates "Closed" every day in the table
Museum dedicated to Guglielmo Marconi, with 1,200 examples of different eras, from the first methods of communication to the technologies of the digital era.
About 2 km east, erected at the end of the sixteenth century and restored in 1710, with a pine forest equipped.
Lemonets terraced between Maiori and Minori.
Small museum in the former oratory of St. John the Baptist with three Madonnas with the Child of Simone Martini, of the Vecchietta and of John of Paul, painted for Castiglione and Rocca d'Orcia.

Municipality of Montagna Pistoiese was born in 2017 from the fusion of San Marcello Pistoiese and Piteglio, among chestnut woods, beech woods and streams: the suspended Bridge of Ferriere on the Lima, the medieval Bridge of Castruccio, the Towers of Popiglio, Gavinana with the Ferrucciano Museum and the parish church with the monumental organ, the Ferriera Papini of Maresca and the Observatory of Pian de' Termini.
The classic Waalweg of Meranese, departing from the village.
The ancient rose garden.

Built between 1676 and 1678 by the Serico entrepreneur Giò Gerolamo Galleani and reached almost intact until today, it is one of the oldest examples of industrial archaeology in Europe: a building with the appearance of an almost fortified noble residence, with two courtyards, cylindrical turrets at the corners and decorations in stucco and terracotta. The guided tours show the torccioi rebuilt in operation, the spinner, the spinning mill and some rooms; it hosts temporary exhibitions and the info point of the Gate of Valle.
The 19th century theatre where Toscanini played.

Founded by the Municipality in honor of the sculptor Fortunato Gacce, born in Polia in 1920: trained in a school of Calabrian art, after the war he settled in Vipiteno and perfected himself in the workshop of Antonio Benetton; gold medal in Stockholm in 1964, awarded in Stuttgart in 1967 and honored in 1990 by the king of Spain for "I guerrieri di Spagna" he died in Treviso in 2006. The cultural center also has a library of about 2,000 volumes and a conference room.
The Arab-Norman park that preserves the islet and the hydraulic system to irrigate the citrus groves.

The Romanesque-Pisan cathedral with the crucifix of Coppo di Marcovaldo, the reliquary of Ghiberti and the silver altar of San Jacopo (1287-1456), masterpiece of the Gothic goldsmithery, with a relic of the Apostle from Santiago.
A stop for those who love sacred art.

In the central square; a collapse of the ground visibly inclined the portal architrave, giving the church an unblemished appearance. It preserves the triptych of Ambrogio Lorenzetti (1340), with the Madonna and Child and Saints Peter and Paul, a Deposition of Salimbeni and the Madonna of the Rosary by Domenico Beccafumi.
The walls of the Samnites who resisted Rome.
The entrance to the medieval city.

The castle (XIV-XV century, enlarged in the 18th and 19th centuries) was already mentioned in 1164 in a diploma of Frederick I. It is surrounded by walls with two towers; it was born in the 13th century by the Templars Nicolao and Iacopo, and since 1855 it has been a municipal property. The museum tells about the pre-industrial processing of plaster, which was obtained here from the seventeenth century, and its use in the architecture of the Basso Monferrato from the sixteenth to the early twentieth century: crystals of selenite, tools, a model of furnace fed by sarmenti and dozens of panels from Piedmonti ceilings. From the castle the view ranges from Monferrato to Superga and the Alpine arch. Open on the first Sunday of the month (November-April 10-17, May-October 11-18), visit of about 45 minutes; on request you can also visit the plaster floors of the Town Hall and the Wine shop.
The most spectacular Baroque façade in the village, with the civic museum under the roof.

Medieval fortified village in stone of the Aterno valley, rebuilt after the earthquake of 2009, with cobbled alleys, steps, doors, walls and towers. In Piazza del Popolo the Fountain with 14th century Masks, symbol of the village; at the top of the hill the 15th century Clock Tower, with its ancient six-hour dial and permanent photographic exhibition on the memory of the eagle earthquake.
A terrace overlooking the sea and the feast of Our Lady on boats.
Country trip.
Benedictine abbey on the hill above the city, known for the large collection of ex-vote paintings.
€5, reduced €3 (under 18 and over 65), free up to 6 years
The fifteenth century of Piedmont.

Narrow alleys, arches, steep stairs, dry walls and houses with painted facades: the popular frescoes are linked to the devotion to Our Lady, who according to legend appeased the plague of 1628-1630. In Via Giusti 24 a Madonna enthroned that nurses the Child of the sixteenth century, in Via Baroni 13 a satirical image of 1672 with a king who offers money to Death. In the square the bronze monument to the coalmaker, with a girl and a kid, a man with wood and the cadasta called "poiat" .
It reproduces the installation of a Waldensian confessional school, developed in the nineteenth century thanks to English colonel Charles Beckwith, with documents on Waldensian history.
The 15th century frescoes by Antoine de Lonhy.
The place of death of Patriarch Bertrando, heart of Friulian history.
Medieval village in the heart of the Val di Cecina, with Larderello, where for the first time in the world electricity from geothermal energy has been produced.

In the hamlet there is a 13th-century tower, massive and with Ghibelline merlons, today surrounded by more recent buildings, and the 16th-century parish church that houses a Renaissance image of the Madonna.
The theatre of the founder.

A small village on the fishing side of Majella, linked to Pietro da Morrone, the future Celestine V: in its territory there are the Celestinian hermitages of Santo Spirito in Majella, the largest and most famous of the mountains, and San Bartolomeo in Legio, dug in the rock of the Vallone di Santo Spirito.
The symbol of Nice.
Gothic church of the 13th century with works from the 15th and 16th centuries and a portal with bas-reliefs of fishing scenes.
Treatment with the mother waters of the salt pans.

Romanesque, 1080, one of the oldest churches in the city: on the corner of the façade the pulpit from which in 1266 preached Thomas Aquinas; inside the fifteenth-century ceiling painting, an anthology of Viterbo painting from the fourteenth to the sixteenth century and the Longobard cloister rediscovered in 1954.

The remains of the Sibaritide from the protohistory to the Middle Ages, with the "Coscante toro" of the fifth century BC and the bronze armor and helmet of a fourth century BC Bruttia tomb; unique ticket with the park.

Small Romanesque church of the 12th century in a dominant position on a promontory above the village, with Romanesque bell tower and frescoes of the 16th century recently restored; view of the lake and the mountains.
The baptistery next to the Basilica of San Giovanni in Laterano, in the complex of the cathedral of Rome.

The village of Lomellina is dominated by the Visconti castle of the fourteenth century, surrounded by a large moat and a high circular tower, which with the adjacent Pila houses the museums and exhibitions of the Fondazione Sartirana Arte; in the surroundings the meandering lake formed by the sesia loops.
The museum that brings together the sacred works of art of the territory of Montalcino and an archaeological section, reported by Visit Tuscany between the stages in the village.
A walk under the arcades of the Bassa.
outside the Christmas period visitable only on telephone request (In Lombardy)
The frescoes by De Lisio.
Church of the 11th century that houses a fresco of San Sebastiano and a relic of the Holy Cross.
The Madonna of the Cintola painted on the altar.
To walk through the tombs of an ancient town of the Murgia.
A polygonal villa with a cloistered court, built between 1474 and 1495 for Bartolomeo della Rovere, residence of the bishops of Ferrara until 1797.
closed for restoration visits, reopening date not indicated by the source
Castle among oak woods; nearby grows one of the largest holm oaks in Umbria, estimated at around 200 years.

Monument of the 1st century AD, from the age of the flavian dynasty, when in Borgo Velino there was a Roman villa; its walls are visible inside the public gardens. It is indicated by Visit Lazio as the place not to be missed in the country.
Mountain life a century ago.

The medieval village, built around the imperial abbey of Santa Croce documented in 887, is still surrounded by the defensive walls with three fourteenth-century doors (Marina, Romana and Canale) and two towers, including the Tower of the Warriors.
The fifteenth-century frescoes of the Earth.

Small natural and quiet area with beach rich in minerals and vegetation that shades close to the sea, the mouth of the Brenta; the mouths of Brenta and Adige are explored on foot or by bike, with bike paths and horseback riding along the shore.
The fifth baroque of St. John's Square.

Tiriolo is known for its embroidery and vancali, wool and silk shawls once part of the ...pacchiana and today objects of artistic handicrafts; also the pieces are produced, colored rugs woven to the frame, lace to the tombolo and traditional musical instruments in wood.

On the bay under Taormina, near Capo Schisò, the Greek colony of Naxos arose in the 8th century BC: today you can visit the archaeological area and the museum, next to the medieval castle of Schisò, the Nike of Mendola and the beaches of Recanati, Schisò and Saia.

Fraction with a Baroque square; the shrine houses a black Madonna brought by Swiss Catholics at the time of the Lutheran reform, linked to the abbey of Einsiedeln. The feast of the sanctuary is held every year on the third Sunday of October.
The walk of the ancient city.

On the southern side of the hill of the temples, exhibits a selection of the finds of the city and the territory and tells the excavations and who lived in the place, with a section on the history and transformation of the landscape. According to the MiC card is open in July on Saturday and Sunday, from August to the first week of September every day except Monday, in the rest of the year only by reservation.
The Borghese village without a car.
Renaissance frescoes and the ancient mule track of Val Gerola.
The name reminds of the drawbridge of the castle.
A day between protected species and thematic paths, inside the courts of a castle.
Carts painted in the Marche countryside.
The memory of cement.

The heart of the village, closed by the Town Hall with the Clock Tower, the church of San Nicolò and via IV Novembre; from the square via Fiorucci offers medieval views. The name recalls Luceoli, an ancient Umbrian city founded in the 7th century BC in the area of the current Pontericcioli.
Wine and cheese in the rock cellars.
The traces of a great medieval abbey in the fields.
A triptych by Andrea De Lithium.
Complete the climb to the Duomo.

Opened in March 2000 in the former convent of San Francesco (XIII century, renovated in the XVI century), it follows a chronological order: artifacts of the Upper Neolithic and Eneolithic tombs of Gaudo facies, settlements of the Bronze Age with Mycenian ceramics of the XI century BC, furnishings from the Iron Age to the Roman era, when Eburum was municipium; also materials from Campagna and Oliveto Citra. Closed on Monday.
312 bird species in the Lower.
The village's living room between palace and mother church.
The Piedmontese baroque.
The Roman flea market.
Verona from 84 meters.
The village of the counts of Arc under the cliff.
One of the first Medici villas.

Hills covered with vineyards and olive groves, woods with lake fauna and the banks of the Mincio, which just from Monzambano begins the descent towards the Mantua plain: an area suitable for walking and cycling.
Perugino and Giovanni Santi on the altars.
A Renaissance Cola dell'Amatrice octagon.

Built for the Clarisses on the surviving section of the caster's moats and completed in 1661, after the suppression of 1793 passed to the Galletti and then to the Gamurrini, who enriched it with works: two shovels by Andrea Sansovino (San Lorenzo, San Sebastiano and San Rocco; Madonna with Child and saints in glazed terracotta), two Robbian altarpieces with Adoration of Shepherds and Miracle of the Snow, fragments of frescoes from the church of San Rocco di Arezzo and, on the main altar, the Presentation at the Temple of Salvi Castellucci in 1663. Under the altar there is the mysterious San Teofilo, a wooden nativity scene from the eighteenth century and an oratory frescoed in grotesques in the early nineteenth century.
A Gothic portal saved from the earthquake.
In the Nature Reserve of Decima Malafede, known since ancient times: Virgilio quotes it in the seventh book of the Eneid calling Albunea the red lake, colored with algae and other substances.
A chapel in the rock.
The municipal palace and, adjacent to it, the 12th century Templar Hall.
Equi, Romans and Garibaldi under the same roof.

Place of worship dug into the rock a short distance from the Ponte Marmone; the legend tells of a traveling seller of votive statues who, remaining with a last unsold Madonna, decided to stop in Pioraco.
Walk around in half an hour.
The original sculptures of the square.

Five funerary enclosures along a secondary road south-east of the walls, with decorated balustrades, replicas of the monuments of the Archaeological Museum and limestone sarcophagi raised for the layer.

More than 1300 pieces on the Domusnovas agricultural tradition and on the Cixerri plain: kitchen utensils, containers, tools for making cheese and wine, iron and wood ploughs, wagons and tools for sowing, harvesting and transport. Opens only by telephone appointment with the owner; admission fee.
The religious and artistic heart of the city.

The underground structure dates back to 1314, under the reign of Roberto d'Angiò, used not only for worship but also as a refuge from the pirate raids; it preserves two altars carved into the rock and several valuable frescoes.
The museum that explains the Fair.
Church of 1657 in the center.
The border stories of the Upper Stura Valley.

In the historic centre, a scenographic stone staircase rises to the Church of St. Joseph, near the seventeenth-century Church of the Madonna della Catena, dedicated to the patron saint; in Piazza D'Antona there is a monument to the senator of the same name.
One of the most beautiful streets in Italy.
Outside the center, in a panoramic position.

Borgo at the foot of the Laga Mountains with the Santa Scala to be climbed on knees, the Palazzo Farnese and, in the convent of San Francesco, the furnishings of the pre-Roman necropolis of Campovalano.
A few steps from the square.

Small village on a spur of Mount Putano, in the Sirente-Velino Regional Park, heir to the ancient Superaequum, one of the three municipalities of the Peligni: it preserves the early Christian catacomb, the church of Sant'Agata, the Palazzo castellano dei Conti di Celano and the complex of San Francesco with the Museum of Sacred Art.
The old flour cycle.
The symbol of the Pontine Reclamation in the heart of the city.
To be checked: ticket of the Civic Museums, also valid for San Domenico
Understand the stone that paves squares all over the world.

Baroque shrine on a scenic staircase, attributed to Giuseppe Ferrara, started in 1722 after the earthquake of 1693 and opened to worship in 1741; the interior stuccoes are by Onofrio Russo, pupil of Serpotta. It preserves the Nativity in glazed terracotta by Andrea della Robbia, brought by Santa Maria la Vetere, and the sarcophagus by Blasco II Barresi; the feast is September 8.
Panoramic point on the Valle di Comino, on part of the Valle del Liri and on the Val Roveto.
In the canonical church of the 11th century, works of the churches of the territory, with a Madonna and Child by Filippo Lippi.

Church of Gothic imprint; next to it is the cemetery of the victims of Stava, with a monument dedicated to them, the last stage of the Path of Memory. In the center there is also the chapel of San Rocco, of the sixteenth century.
Resurgence water and mills in the heart of the country.

Benedictine Abbey in the upper part of the historic centre, on the remains of the acropolis of the Italian and Greek city (in the necropolis cloisters from the VII century BC). It is spread over three floors around the cloister, with cellars excavated in the rock; on the upper floor frescoes of the XVI-XVII century, including the cycle of the library attributed to Girolamo Todisco, and sculptures of Altobello and Aurelio Persio; the church has stuccoes of the early eighteenth century and four frescoed chapels on the side.

Temple of the Waldensian community, also called the Bellonatti Church: the project was approved by the Napoleonic government on April 9, 1806 and the community built it with voluntary work and own contributions, completing it thanks to the gifts of foreign friends. It rises in the hamlet of San Giovanni, in front of the Catholic church of San Giovanni Battista. Visits by reservation or on Sunday morning during worship.
Suitable for families.
A descent through the vineyards.

The birthplace of Sant'Ignazio (1701-1781), the most venerated saint of Sardinia, in the historic center, houses a small museum and is the first stage of the devotional itinerary; in the festival week of late August pilgrims from all over the island and from abroad arrive there, and on August 31 the procession takes place with knights in costume and confraternities.
Ancient military citadel with park, historical cannons and view of the city; it houses the 19th century Museum of the Museum of Stories and the Park of the Memorials.
Wolves, deer and donkeys are free.

Small church in the hall cited in the will of Brunetto dei Montegnacco, was radically rebuilt in 1626: the original construction remains a sculpted spire of 1486, placed on the tympanum. Between 1790 and 1796 Girolamo di Montegnacco embellished it with stones from the demolished bell tower of Collalto di Tarcento.
The regional portal indicates the historical center, monuments and museums of Muccia partially usable
Romanesque church in the hamlet Scandeluzza, which contains fifteenth-century frescoes in the apse.

Fortified castle owned by the Cordero di Mondovì family: quadrangular palace along the road to Camerana, overlooking a large park with views of the Cuneo plain. Next is the parish church of San Benedetto.
Museum closed until date to be dedicated according to Parma Welcome (info Municipality 0521 622137)
A break in the shade downtown.
Bernini's pearl.

Beyond Piana di Fornero, the most interesting underground complex in the valley, with winding tunnels, small waterfalls and holes that tell the geological history of the area; the main cave (Cave of the Witches, old mine) is 707 meters long.
The traditional market in the small square dominated by the patron's basilica, reached by the porticos of Broletto.

Malaspinian castle made autonomous by Azzone Malaspina, partly demolished by the Campofregoso in the mid-15th century and enlarged by the Grand Duchy of Tuscany in the sixteenth century; damaged by the earthquake of 1920, passed to the State. You can visit the kitchen with large fireplace, stables, chapel of soldiers, noble floor and walk of panoramic round. Since 2004 it houses the Museum of Emigration with 66 panels in eight sections of photos, letters, passports and documentaries, including the history of the booksellers of Montereggio.
Outdoor art in the chestnut trees.
The sanctuary retouched by Giulio Romano.

Park of 43 hectares at 420 meters, on a panoramic ridge about 25 km from Modena, of which three are dedicated to over 800 varieties of roses: ancient and classic rose garden, "Herbario dei sensi" (Herbary of the senses), "Le roses rediscovered" (Roses found) and a nursery of roses in pot; the shop sells roses products and can be ordered with local specialties. The cynorrhoids are admired from July to January.
The collection of the national sculpture contest.

It rises around the year 1000 outside the village as the chapel of the Augustinian Fathers dedicated to St. Michael, it is mentioned for the first time in a bull of Pope Celestine III of 1192 as property of the abbey of Santa Giustina of Sezzadio. In the 13th century it was enlarged and housed the humble nuns (from Santa Maria Vallechiara derives its current name); after their departure it remained for three centuries under the parish of San Martino. At the end of the sixteenth century the Romanesque complex was enlarged to the present size, in the eighteenth century the bell tower was added and in 1893 a restoration opened four lunettes and erected the porch in front with columns of an ancient convent portico. The FAI card mentions frescoes by several painters, some of the school of the brothers Boxilio di Castelnuovo Scrivia: St. Biagio, St. Lucia and St. Francis in the right camp, a Madonna with Child on the left.
Regina's female futurism.
The churches of the confraternities in the center of the village.
The red dome.

In Borgo Marina, the history of the sea from the seventeenth century to today with archaeological finds, nautical instruments, multimedia installations and simulators; under a green copper dome the planetarium projects over 6,000 stars.
The houses of cooked wine.
Woods and wetlands between the swamps of Bientina and Fucecchio.
The most mysterious sculptures of Tuscany.
Ancient seat of the Mint, next to the parish church; linked to the history of the principality (954-1729) and to the coins "luigini" .
A rare round tower in Umbria.

It occupies the entire north side of Piazza Mazzini, between the Civic Tower and the Torrazzo, and was the residence of all the lords of Castel Goffredo. Born from two buildings of the first fortified nucleus, it was transformed into a residence from 1480 by Bishop Ludovico Gonzaga with the architect Ermes Flavio de Bonis; from 1511 the Marquis Aloisio Gonzaga made it the seat of the feud that included Castiglione and Solferino. In 1776 it was sold to Colonel Giacomo Acerbi; the eighteenth-century façade is by Gaspare Turbini, the entrance loggia of the sixteenth-century has entirely frescoed vaults. There were born the writer Giuseppe Acerbi and the Garibaldi patriot Giovanni Acerbi. It is private: porch and some rooms are open for events.
The mill and water life of the Park.
The life of medieval pilgrims told by stones.
The museum-atelier of via del Babuino linked to Antonio Canova, which in 1818 was at the apex of fame, and to the sculptors Tadolini.
A altarpiece of Moroni still on its altar.
The civic center of the village.

Castle built in 1033 by Rainulfo and enlarged in the twelfth century, with interventions also by Frederick II; it was surrounded by two walls separated by small towers. Today on the top of the hill remain the wall and the door, with the coat of arms of the Carafa still visible on the stone of the entrance gate, and the remains of a drawbridge at the entrance.
A medieval neighborhood collected and silent, often neglected.
Umbriatourism: private property, visible only from outside

From Passo Pordoi (2,239 m), about 12 km and 28 hairpin bends from Canazei, the cable car climbs in a few minutes to 2,950 m; from the terrace you can see Marmolada, Sella with the Piz Boè, Sassolungo, Catinaccio, Tofane and Pelmo, and on clear days the Austrian and Swiss Alps. On top of a refuge, base for Forcella Pordoi and Piz Boè; the cable car opens from mid-May to early November and reopens before Christmas.
In Palazzo Ghisilardi, the Bentivoglio age: tombs of the Doctors of the Studio, weapons, avori and the large golden copper statue of Bonifacio VIII (1301).
Discover Cesena Card €13 (with Malatestiana, Rocca and Villa Silvia)
The Renaissance church of the city.
On the west coast cliffs and coves of sand and pebbles: Valle della Luna, Coscia di Donna and Cala del Vapore, some reachable only by sea.
The silvers donated by Nelson.
A former crafts and the ancestor of the parliamentary stenotype.

The oldest wine school in Italy, founded in 1876, with a teaching cellar since 1927 and a classroom decorated by Antonio Maria Morera; from 2016 on the first floor the museum dedicated to Luigi Manzoni (1888-1968), author of the Manzoni crossroads such as Bianco 6.0.13, with instruments, botanical collections, cameras and microscopes of the early twentieth century. Visit by telephone reservation.
On the trail of Saint Benedict Cambiagio.
The only bridge in Florence saved in 1944.
The largest archaeological collection in the region.
A village intact inside its towers.
The palace between Piazza delle Erbe and Piazza dei Signori where Bartolomeo della Scala lived and where Romeo was sentenced to exile in the tragedy, today home of the modern art gallery.

On a hill on the right of the river Olivento, a few kilometers from the village, remain the ruins of a Roman villa of imperial age with rooms in red brick and an ancient thermal system; it is the most important Roman archaeological structure of the territory, excavated since 1998. The visible area is not fenced.

Fiumicello goes from the headland of Ogliastro to the tip of Santavenere, with small caves and kayak; Fiumicello and Castrocucco are the largest and easiest to reach beaches, suitable for children. On the coast of Acquafredda there are Anginarra and Luppa, divided by a cliff, Grotta della Scala, Porticello and Marizza; in Cersuta the famous beach of u Nastru and Porto i Vranne, reachable only from the sea.

Country of the lower Ossola on the plain of Toce, with the sanctuaries of the Madonna del Boden and the Madonna della Guardia on the hill, the ancient marble quarry that from the fourteenth century refurbished the Duomo of Milan, the fortifications of the Cadorna Line and the Partisan museum dedicated to the Republic of Ossola.

Castle walled at the foot of Monte Cucco, bought by Gubbio in the 13th century, with four doors, the Civic Tower and the church of San Francesco; it is the gateway to the Park of Monte Cucco and its cave, among the major in Italy, with the Museum-Laboratory of the Park and the National Centre of Speleology.
On February 4th, the feast of the patroness, stalls and the sweet aniseed piadina

Parish church built between 1771 and 1795, indicated by the Parco dei Colli among the most important buildings of the municipality; the cult of San Faustino in Villa is already attested in a parchment of 927.

Ancient aleramic marquisate between the Bormida, Erro and Orba valleys, Ponzone is the largest municipality in the area, with ten hamlets among mushrooms and truffles woods; from the viewpoint you can see the Alps, Apennines Ligurian and Monferrato, and in the territory you will find the parish church of San Michele of 1627, the sanctuary of the Pieve and the Partisan shrine of Piancastagna.
The best view of the village and sea.
€5, free under 12 and Museums Subscription

Neoclassical villa built by Giacomo Vicentini after 1829, with frescoes, central colonnade façade and an octagonal cellar under the garden accessible from an underground passage. It is the seat of the Monfalconese Cultural Consortium, with archive of memory, library, magazine "Il Territorio" and the photo library that has been active since 1978 (about 12,000 photographs on the history of Bisiacaria and a collection of cameras); it hosts conferences and exhibitions. Visits by reservation.
A tiny village.

Permanent set-up of work tools, handicrafts and everyday objects, with reconstructions of domestic and working environments. It exhibits the tools for wood processing and the production of the typical stuffed chairs of Serrastretta, woven with the ... vuda, plant of the wetlands, and a clock of the late nineteenth century still working; in the courtyard an ancient nineteenth century mill and a water mill.
The bridge to a single arch on the throat.
€4, free under 8 years
Ass-back excursions on the island of Lipari, accompanied by environmental guides.
The finds of the village of the Bronze Age.
A dense forest that surrounds the village and is part of the Natural Park of the Albano di Lucania Wood, where outdoor activities are also held.
Civic museum with archaeological section and antiquarium of the sea.
Caves not far from the village and easily reachable, in a paleontological deposit of the Quaternary.
The houses of wood and stone.
A tour of walls with views to the islands.
The basilica on the harbor.
The university heart of Pisa.
On the hill above the southern part of the lake, a 23-metre-high signal tower of an outpost documented since the 12th century.
In the 18th century Military Districts, a multimedia exhibition on the history of Turin from racial laws to Liberation, with temporary exhibitions.

Dimora dei Ferrero della Marmora for seventeen generations: 16-metre-long Gallery, Salone delle feste frescoed by Galliari, room on the Risorgimento of the four generals La Marmora and garden on the city with the octagonal tower; visits by reservation.
One of the most animated squares in the center, dedicated to the historical Cividalese author of the Historia Langobardorum.
Remains of a Romanesque pluteo of the abbey destroyed in the nineteenth century.
One of the great abbeys of the Italian Middle Ages.
On the Road
The romantic park above the lake.
Overlooking the homonymous square next to Piazza Umberto I, where stands the Praetorian Palace.

The capital between the Gran Sasso and the Adriatic, the ancient Interamnia: the Cathedral with the silver palace of Nicola da Guardiagrele, the Roman theatre and amphitheatre, the domus of the center and the civic museums.
A destination of pilgrimages, with a statue of the Madonna and Child on the altar found centuries ago by peasants; enlarged in the eighteenth century.

Set up in the former Palladio power plant, it reconstructs the production chain of sulphur in all its phases and the socio-economic aspects of mining, documenting the plants of the Trabia-Tallarita mines.
A monumental Giant tomb on the hill.
Neo-Gothic church built in 1904 and blessed in 1926, with an older chapel; according to local legend in 1805 there was held for two days a mysterious character identified with Giuseppe Bonaparte.
It was built on Romanesque remains and rebuilt at the end of the 19th century; the parish museum preserves ancient liturgical objects and sacred works of art.

Probably founded in the Lombard age on older foundations, it was rebuilt in the 10th century with a single nave; the bell tower, high and decorated with hanging arches, and the side aisles were added later. Inside the medieval altar has decorations with geometric motifs of the tenth century, and walls and apses preserve frescoes of the fourteenth-fiveth century; it was parish until 1669.
Church built between 1624 and 1648, with convex façade and bell tower reminiscent of the Duomo of Lecce; next is the column of the Madonna delle Grazie.

Romanesque church built between the 11th and 12th centuries, according to tradition on a church desired by the Longobard king Desire, documented from 1230 and collegiate from the 16th century. Façade with four columns porch, rosette and symbols of the Evangelists; inside three naves with carved capitals, presbytery raised with ciborium and schola cantorum, fourteenth-century floor with cosmatesque and crypt imitation with a sixteenth-century crucifix in alabaster venerated as miraculous. It preserves a triptych by Nicolò Alunno, the Decollation of the Baptist by Livio Agresti (1571) and a Tyrolean organ Werle of 1756.

One of Sardinia's best preserved single tower nuraghi, the Bronze Age: blocks of limestone in regular rows, about 10 m in diameter and over 8 m in height, with two construction phases for a restoration of the Nuragic age. Inside the tholos vault is integrated, three cross niches, a triangular window and a staircase interrupted after five steps. It is reached from a dirt road towards the dam of the Mulargia and then on foot on a steep slope (about 15 minutes).

The historical centre, called Bicocca, has medieval layout and tuff houses; the seventeenth century Baronial Palace is now a cultural centre. The fountain of the Billellera, dating back to the 17th century, takes up the model of the fountain of Rosello in Sassari: according to tradition those who drink its waters go crazy.
One of the most intact medieval squares of the Aquilano.
Sacred art a stone's throw from the Palace.

On the plateau between the Rio de' Lanzi and the Rio Pezzasecca the ancient Cales survives, founded by the Ausoni and Roman colony from 334 BC, with walls, thermal baths, amphitheatre and theatre; in Calvi Vecchia there is also the cathedral of San Casto, of late IX century.
€5, reduced €3; cumulative €8
The gold and mosaic of the Banquet Hall.

In the fifteenth-century Torre di Porta Marina, over a thousand finds on three floors from the Etruscans to traditional handicrafts: archaic and Renaissance ceramics, liturgical art, paintings, medieval and industrial archaeology, with audioguides and workshops.
Only surviving part of the castle wanted in 1324, the only trace of the ancient walled city.
Medieval village with the frescoes of the pilgrims' hospice founded in 1368 and the old Roman bridge, rest of the road to the Gauls.

Medieval church on a rocky spur above the city, erected by a community of monks, perhaps humiliated, and also used as xenodochius for pilgrims and strangers. In the apse there are early medieval frescoes discovered in 1987 and restored, among the oldest wall paintings in the province; from the churchyard you can enjoy a panorama of Tirano.

Historic centre with Renaissance buildings around Piazza Sedati, a 17th century fountain linked to the De Capua and a watchtower at the entrance of the centre, now home to the Town Hall; the church of Santa Maria Assunta has a portal from the 14th century. The Sunday market is held in Piazza Umberto I.
Mother church of the village, it preserves the statue of the patron saint of St. John the Baptist, celebrated on June 24.
Inside a fortification above the source of the Adige.
The Valtorta-Piani ski area of Bobbio-Barzio, with the cross-country trail Tre Signori and, in summer, mountain bike trails.
Contemporary art inspired by Saint Francis.
The most photogenic square.
The story of Ivrea.
The stones of ancient Equi.
The village between orchards and vineyards at the gates of Aosta, with the royal castle where the Savoys used to hunt in the valleys of the Gran Paradiso.
A village of tuff to walk.
A community museum in the hills.
The Brianza peasant life in a medieval village.

Built between 1494 and 1500 and known as "dei Borgia" in honor of Pope Alexander VI, it was the last fortification of a system of border disputed between Spoleto, Todi, Foligno and Perugia. Triangular plant with three round towers, conical, connected by underground walkways; the highest, 20 meters on 5 floors, has a base of 80 meters of circumference. In 1624 Galileo Galilei stayed there, who called it a small compendium of the universe.

A hilly town north of Udine, where in the village of Fontanabona the castle with its hamlet and the land forms a complex of about 200 hectares remained almost intact, also home to the Museum of rural history (now closed for renovation).
A day in the woods between the suspended routes.
The pomegranate fountain.
Frescoes rediscovered.

the Park card indicates it is \momentally closed Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â Â
The symbolic monument that dominates the country.

Parish from millenarian history, built on the site of an ancient abbey dedicated to St. Peter; almost entirely destroyed by the earthquake of 1783. It is reached by a staircase; a side entrance has a ramp for people with disabilities.

Ring of about 2 hours from the Museum of Fossil: climb to the parish church and to the top of Monte Purga, with 360 degrees view over the valleys of the Alpone and Chiampo, Veneto plain and Small and Great Dolomites; the return to the road of the Madonna is through the forest of Purga with its columnary basalts.

An ancient residence of the Filiani family wanted by Giacinto Filiani, in rural style with double central staircase and internal altar frescoed; until the fifties some rooms served to the bachiculture, from which the mulberry trees of the garden. Restored by the Municipality in 2005, it is the seat of the Museo Etnomusicologico d'Abruzzo and hosts exhibitions, conferences and concerts; accessible with monastery. Information to the IAT Office (055 9491745).

Sections of painting, sculpture and archaeology; among the masterpieces the Polyptych of San Gregorio di Antonello da Messina (1473) and two canvases of Caravaggio, the Adoration of the Shepherds and the Resurrection of Lazarus.
Ancient pieve of the village, which hosts the Palio dell'Uovo on Easter.

Founded in 1079 by Saint Albert of Prezzate, who returned from the pilgrimage to Santiago donated some of his assets to Cluny and placed the monastery under Abbot Ugo, expanding a church of Saints James, Bassano and Nicola. Here, on April 7, 1167, tradition places the oath of the Lombard League against Federico Barbarossa. The visit includes the fourteenth-century basilica, of Gothic style inside, with Romanesque capitals, frescoes in part of the Marinoni family and medieval Lombard sculptures, including bas-reliefs of the ark of Saint Albert; bell tower and statue of the saint are Renaissance. The complex is completed by the two cloisters, the Renaissance sacristy, the capitular hall and the museum, with paintings and ancient objects used by monks.
Olive groves and holm oaks on foot or by mountain bike.
A monument of art in a panoramic point of Monferrato.
A 15th century wooden Madonna in a small country village.
Parish church with wooden altars and holy waterworks, several times consolidated; next to the Casa Torre, once a watchtower.
A basilica with catacombs.

The largest complex of mud volcanoes in the southern Apennines: small cones emitting hydrocarbons, especially methane, and a continuous flow of slightly brackish waters. The legend sees the punishment of a host that robbed the travelers of the Via Traiana; not far away, in the locality Ripa della Conca, between cliffs and calanchi, there is the Eye of the Devil.
The village on the cliff.
The Pala di Bellini and Renaissance ceramics.
In the heart of the village, built in 1522 and decorated with paintings of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries.
Medieval alleys on the verge of the gravina.

Heir of an eighteenth-century room, was renovated by the architect Vincenzo Costa and inaugurated in 1846; the restoration of 1882 (Carlo Sada and Antonino Grasso) gave him the present appearance, with a horseshoe room, 44 loggias on three orders and golden stuccoes, and curtain of Giuseppe Rapisarda with Timoleonte in the temple of Adrano. The Liberty façade, completed in the early twentieth century by Gaspare Silvestri Amari, is crowned by the group of Mario Moschetti with Tragedy, Music and Comedy. Since about 1920 it bears the name of Bellini; it appears in the Italian-style Divorce of Pietro Germi; it was recovered in 2004 after more than twenty years of closure.

The Irish spot lace is of the fishermen.
The triumphal crucifix.
The Clarisse Monastery of the late sixteenth century, damaged by the earthquake of 1783 and partly rebuilt by order of Murat; today the seat of the Vibonese Librarian System and cultural events.
Bergamo before medieval Bergamo.

The highest view of the coast of Taormina.
The basilica of Don Bosco.
The stone circles of a pre-Roman civilization.
By bike along the river between villas and castles.

Villa belonged to the Nani, then to the Trieste and the Fanzago, sold to the Municipality in 1927 and restored in the eighties of the twentieth century; it has an eighteenth-century sundial and the oratory of San Giovanni Battista, documented since 1686. Visit during the opening hours of the municipal offices.
A medieval village still closed in its walls.
The ghost village of the Taviani cinema.
Listing in enlargement: the guide covers for now 5 of the 14 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Probably the first official place of Christian worship in Rome, in the central square of the district.
The collection of the Dukes of Este on the fourth floor of the Palazzo dei Musei: the bust of Francesco I del Bernini, the portrait of Velázquez, the Triptych of El Greco.
The city dug into the rock.
