Small octagonal temple of the early eighteenth century, attributed to Sangallo, built on a fifteenth-century votive chapel near a source considered miraculous.
Woods and waters between Casentino and Valtiberina.

160 small portraits in terracotta hidden between tiles, cornices and branches of the country, realized in 2018 by 30 participants and by inhabitants for ...Change as Montmartre , curated by the artist Juan Sandoval with Munlab and the support of the City.
Stable museum of peasant civilization set up inside the castle of Bardi.

It rises on the site of the ancient Catholic church of the village, often destroyed and rebuilt; the current building was built in 1706 thanks to the charity of the French Huguenot marquis Pierre de Belcastel, and its pyramid bell tower, built together with the temple, is unique in the Waldensian valleys. The interior with three naves, with barrel vault without decorations, is illuminated by seven windows and a rose window; the door and its key are from the beginning of the eighteenth century, while the wrought iron chandeliers were donated by the Waldensian Church of Milan after the demolition of the Romanesque church of San Giovanni in Conca. On the frieze of the portal the verse "Come, let us worship the Lord" from Psalm 95.
For a souvenir bought in the square.
Andrea Doria's safe house.
The twin village still alive.

The walls wanted by Filippo d'Acaja at the end of the fourteenth century preserve the medieval tower and four doors: Porta di Pinerolo and Porta di San Giusto intact, Porta di Torino restored after the damage of 1977, Porta di San Donato rebuilt after 1965; on the arches the ducal stuccos painted in 1586 by Bernardino Lanino. In the square two houses of the fifteenth century (of the Rolletti di Bricherasio and of the Vicar of Pinerolo) with Gothic windows in terracotta and frescoes of the fourteenth century; through the streets votive frescoes and sundials from the seventeenth to the nineteenth century.

Municipality of the Irno valley behind Salerno, formed by five hamlets of medieval origin, with the former Augustinian monastery of the Holy Spirit, today a panoramic museum complex, and the fourteenth-century church of the Madonna delle Grazie in Capriglia.
A trip to prehistory.
The chapel in the valley.
Karst cave in the Apuan Alps Park, near Casoli, inhabited by Neanderthal hunters and then used for agriculture and breeding in the Neolithic and Copper Age; waterfalls feed a stream at its base.
The votive Norman church.
Medieval frescoes found.

In the sixteenth century deconsecrated church of Sant'Egidio is exposed the Dancing Satyr, bronze from the end of the fourth century BC attributed to the school of Praxitele: the left leg was fished in the spring of 1997, the body on March 4, 1998 by the fishing boat Capitan Ciccio, between Sicily and Capo Bon; it depicts a dancer in ecstasy with panther skin, restored by the Central Institute for Restoration. Also displayed is an elephant paw in punic-hellenistic bronze, a medieval cauldron, amphora and two cannons of Torretta Granitola.
It houses a altarpiece by Pedro Torres (1594) and hosts the permanent exhibition of sacred art "La Veste della Sposa" (The Vest of the Bride), with two Venetian palates on Guardian school leather.

Borgo peroccato sopra Taormina, which takes its name from the Norman castle (castello and Mola): the ruins of the fortress, Piazza Sant'Antonino with the viewpoint on the Ionian coast, the Church Mother of St. Nicholas overlooking Etna, the historic Caffè San Giorgio del vino al al almondla and the path of Monte Veneretta.
Woods and the highest peak of the Sicani.
A early Christian baptismal font and a 17th-century retablo.
All the Popes of history in one gallery.

Two rooms of the Civic Museum dedicated to the Cremasca organarian tradition, which in the first half of the twentieth century reached international fame with the shops Lingiardi, Franceschini, Inzoli and Tamburini, exporting to Great Britain, America and Japan. The first room has instruments, rods and protagonists, with a section on Pacific Inzoli and a multimedia instrument similar to a double keyboard organ; the second is a laboratory on the construction phases, from the rods to the finished instrument.

One of the main green areas north of Milan, over 800 hectares of cultivated fields, tree-lined rows, woods, canals and cycle paths, created to protect the last agricultural and natural spaces after the urbanization of Brianza. The need for protection dates back to the eighties and the park was officially established in 1999 by several municipalities; the name comes from the Catasto Teresiano of 1722.
The rosette with eleven columns, unique in its kind.
Benedictine and Diocesan Museum for a fee
In the House of Friars in Costa Parrocchia, he tells the family of painters Guido da Ranzo and in particular Pietro Guido, active in the Ligurian West between 1490 and 1532.

Fortified village of the fourteenth century in local stone with square plan; the church is formed by two overlapping churches, the lower one of the 11th century with Romanesque crypt and the upper one of the late thirteenth century. There are also the church of Sant'Apollinare (XIII-XIV century) and that of Our Lady of Graces (XV century).
Fortified buildings in the Rioveggio area.
Poetry, castles and panorama in half an hour's walk.
Moretto, Romanino and Paolo Veneziano by the lake.
The mountain peasant life in a secluded valley.

Medieval village perched on the Lucera Castle of Sangro, called Civitavecchia until 1875 and identified by some scholars with the Duronia Sannitica conquered by the Romans in 293 BC. Above the village the Civita massif, with the remains of the Sannitic fortifications and a view of 28 municipalities.
Public park along a stretch of the Roman walls of Interamna; there stands the sixteenth-century Church of Carmine, restored and used for exhibitions and concerts.
The art of the Cosmati.
End of November to 6 January

Born from the donation of the collector Damiano Paparella, it has thousands of objects of agricultural and artisan life between the end of the nineteenth and mid twentieth centuries: a peasant house of the twenties with kitchen, room, wash and stable, the sections on terracotta and iron, the cycles of oil and wine and a miniature of the chariot of the Madonna di Sovereto. Stage of the Olive Oil-Terra d'Ulivi Road, with audio guides.
Tastes of the Roman Agro.
Lose between covered passages and carved portals.
The conference center in steel and glass designed by Massimiliano Fuksas.
A barbaric house told room by room.
The crypt with the tombs of the martyrs Felice and Adautto, Byzantine paintings and a 9th century graffiti.
The walk from the castle to the Duomo.
Five centuries of mill and the life of sharecroppers.
At 2088 meters, of an intense blue and surrounded by peaks.
Dozens of graves carved in the tuff along the gorges of the Etruscan Park.

Built between 1437 and 1444 on the main square, it follows closely the Brunelleschi models and is defined the first Brunelleschi building outside Tuscany: square body with grooved sandstone pilaster, octagonal drum and hemispheric dome, inside similar to the Old Sacristy of San Lorenzo in Florence. Open Tuesday-Saturday (winter 9.30-12.30 and 14.30-17.30, summer 10-13 and 15-18), Sunday and holidays 10-13 and 15-18.
The strong walls defend the village on the side of the valley; in via Cervetti the ancient door to sharp arch, intact in medieval form, introduces to the old village.
The story of RAI.
You can see where the majolicas used to cook.
A medieval castle in the woods towards the Orsiera.
The Madonna of the protective mantle.

Church of Byzantine origin (X century), re-used in the XII century as a private chapel of the Norman kings, who reached it from the castle with an underground passage. It preserves columns and cosmatesque pieces of floor; on the high altar an Annunciation of Tuscan school of 1597.
Medieval church next to the museum that houses the sarcophagus of Fedra, an important example of Roman sculpture in Sicily.
Green in town.

It is located in the restored historical mill and tells about the reclamation of the territory, the rural civilization, the electrification of Sardinia and urban history; it preserves the Historical Civic Archives. The historical section presents architecture and architects of the city with vintage films and a touch table with about 800 historical images; the archaeological section exhibits the materials of the nuragic sacred well of Orri and, in the Antiquarium, more than 300 finds of the necropolis of S'Ungroni from the Punic to the Byzantine age. Open Saturday 14:30-19:30, Sunday 8:30-13:30 and Monday 14:00-19:00.

Medieval village of the Madonie, already fortified citadel and residence of the Ventimiglia, known as the "Borgo degli Immortali" for its longevity: the ruins of the castle with the small church of Sant'Anna, the Bevaio della SS. Trinity, the Mother Church with the works of the Gagini and Geraci's treasure, the Salto dei Ventimiglia and, in the forest of Vicaretto, Santa Maria della Cava.
The memory of the Cardinal of the Lateran Pacts.

Church of the XVI century with Renaissance portal in limestone of 1540, unique in Abruzzo for the rare iconographic motif, and rosette of 1585 with snakes twisted to the compasses and the coat of arms of the Sangro. Inside a polychrome statue of San Rocco of 1530 of local ceramists, a sixteenth-century wooden tabernacle gilded in 1664 and a copy of the Triptych of Antwerp, whose original was stolen in 1981.

The city of Archimede, UNESCO heritage: the island of Ortigia with the Duomo born from the temple of Athena, the Temple of Apollo, the Fountain Aretusa and the Castle Maniace; on land the Greek Theatre, the side rooms with the Orecchio di Dionisio, the Museum Paolo Orsi, the catacombs and the Castle Eurialo.
A thousand years of Novara countryside on an itinerary.
The treasure of the Collegiate Church, a stone's throw from the Basilica.

The eighteenth-century residence of the Counts Bettoni in Bogliaco, called "small Versailles" and registered in the Register of Historic Houses of Excellence; there were guests Puccini, Victor Hugo, Garibaldi and Napoleon. The Italian garden, beyond the state road and connected to the house by two raised walkways, has stairs, three fountains, an artificial cave, remains of a lemon house and sculptures by Gian Battista Locatelli. Guided tours only in spring and summer, by online reservation, conducted by a family member.

Tignale is formed by six nuclei with ancient houses and alleys of medieval origin: Gardola with the parish church of Santa Maria Assunta, Piovere with the viewpoints on the lake and the church of San Marco, Oldesio with the alleys, the ancient wash-houses and the chapel of San Rocco; between Piovere and Oldesio stretch out the characteristic terraces cultivated with olive trees.

Borgo dei Monti Dauni overlooking the Fortore valley, Carlantino has a small old town closed by a double wall, gathered around the church of San Donato, and is a panoramic balcony that ranges from Gran Sasso to Tremiti, from the dam of Occhito to Gargano.
Wildt sculptures off the circuits.
A room of mushroom wonders.
The market of city herbs indicated by the Region among the flavors and craftsmanship of Macerata.
Birdwatching on a migratory stop lake.
Taste the symbol dish of the Piana.

Inaugurated in 2015 in the locality Colleveduta, about 800 m of altitude on 10.770 m2 of fir forest, bushes, fruit trees and pastures; you can visit with a guide along a dirt track and hosts three brown bears born in captivity. Visits by reservation from March to November (season hours), closed in December and January for hibernation.
A thousand years of history in a few walls.
About 10 hectares of meadows for the popular sports of the Val d'Aosta such as rebatta, fiolet, tsan and palet, reachable by bike from the bike path along the Dora.

The 16 hamlets are placed on a terrace on the slopes; the Walser colony, the oldest in Valsesia, settled from the thirteenth century probably through the filling of the Dorchetta from the Anzasca Valley, and language and traditions are still alive. Due to the scarcity of larch, the Walser architecture is less developed than elsewhere and houses have closed loggias. Among the villages: Church, Sella, San Gottardo, Villa Inferiore, Roncaccio Superiore. In the past gold, nickel and cobalt were extracted.
One of the oldest churches in Ascoli.
The cast of the altar of Su Mulinu and the history of the site.
The legend of Tiburzi told in an interactive way.

Neo-Gothic burial church built between 1860 and 1869 on the design of the Viennese Moritz Wappler, considered one of the first and most successful sacred architectures of this style; in red sandstone and granite of the area of Mount Ivigna, rises on an artificial terrace on the west side of the hill. In the crypt the marble sarcophagus of Archduke John of Austria and his wife. Only with guided tour, in the morning, from June to October; closed in winter.
Venetian villas that were headquarters in the Great War.
The large square with the neoclassical basilica of San Francesco di Paola and, in front, the Royal Palace.
King Arthur in Alexandria.
Winter skiing, hiking and mountain biking in summer.
Green path along the stream, connected to the thermal baths.
The work of Angiolo Mazzoni, the most interesting architectural building in Sabaudia: almost entirely covered with blue mosaic tiles, with large windows framed with red marble of Siena.

Here Antonio Stradivari married Francesca Ferraboschi in 1667 and opened his first workshop; there were born his children and the family lived there until 1680, when he made the violin Clisbee and the viola Mahler.
The nature of the plateau told in dioramas.

The "city of roses" between Po and Adige: Piazza Vittorio Emanuele with Palazzo Roverella and Palazzo Roncale, the towers of the castle, the octagonal Round with the bell tower of Longhena and the Museum of Great Rivers.
The castle of the turrets.
A Roman theater came to light after 2,000 years.
Outside the village, with Baroque altars in carved wood and an austere 17th century cloister.

The oldest sites in the country, destroyed by the earthquake of 1783, of which many ruins remain; near the rock of the Stone of the Monks there is the cave of the chisels where the modules of the Baroque fountain were prepared.

Country of the Taranto Ionic arch surrounded by about 3 km of ravine, with the rock villages of Rivolta and Casale, the Norman castle built in 1080 by Robert Guiscard and the sixteenth-century Matrix Church at the foot of the ravine. On the sea, the Marina di Ginosa, long beach with pine trees, Blue Flag.
The symbol of the medieval Ginosa, overlooking the gravina.
A 17th-century canvas in the village.
Baroque church in panoramic position above the main square of the village.

Inaugurated in 1929 by the prevosto Giovanni Bonzi at the invitation of Angelo Roncalli, future John XXIII, in a Gandinese Renaissance residence connected by a overpass to the churchyard of the basilica. The section of sacred art exhibits vestments, goldsmiths, Flemish tapestries by Frans Guebels and Mattens, illuminated codes, wooden statues, paintings by Sebastiano Ricci, Antonio Balestra and Antonio Cifrondi and twenty-three macabre panels with skeletons used in the Triduo of the Dead. The museum is completed by the section of the nativity scenes, coming from dozens of countries and dedicated to St. John Paul II, and the textile one, with machines such as the gauze machine for the Pannilana of the valley.
A 17th-century church wanted by the municipality.
The cathedral of the Arbëreshë community, the main stage of the visit.

Church founded in 1599 and completed in 1638 by the foreman Giovanni Battista Pianca, restored last time in 1931 and then abandoned: there are three perimeter walls. Tactile panel and picnic area; it is the crossroads of the paths to Lake Bertignano, Mount Orsetto and the Roc d'la Regina.

open only on Saturdays and holidays 15:30-18; different address between MiC (Via Vittorio Emanuele) and in-Lombardy (Cascina Mirani)

Born in the thirteenth century with a chapel dedicated to the Madonna and a female convent of Carthusians, it passed in the fifteenth century to the Dominicans and the early seventeenth century to the Camaldolese, becoming a pilgrimage destination. In the nineteenth century it was transformed into a villa with mythological paintings by Francesco Gonin; the bombings of the Second World War severely damaged the abbey church, of which the ruins remain. On the slope of the hill the alabaster quarries. Visits by reservation.

Left by the inhabitants between 1902 and 1908 for a landslide, according to the laws on landslides: the stone houses in the chamber around the eighteenth-century church of San Nicola and the large Piazza Giovanni Nicotera with shops, barns, stables, water troughs and fountain; in the houses remain beds, kitchens and a stable.

Considered the oldest church of Modica, probably the early Middle Ages, parish of a Greek-speaking district: the apse is covered with Byzantine-style icons with the Christ Pantocrator in almond; identified in 1987 in a cave used as a deposit.
Fraction between vineyards and wooded hills, with a small waterfall that descends from a rock wall, in the area of the Prosecco hills of Conegliano and Valdobbiadene UNESCO World Heritage.
The palace of the Marquises, today city hall.

The first village of the Iblei Mountains chain, about 700 meters away, already documented in 1168 as "Monte Jahalmo" and rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693: the piazza "u chianu" with San Giovanni Battista and the noble palaces, the Neo-Gothic Mother Church, Sant'Antonio Abate and the medieval Quarter of Cava; in the surroundings the necropolis of Monte Casasia.
Only by reservation from the site of the Municipality

For shopping in the comaschi.
Church of the XIV-XV century in the area of the Castle, with terracotta portal, a golden wooden tabernacle and a painting of the Madonna del Rosario of the late sixteenth century.
The frescoes found.
The baroque altars of the fraternity, in the heart of the village.
The Tonino Guerra fountain dedicated to music.
Green area just outside the center, for walks and venue of events.

Highest peak of the Bletterbach system (2.317 m), next to the Black Horn (2.439 m); from the Visitor Centre a path of 9.6 km and 940 meters of difference in altitude, about 5 hours, climbs to the Laner mountain hut, Kösertal and Grossnerwiesen meadows, with a teaching station on the formation and tectonics of the mountain.
Going down into the life of the pyrite miners.
The millstones of a historic mill.

The 17th-century parish church of San Giacomo preserves, behind the present altar, a more ancient altar in carved wood and golden of exceptional workmanship; the oratory of San Carlo holds a polychrome wooden Pietà. In the canton La Sella a fountain and the oratory of the Immaculate Conception with a cruising porch; The Caterra is a small nucleus of dense houses.
The water channels.

Modesta chapel in 1578 was enlarged from 1643 and became parish in 1669, inheriting the title from St. Peter; the pronao with granite columns of St. Fedelino is from 1764 and the present aspect is due to the enlargement of 1893-98 on a project by Cesare Nava. It preserves wooden furnishings by Bernardino Castelli (pulpit, group of the Addolorata, Crucifix) and decorations of about 1923-33 of Innocent Salvini and frescoes by Giovanni Battista Jemoli.
Built in 1507 by the feudal Bartholomew III of Capua, it has an external balustrade carved by hand by local stonemasons and preserves two sculpted noble sarcophagi, linked by tradition to the names

The regular plant centre was built around the castle built in 1290 by Alberto Scotti, with the quadrangular system between the streams Lora and Carona; along the main streets examples of liberty architecture of the early twentieth century.
The little church mirrored in the pond.
Playful and educational space in the Opera Vittorio, renovated in 2023, on climate change and glaciers.

Fortification of the castle's walls, built after the sacking of 1525 by the pirate Dulcigno and transformed into a museum in 2004: about 230 works by the grottammarese sculptor Pericles Fazzini, including bronzes, silver, gold, drawings, pastels, engravings and two portraits of Giuseppe Ungaretti, with the silver sketch of the Resurrection of the Sala Nervi in the Vatican.
Napoleon in Val Bormida.

The largest of the twelve residences of Tiberius, mentioned by Tacitus, 334 meters on Mount Tiberius, at the eastern end of the island: in the center a large square with cisterns, an atrium with columns of chives, the thermal baths with apsed calidary and, on the summit to the north, the private apartments of the emperor with the terrace on the Gulf.
Erected in 113 A.D. to celebrate the feats of Traiano in Dacia, the first coclid column with spiral relief.
The Gran Sasso mirrored in the lake.
A pharmacy from the 16th century with its Urbinated majolica vases.
The medieval bridge.
The park door.
Prehistoric tombs and starry sky above Troina.
Church founded in 1613 by the Augustinians Scalzi.
The palace on the hill.
Small pebble beach reachable only from the sea, by boat or with the turtle's taxi; it takes its name from a cliff of five meters in the shape of a turtle and is quiet and surrounded by clear waters.

Austro-Hungarian fortress built between 1908 and 1914 at 1,177 m above the upper Valle dell'Astico, with concrete roof of about 2,10 m, three 10 cm obici in armored domes, 22 machine gun stations and four outposts connected by galleries; the motto was "Per Trento" is enough for me. Buyed by the Municipality in 1997 and restored with the Province, it is a museum on the three floors of the block casematte: system of the forts, war at altitude, medicine of war, rebuilt trench and the multisensory .
Life in the farmhouse of Cremasco in the early twentieth century.

Built in 1626 in Gagliago, instead of a 14th-century chapel, it preserves Romanesque features in the bell tower. Inside are frescoes by Bernardino Peretti and Antonio Cotti: the twelve apostles around the choir, the Trinity behind the main altar and the Annunciation; the baptistery is precious. On the façade there is the Baptism of Jesus, a Madonna, the coat of arms of Ferrari Ghibellines, the Borromeo coat of arms and several sundials.

The lake, reserve of the Regional Park Campo dei Fiori, is also seen from the main road and can be reached on foot with a short dirt road; not far away is the Pesegh Falls. From the lake pass the paths 10/310 C and 20/320 of the park.

Built in the early twentieth century in stone and brick in Liberty style, recognizable for the towers on the facade, it worked as a playhouse only until 1917; today, restored, it hosts congresses, weddings and events. Outside friezes, bas-reliefs with flying deer and butterflies, balustrades and wrought irons; inside crystal chandeliers, frescoes and sculptures, an atrium with eight columns of red Verona marble and a monumental staircase. You can visit with guided tours by local operators (from €7; Liberty tour of the city from €15).

The museum occupies the crypt under the Cathedral, re-emerged after the 1980 earthquake. It exhibits a cycle of apse frescoes of about 11 square meters, probably of Neapolitan students of Giotto and restored by the Superintendence, with the Crucifix enthroned among Saints Peter, Catherine of Alexandria, Antonio Abbot, Giovanni Battista, Guglielmo da Vercelli and a Madonna with the Child; next, the lid of a Roman tomb with inscription, a mensory stone to measure cereals, two Corinthian capitals and two wooden sculptures of the Madonna of the Free of the XIV and XVI century.

One of the few historical collections of Puglia, formed in the nineteenth century by Baron Adolfo Colosso with finds of Ugento and of the territory: 794 pieces from the sixth century BC to the high Middle Ages, more armour, weapons and bullets of cannon of modern age, preserved in Palazzo Colosso.
Understand how the Bonifiche and the Great War designed the Lower Piave.

The municipality of Val d'Ultimo, with the hamlets of Santa Valburga, Pracupola, San Nicolò and Santa Gertrude: in San Nicolò the museum of peasant life, in Santa Valburga the Culten archaeological documentation centre, in Santa Gertrude the three thousand-year-old larch trees and the visitor center of the Stelvio National Park in the ancient Lahnersäge sawmill.
16th century hospitality for pilgrims.
Mineral and fossil.
Tribute to the master of the Italian western.
partly private property: the municipal spaces are visited during exhibitions and events; not accessible to people with motor disabilities
One of the highest lights in Europe.
An ancient abbey in the country.

Ancient Casteldurante, the city of ceramics in a loop of the Metauro, with fifteenth-century plant and arcades; Orange Flag of the Touring, is linked to Montefeltro-Della Rovere, of which it preserves the Ducal Palace with museum and library and the Doge's Barco, and houses the Mummies Cemetery.

Dedicated to San Dionigi until 1721, it is considered the oldest building still existing in the village, probably of the eleventh century. The restorations brought to light the foundations of a second apse and remains of graves, clues of a cemetery area of the VI-VII century.

The medieval shelter is still readable as an elliptical ring of buildings; in the center rise the neoclassical Town Hall and, in Piazza IV Novembre, the castle indicated by the Municipality as of the tenth century. On the parish churchyard there is the Monument to the Fallen.
The 17th century frescoed cloister.
Dedicated to the Novara Riccardo Casalaina, it has a decorated façade and three orders of stages arranged amphitheatre on different levels.
The stone of Luserna in a 20th century church.
The popular heart of the center.
The treasures hidden under the hill.
Sienese wooden statues are rare.
Medieval traces on Mount Pasillo.

From the top the view stretches over Valsassina, Valtellina, lakes of Como and Lugano and, on clear days, up to Monte Rosa; the territory of Val Muggiasca includes three alpine pastures, seven hamlets and twelve churches.
Medieval frescoes in one of the oldest Benedictine monasteries.

The municipality of Alta Val Venosta on Lake Resia, the artificial basin created in 1949-1950 by combining the natural lakes of Resia and Curon: the submerged water Curon Vecchia and part of Resia, and from the lake emerges only the Romanesque bell tower, today one of the best known images of South Tyrol. The Alta Val Venosta Museum tells the story; near Resia there are the Adige and you can visit the Bunker 20 and the barrier of the Vallo Alpino di Plamort.

An integral natural reserve established in 1998 and managed by the University of Catania: volcanic islets of about 500,000 years ago, linked to pre-ethnic volcanism, among white marl, clay and black basalts, with the columnar basalts of the Faraglione Grande and the arc of marna   .Occhio del Ciclope on the Lachea Island, about 400 meters from the coast. Built as a "receptum" in 1243, it was enlarged by Matteo I Visconti and Bernabò, who gave it the quadrilateral structure with high angular towers; passed in 1512 to the Marquis Brivio, since 1532 it was Gian Giacomo Medici, who made Melegnano a Marquisate. The halls (Emperor, Battles, Seasons, Hercules) and the staircase are frescoed in the middle of the XVI century with the enterprises of the marquis; on the revel with the bridge remain the coats of arms of Marzia Orsini and of the Sforza. Rectangular fortress with central mast and semicircular towers, born between 1029 and 1081 when the monks fortified a watchtower in the Fundum Sancti Pauli; passed to the Orsini (feud since 1429), in 1558 to the Cesi, who in 1603 established the headquarters of the Accademia dei Lincei, and then to the Borghese. House museum among the best preserved in Europe: the second floor recreates the home of Querini Stampalia, while on the ground floor stands out the area restored in 1963 by Carlo Scarpa.
Twenty arches of Gothic frescoes, including elephant.
The bishop's tower.
Known for its marble altar inlaid.

A few kilometers from the village, on the edge of the forest near Santa Maria della Montagna; dates back to the sixteenth century, it was rebuilt in the twentieth century and then renovated. Behind the altar there are frescoes by a local painter anonymously with Saints Peter and Paul and the Virgin with the Child; she preserves a painting from the sixteenth century with the Madonna delle Grazie.
Mattia Preti and Boccioni.

Church of perhaps the VII-VIII century dedicated to the first bishop of Rimini, with crypt of the XII century that preserves the relics of Santa Marcellina, arrived from Rome in 1666, and fifteenth-century bell tower of 25 meters. Inside works in white and black scagliola of the late seventeenth century, including the altar post of 1687 with St. Francis of Paola, a marble balustrade of the seventeenth century and the baptismal font obtained from a Roman cyp.
The Museum of the Economic Society.
The most unusual museum in Rome.
The medieval gates of the village and the oratory of San Bernardo; the village is known for the Infiorata del Corpus Domini.

Maniero built by the Normans in the 11th century on Lombard military structures, on the highest peak of the country: Riccardo Cuor di Leone (1190) and Giacomo d'Aragona (1289) passed there, and in 1250 Ruggiero di Lauria was born there, admiral of the Aragonese fleet remembered by Boccaccio in the Decameron. Abandoned at the end of the eighteenth century, the walls remain, the base of a circular tower, a fifteenth-century bulwark and walled blackbirds.
17th century sacred vestments and silvers of the upper valley.
The origins of Valle Trompia in a medieval brolet.

Small Romanesque building, probably from the 12th century, already mentioned in the donation of Ludovico II of 864: restored several times, it preserves fragments of frescoes. Just outside the center.

A pyramid-shaped hilltop village on a large containment wall, dominated by a Romanesque tower with cusp; walls and alleys make it an open-air museum and according to Italia.it was a stop of the Templars on the road from Rome to the Holy Land. From the square the look goes from Conero and Sibillini to Gran Sasso, Maiella and the sea.
The sacristy of Vanvitelli.
One of the three symbol churches of the city.
The bust of William Shakespeare sculpted by Sergio Pasetto on the wall of Piazza Bra facing the Arena, with a quote from Romeo and Juliet.
Walk in the heart of the plateau.
The autograph codes of a great preacher of the fifteenth century.
Grey gold quarries in the saddle.
The Bodoni character where he was born.

Baroque villa built in the seventeenth century by the Marquis Giorgio Clerici, today a museum with sculptures by Antonio Canova and paintings by Francesco Hayez. The park of about 20 acres combines Italian garden with hedges, statues and water games, romantic English garden and forests of rhododendrons, camellias and azaleas that make it a botanical garden. Open from March to November, with variable times; admission fee.

Next to the cathedral, the chapel wanted by Pope Sixtus IV, not to be confused with the Roman homonym; there is preserved the funeral monument of the pope's parents, with the Madonna enthroned between Sixtus IV and Saints Francis and Antonio da Padua.
Sacred art in the monastery.
The walls with eighteen towers overlooking the Ciociaria.
The green viewpoint above the roofs.
Dresses and accessories from the eighteenth to the twentieth century, the Gorizia lace and a section on the processing of silk with a large original torciator of the eighteenth century.

Arbatax cove protected by the Red Rocks under the promontory of Bellavista, between red and granite porphyry, with low and clear seabed and calm sea, suitable for children and snorkeling; you can reach it on foot with a path and a staircase. The name recalls the Saracen raids (is morus).
Church of the 14th century of which the earthquake of 1976 has spared only the main facade, with Gothic portal to figurative and floral capitals.
The Christ under water.

The parish church, built in 1607, has a granite façade and a hut roof; inside a barrel vault on three arches, artistic stained glass windows and a painting of the late seventeenth century,  ...St. Nicholas and St. Lucifer defenders of the divine motherhood. In the village also Santa Croce (XVIII century, restored in 1980) and the church of Carmel, eighteenth century in Gallura style.
The entrance door to the swamp and its history.
The waters and the Liberty dome that made Boario.

Church linked to the cult of the dead, with a bell dated 1649 and the "varetta" with the statues of the Deposed Christ and of the Risen Christ; the statue of Christ is the protagonist of the Affruntata and the processions of Holy Week.
The museum that explains Pompeii.

According to the MiC closed from 1 November to 28 February except events and holidays; the Park of Pompeii does not indicate ordinary times and announces only extraordinary openings: check on longola.it or at 081 8658111
The museum that traces the art of Pisa between ceramics, painting and sculpture.
The cathedral in the historic center, near the castle Ruffo.
The Greek city of Poseidonia, founded at the end of the 7th century BC: you can visit the Doric temples of Hera, Neptune and Athena, among the most important monuments of Magna Grecia.

15th century country building on the road to the Trompia Valley, built by the Counts Lodron and purchased by the Montini family in 1863: here on September 26, 1897 Pope Paul VI was born. It preserves a sundial dated 1658, a seventeenth-century balcony in wrought iron above the entrance and a gallery of the seventeenth century with twelve medallions of landscapes of the months and signs of the zodiac. Left in 1997 by Eng. Vittorio Montini at the Opera for Christian Education in Brescia, is a pilgrimage destination and has become a biographical journey on the stages of the Pope's life and pontificate; next to it lives a community of Daughters of Mary Help of Christians who welcomes visitors. Open from Tuesday to Saturday 10-12 and 14.30-17, Sunday 14.30-17.

Country at the entrance of the Germanasca Valley, in the Waldensian valleys, with the Latin School that hosts the exhibition "The ancient crafts" and the heroic vineyards of the Ramie, from which the Pinerolese Ramie was born produced only here and in Perosa Argentina.

The highest village in Sardinia, about 1000 meters on the Gennargentu, with the ski resorts of Monte Spada and Bruncu Spina: the Baroque basilica of the Virgin of the Martyrs with convent and oratory of San Michele, the districts with murals and roofs in scandulas, the Museum of Pastoral Culture and, towards Pratobello, the nuragic sanctuary of Gremanu and the tombs of Giganti di Madau.
MiC card (updated 2020) marks closed every day and refers to contacts of the diocesan Curia and Municipality; times not indicated by Teramo Tourism
Built in 1742 as a chapel of Villa Castiglioni (now Nai Bossi Poroli, of the eighteenth century), along the Naviglio immediately after the bridge, it is an example of Lombard rococo.
16th-century villa outside the centre, anchored to the rock with a suggestive waterfall and a round arched opening with water.

In the upper part of the old town, it dates back to the mid-eighteenth century and incorporates the ancient medieval church of San Nicolò; inside a large wooden choir with organ of Callido of 1767. It is dedicated to Maria Goretti, born in Corinaldo in 1890 and canonized in 1950.
Mithra's secret cult.

The Teatro Angelo Battelli, from the 1930s, has been completely restored and is still in operation; of the eighteenth century Teatro dei Condòmini remains the facade of the original building. Nearby is also the eighteenth-century Palazzo Antimi Clari with the adjoining chapel.

The convent of the Capuchins, the order of Father Pio, was completed in 1928 on a place chosen by the saint and houses a small museum of objects of his life; the path tells his biography, even in difficult times, and exhibits paintings of Francesco Gentile on the landscapes of his history. Open every day 9-13 and 15-19.
The church of the patron saint.
A miniature alpine world, carved in the box.

Born from the collection donated to the Municipality in 1984 by Don Giuseppe Dalla Tomba, Abbot of Villanova from 1939 to 1980, and set up from 2003 in the abbey complex designed by the geologist Enrico Castellaccio: 21 windows in two rooms illustrate the geology of the territory and fossils of all ages, with specimens of Bolca, and 78 minerals. Guided tours by appointment with volunteers.
Quadrangular coastal tower of the sixteenth century at Capo Colonna, completed in 1568; after the Unity of Italy hosted a brigade of the Guardia di Finanza.
Ancient parish church with Romanesque traces, inside the walls next to the Leonina door, with paintings and sacred furnishings.
Industrial sulfur archaeology in an open landscape.
The medieval village along the Via Francigena at the foot of Mount Pirchiriano, on whose summit stands the Sacred of San Michele, symbol of Piedmont.

Planetary with full-dome screen of 10 meters, with performances on constellations, Moon, planets and galaxies and stories about the myths of the night sky. In the Paleobotanic Garden there is the six-metre-long, life-size reconstruction of ... Tito , titanosaur of about 112 million years whose remains were found in the stones of a dry wall near the village, along with the models of a Diplodocus and a Sartriosaurus.

For the Faccanoni family the Milanese architect Giuseppe Sommaruga signed in Sarnico villa Pietro Faccanoni (1907, former spinning mill, irons by Alessandro Mazzucotelli and wood by Eugenio Quarti), villa Giuseppe Faccanoni (since 1907, with bas-reliefs by Ernesto Bazzaro and terrace garden open on the lake), villa Luigi Faccanoni today Villa Surre with high tower, the childhood nursery of 1912 and the mausoleum Faccanoni in the cemetery, with sculptures by Ambrogio Pirovano.

Ancient underground mill where already in the eighteenth century oil was produced throughout the fief. It is located in a karst depression with views of the Ionian-Salentine plain that separates the Murgia from the sea. Access is clear.
Gothic, on the main square, among the best preserved examples of medieval architecture in the area; documented since the 13th century, with Romanesque bell tower.
The lake occupies the basin of the Sabatino volcano off and is part of the regional park of about 17,000 hectares between Tuscia and Rome; sailing, rowing, surfing and birdwatching is practiced.

Sanctuary dedicated to Sant'Orso, patron saint of the village, and to the Madonna del Monte Summano, is the building of most architectural interest among the churches of Santorso. Designed by Ottone Calderari in 1777 and built in the early nineteenth century in neoclassical style, it houses interior decorations and paintings by Alessandro and Gian Battista Maganza.
Little Jerusalem.
The dome can be seen from all over the city.
A fresco from the 15th century that has just been restored.
A Romanesque parish church of the year 1000 in the hills of Garda.

An itinerary between historical residences: Palazzo Valentini and Casa Turrita in via Gramsci (mid 16th century), the Renaissance Palazzo Adamo Izzo with garden in via Vespucci, Palazzo Colella Bisanti on Piazzetta Villani with dovecote of 1563 enlarged in 1770, the Corte Soronzi of the seventeenth century, Palazzo Villani of the eighteenth century, Palazzo Arditi of the late seventeenth century, the sixteenth-century houses Cesi and Rollo (with garden hidden at the bottom of a long androne) and the neo-Gothic castle of Corso Italia, transformed in 1924 by an eighteenth-century structure.

Medieval church in red-ochite ochre, with a single nave with sail bell tower: the inscription on the façade recalls the consecration in 1291 after the renewal desired by the abbess Sardigna de Lacon, with Gothic changes in 1368. It was located in the old village of Zuri, today submerged by Lake Omodeo and visible in the periods of drought: since 1924, with the construction of the dam, it was dismantled and rebuilt with the bottom, returning to use after 28 days.
Reserve in San Savino, inside the Regional Park of Lake Trasimeno, with visitor center, documentation center, ringing station, wooden footbridge and birdwatching observers.

Borgo between the valleys of Potenza and Chienti, the ancient Pollentia rebuilt around the Mille as Montemilone and renamed Pollenza in 1862, known for over five centuries for ceramics, woodworking and restoration of antique furniture; in the center the Collegiate of San Biagio, the Verdi Theatre and Palazzo Cento, in the countryside the Altomedieval Abbey of Rambona.
A walk in the dream of a cardinal.
A marble by Domenico Gagini.
Loggia del Trecento in Piazza Marconi.
Sacred art from Piedmont between the Six and the nineteenth century.
Wet in the tubs of the monks of Cassiodoro.

In the countryside of San Tammaro stands the Real Site of Carditello, a Bourbon estate commissioned by Carlo di Borbone since 1744 and transformed by Ferdinand IV into a model farm, with the neoclassical residence of Francesco Collecini, the great royal galloping trough with the temple and the woods of eucalyptuses, holm oaks and cerres.
The Roman Fossato along the Flaminia.
A small 19th century golden theatre.

From the severe and simple façade, it is one of the best examples of seventeenth-century baroque in the Marches: it preserves paintings by Pasqualino Rossi and a rare organ by Giuseppe M. Head of 1675, still working.

Karst cavities in the limestone of the Poggio delle Forche, about one kilometer from the village following the signs; the name means "saxo" dripping, for the concretions on the walls. Once used as a barn, in the visitable stretches it has stairs and houses large colonies of bats, up to 2,000-2,500 specimens in summer; in the surrounding mining tunnels and Etruscan tombs.
The forgotten fruit varieties of the Secchia valley.
Under the basilica, the Roman city.
The eighteenth century of Neive.
Fountain and Delaunay in a former slaughterhouse on the sea.

Monte Crocetta was part of the fortifications of the First World War (Linea Cadorna), with trenches and restored walkways; the small church of San Maurizio, built in 1975 by the Alpini di Menaggio with two frescoes by Bruno Azimonti, overlooks a shrine in the bunker. From the viewpoint, about 30 minutes of steep climb from Cross, views of the Lake Centre, the Lecco branch, the Orobie and the Upper Lake.
The convent where Saint Francis passed, with a gold background of the fifteenth century.
The beach of the Cagliari, about 8 kilometers long from the Devil's Sella in Quartu, clear sand, historic establishments such as Lido and D'Aquila, kiosks and a bike path.
A nineteenth-century sanctuary in the center of the city.

The Belvedere Donatori di Sangue, known as the Pincio, is a avenue of about fifty lindens planted in 1901 with a large cedar in the center of Lebanon, among the oldest of the Marches. From the terrace the view goes from the Sibillini to the Adriatic, with the Basilica of Loreto, Recanati, Castelfidardo and Cingoli.

Regional reserve of about 1,000 hectares between Mentana, Monterotondo and Sant'Angelo Romano, managed by the Metropolitan City: hills mosaic between pastures and woods (Macchia del Barco, Bosco di Gattaceca, Monte San Francesco, Bosco Nardi), karst phenomena with sinkholes and swallowholes and a stretch of the ancient Via Nomentum-Eretum. Paths CAI 436-439; Welcome Area in via Nomentana km 21+200.

Distributed between the walkway of the cathedral, the chapel of Loreto and the Old Treasure, it tells the evolution of the Duomo with frescoes, sculptures, tombstones and paintings: the portal of the Nymphios, the tombs of the bishops Giorgio Manzolo and Balduinis, the Triptych of San Michele of the school of Antoniazzo Romano, the Madonna of the Gonfalone by Francesco Solimena, the silver throne by Aniello Guariniello (1755), the Breviarium aversanum (1499) and seven fifteenth-century tables by Angiolillo Arcuccio.
The shop life of an Apennine village.
An old-fashioned cellar in the vineyards.

The original nucleus of the village, built along a rocky ridge with rock spurs that emerge between the houses and the castle on the highest summit, was abandoned for the damage of war, the difficult conditions of life and the high hydrogeological risk; the new center, Rocchetta Nuova, was born at the end of the nineteenth century on the plateau between the Mainarde and Volturno. Today it is a suggestive ruin among whose alleys you can walk.

The birthplace of the verista writer Luigi Capuana, to which are dedicated the museum house and monument in Piazza Buglio; in the territory the archaeological area of Palikè, home of the most important sanctuary of the Siculi.
A 14th century cloister linked to the history of lemons.

On the fortress to the east of the village, you can reach the churchyard of San Michele Arcangelo on a path through medieval alleys; sighting tower built by the Arabs in the ninth century, cylindrical with a dry stone dome, crowned by the tower called "saracena" of uncertain dating. Already in ruins in the eighteenth century.
A small protected biotope.
A Franciscan hermitage suspended in the woods of Valtiberina.
The museum in the fifteenth century palace on Piazza Venezia.
The panorama from the Sibillini to the sea.
The city of the Tricolor, born here on January 7, 1797. All the locations of the Civic Museums are free of charge, including Palazzo dei Musei, Museo del Tricolore and Galleria Parmeggiani.
The terrace suspended over the city.

Natural monument in the forest of Addolì, on the border between Sadali and Seulo: a threefold karst phenomenon of swallowery, cave and rise, where the river Su Longufresu jumps for about 16 meters in a pond between limestone walls covered with moss. You can reach it with a marked path or with a guide.

Borgo perched on a hill of Molise, home to one of the oldest dioceses in the region: the Cathedral of Saints Nazarius, Celsus and Vittore, consecrated in 1076, houses the Romanesque crypt of San Casto. The historic centre is reached by climbing the steps of St. Nicholas, between Roman and medieval stones walled in the houses and crochet works of the Yarn Bombing.

Borgo at the outlet of Valcuvia, about 4 km from Lake Maggiore, the birthplace of the champion Alfredo Binda, to which a museum is dedicated; from the village start the paths towards the three waterfalls of the stream San Giulio and the ascent to the Passo del Cuvignone passing through the mountain village of Vararo.
The Doge's Palace with its park, in the centre of Pavullo, hosts the Civic Galleries with contemporary art exhibitions.

About a thousand artifacts on ancient crafts and peasant life: the first room exhibits archaeological finds of the territory, the others reconstruct domestic and working environments (plows and harrows, vinification, killing of the pig, corners of the blacksmith, carpenter, shoemaker, chaplain and knitwear).
Part of the homonymous monastery founded between the VII and IX century and connected to the aqueduct; destroyed by the Saracens in 844, and rebuilt by the abbot Angelario.
Maiolica dei Massa and Giaquinto's paintings.
A romantic walk.
The symbol of the valley, one of the highest jumps in the Alps.
One of the most amazing interiors in Italy, in a few minutes of visit.
The castle passing between fortress and Renaissance palace, overlooking the Fucino.

Neoclassical villa of the Marquis Ferrajoli in a park, with pronao tetrastyle and pediment with the myth of Ceres that teaches agriculture in Triptolemo; the interiors are decorated by Giovan Battista Caretti in the early nineteenth century. Twenty-three floors rise from the Paleolithic (fauna of 300,000-30,000 years ago) to the Middle Ages: the finds of the palafittic village of the Macine submerged in the lake (age of the Middle Bronze, XVIII-XVI century B.C.), the Lazio civilization of the period "Albano" (XI-IX century B.C.), the polychrome head of a Latin warrior of the 5th century B.C., the finds of the villas of Cavallacci (head of Tiberio Gemello) and Pompeo Magno, and a collection of graphics from the 17th to the 20th century with many works by Piranesi. Sunday opens only the 1st and 3rd of the month.

354 works among paintings, drawings and sketches from the sixteenth to the twentieth century, in five sections mostly chronological, including the ...Nude feminine by Man Ray (1912) and the dynamic rhythms curvilinear snapping by Giacomo Balla. Set up in the Renaissance Palazzo Sylos Calò, restored by Giovanni Alfonso Sylos until 1584, with the loggia on the piazza dismantled in 1929 and rebuilt in 1983.
The noble palace seat of the Risorgimento Museum.

Church of the Franciscan monastery disappeared, founded in the sixteenth century by Minori Conventuali: a single nave with a square apse covered by dome on plumes, stone portal with inscription of ...Andria Tuscano and date 1559, triumphal arch dated 1615 and an altar with fluted pilgrims and stylized roses.
Going down from the square for the homonymous coast, the neighborhood with half-timbered houses, the shroud fresco and the church of San Nicola da Tolentino.

Podere fortress built between the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries with a starry plan with six bastions; abandoned in the nineteenth century, it was prison and prison camp in the wars. You visit with guided tours.

Fortified village on Flaminia, which tradition attributed to Baron Sancio, of Germanic origin, grew around a Benedictine community. There are the church of San Benedetto (around the thousand, today desecrated and private) and that of San Cristoforo, then Santa Maria della Misericordia, with a miraculous image of Our Lady.
The rural memory of Belice.
From the tower you can see San Gimignano.
Church of the end of the fourteenth century at the exit from Porta dell'Ospedale, with two arches of a small cloister.
Prehistoric tombs of Sicily.
The Arab quarter with the cast houses.
The most intact Cistercian cloister in Emilia.

In the highest point of the medieval village, built in the Lombard age between the IX and XI century and rebuilt in the Norman-Sveva age; after the earthquake of 1466 he received two round towers with shoes that incorporate the most ancient square towers. The cylindrical tower, built by the Saracene feudal lords, is quoted from 1151. In the seventeenth century the Caracciolos transformed him into a residence; the name comes from the marriage of Laura Caracciolo with Emanuele Ruspoli, a family that held him until 1959, when Terry Margherita Blanc, widow of Camillo Ruspoli, donated him to the municipality. Rebuilt after the 1980 earthquake, it now houses municipal offices, the civic museum, the Pro Loco and the Museo del cinema dell'Associazione Sergio Leone, dedicated to film of the director (1929-1989).
The canvas of Moncalvo.
One of the most beautiful palaces, today home of archive and library.
The Middle Ages of Asti.

Colle di origine vulcanica at about 256 meters, 4 km from Siliqua, declared a Natural Monument in 1993 for the geological, landscape and flora-faunistic interest: at the foot a forest of eucalyptus and pines with picnic area, suitable for trekking and birdwatching, where they nest gheppio, buzzard and hawk cricket.

Museum of sacred art in the 17th-century church deconsecrated on the southern outskirts, dedicated first to the Virgin of the Rosary and then to St. Christopher, a single nave with three arches and wooden cover; it recalls the Way of Santiago for devotion to St. James, patron saint of the village. It exhibits polychrome statues from the 16th and 17th centuries and sacred furnishings recovered from St. James and the campestri churches, including works by the Genoese silversmith Luigi Montaldo and the Virgin sleeping on a canopy of carved and painted wood.

Alessandro Antonelli worked for Bellinzago from the mid-19th century to 1888: he expanded the parish church of San Clemente with vaults made without scaffolding, designed the Asilo De Medici with a staircase with a canopy in slabs of beola, the parish house and the square with the arcades; the bell tower, similar to the Mole di Torino, remain only unfinished pillars. The church is always visitable, the kindergarten only with guided tours.
Convent and church built in 1611 by some noblemen, with facade with churrigueresque decorations and floral bas-reliefs.
A rare site of industrial archaeology in Central Italy.

The medieval nucleus, the 'cittadella', preserves a stretch of walls with three bastions almost intact, alleys, arcades and tower houses; the Town Hall is of 1577, work of the Malombri brothers, the arcades of Piazza Repubblica (13 arches) of 1823. Around the New Church (1618), the Oratory of St. Anthony Abbot documented from 1364, and the fifteenth-century Casa Cavezzi.

Country on the eastern side of Etna, born in the early eighteenth century around the Mother Church in lava stone, famous for the Castagno dei Cento Cavalli, estimated over 3000 years, and for the nearby Castagno della Nave.
The secret school of preachers.
Opened in 2021, with a suspended terrace offering incredible views of the Valdera hills.
The fifteenth-century mill still at work.

An ancient place of worship north of the city along the Roman route: devotion dates back to tradition to before the thirteenth century, the foundation in the fourteenth century; expanded in Baroque forms in 1763, has interior to three aisles sober and luminous with altar greater in painted marble, two wooden altars and numerous ex-vote.
It dates back to the 9th century, with neoclassical façade and three Baroque naves inside: it houses a baptismal font from the 12th century and the icon of the Black Madonna of Capo Colonna.
The tower of Casale.
Mountain life on three floors.
Alexandria's living room.
A modern church with ancient paintings of the Chapel of San Carlo.

A 24,40 meters high square-plan tower, with protruding apparatus, built for the sighting and defence of the historic nucleus; unlike the major tower of Montone, it has been transformed into a bell tower.

Renaissance masterpiece by Antonio da Sangallo il Vecchio, built between 1518 and 1548 on a meadow under the walls, with a Greek cross with dome; it houses the fourteenth-century Madonna of San Biagio and inspired Michelangelo for San Pietro.
To be checked with the operator
Museum dedicated to the art and fauna of the Sibillini, also housed in the sixteenth-century Palazzo Leopardi next to the Pinacoteca Duranti.
To see the 16th century altarpiece of San Pantaleo.
The house of the works of Cola dell'Amatrice, waiting to reopen.

Medieval village on a hill inside the volcanic Caldera of Latera, 124 km from Rome: Palazzo Farnese on Piazza della Rocca, the Pieve di San Clemente from which starts the Tour of the seven churches, the historical fountains and the Museum of the Earth in the Grancia of San Pietro; from here passes the Path of the Briganti towards Lake Mezzano.
The ceremonial cart of Civita Giuliana.
The Annunciation of Castellano and the frescoes of 2008.
Cloister of the sixteenth century in the center of the village.
The church from which the city was born.
The municipal villa of eighteenth century plant, about 16,000 square meters with rare plant species and marble statues.

In the renovated Luxus house, it collects furnishings, books and pharmaceutical instruments between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries gathered by Dr. Fanni; the nucleus comes from the pharmacy Mancosu, of which remain counter and balance, and the reconstruction of the ancient pharmacy includes medicines distributed by the American army in the second world war; small library of ancient pharmacology. Free entrance.
The mountain house, among canyons, caves and ski slopes.
opens with the Mine Exhibition, closed until spring 2027 according to the site of the Park
Flowers at 2173 meters.
The medieval village on the slope.

Dry walls, stone paved sections, round pillars, large roofs and balconies in larch, a bread oven put into operation and the chapel of Saints George and Anna at the entrance; on the façades the frescoes of Giors Boneto, including a Crucifixion with St. Anthony Abbot and St. John the Evangelist and a Madonna of the Seven Dolori with the dead Christ. A carved beam carries an inscription on the brevity of life.

Ethnographic Museum of the Ecomuseum of the Umbro Apennines, inaugurated in 2008 in the sixteenth-century Town Hall on the main square: tools collected from the seventies, textile collection, a frame of the late eighteenth century and the installation Spinning Dolls of the British artist Liliane Lijn. In the weaving workshops, manual frames are still being worked; the spaces are finished with hemp and lime plaster.
The ruins on the white cliff where in January 1077 the emperor Henry IV waited for the forgiveness of Pope Gregory VII; the museum exhibits the finds of the nineteenth-century excavations.
The wooden group of Antonio Canepa and the feast of August 29.

Built in the 12th century for the first counts of Montefeltro on a spur of tuff and partly rebuilt by Francesco di Giorgio Martini at the end of the 15th century; consolidated by the Malatesta, it passed to the Montefeltro after their defeat in 1464. On three floors: basement living room with barrel vault, loggia, conference room and hanging garden with bust of Uguccione della Faggiola, and the noble floor with Renaissance windows overlooking Monte Carpegna and the valley of the Conca. Opening on request (tel. 0722 75350).
Beach, pine forest and citrus groves a few minutes from the village.
The Roman entrance to Spello.

Museum in the former mill Angeli, an ancient mill where wheat and other cereals were ground, in the hamlet of Marter. The permanent collection is dedicated to scarecrow, the result of researches by photographer Flavio Faganello in Trentino on these figures of straw, with legends and curiosities; it offers educational activities for schools and families.

The lead and zinc mine of Raibl-Cave del Predil, for centuries among the most important in Europe, closed in 1991, had 120 km of tunnels on 19 levels up to 520 m of depth. You can visit only with a guide (about an hour), on foot or with an electric train; the Exhibition of the mining tradition tells the country, the work of miners and the closure. A cumulative ticket with the military historical museum.
The fortified village on the sea.

Sanctuary from 1781 of the patron saint, who died in the monastery annexed in 1663, whose remains are in the crypt under the presbytery; preserves the table of Antonio Solario Vergine in throne and Saints (1503).
Octagonal church of 1714 with the iconic Baptism of Christ of Moncalvo and a precious organ of the seventeenth century.

The Church of Calvary was built in 1885 on a hill next to the village; the Church of Nucifora was built by the inhabitants of the homonymous neighborhood, devoted to Our Lady of Tindari, without aid or subsidies.
The Renaissance polyptych arrived from San Filastrio.

Along Via Roma, Palazzo Lattanzi and the sixteenth-century Palazzo Pretoria, seat of the civic magistrates until the early twentieth century (visible only from the outside); of the ancient belt remain Porta Romana and the well-preserved Porta Marina; in the center also Palazzo Tornaforte, Palazzo Anguillara called Palazzaccio and the church of the Madonna delle Lacrime.
The square of the city with the obelisk of the patron.
