An Irpina town on the river Saturday, born next to the Roman colony of Abellinum, whose remains on the plateau of the Civita form the archaeological park; in Piazza Umberto I the Palazzo della Dogana dei Grani houses the archaeological museum, while the church of Sant'Ippolisto houses the Specus Martyrum.
The largest hamlet, with winding alleys, climbs and covered passages typical of the medieval hillside villages, connected to the others by the ancient creuze.

Città dei papi Della Rovere sulla Riviera di Ponente: the Priamàr Fortress on the port with the civic museums, the Torretta di Leon Pancaldo, the Cathedral of the Assumption with the Sistine Chapel commissioned by Sisto IV and the Art Museum of Palazzo Gavotti, with the Sanctuary of Our Lady of Mercy in the valley of Letimbro.
The walls of Tuscania.
Roman mosaics next to the airport.

Refuges started in 1943 on the hill above the working-class village, able to accommodate 2500 people, built to protect workers from bombing; today they are visitable. Fixed openings for individuals and small groups from April to September; schools and groups over 3 people book at least 7 days before.
A cycle of fifteenth-century frescoes on the life of King David.
In Civitanova Alta, it hosts summer exhibitions for some years.
The relics of the martyr from the catacombs.
A 9 km ring path that starts from the centre, suitable for children; the most suggestive stretch passes under the railway bridge over the river Stura along a brick corridor.
The starting point of the visit.

Bronze statue of the sculptor Kee Sansen, inaugurated on December 14, 1997 between the Torrione and the church of San Celestino, symbol of the economy of the country linked to the processing of pigmeat.
The oldest gate in the city, with one of the oldest astronomical watches in Europe, in 1596.
the Municipality (July 2025) indicates the museum normally closed to the public, with only extraordinary openings; the MiC card instead shows opening Saturday and Sunday
The tower at the entrance of the lake.

Sanctuary perched on a spur of limestone rock overlooking the lake, reachable on foot or by car with a steep climb; it is known for the fresco of the Madonna and for the largest ex-vote in Europe, which represents the last moments of the bandit Zanzanu. The first reliable testimony of a church is the date 1458 on a fresco; it is still a pilgrimage destination.

In the thirteenth century the Municipality of Reggio built a castle to defend the Via Emilia and the passage on the Secchia, renovated by the Estensi in the second half of the fifteenth century; of the fortress there are few leftovers, mostly transformed into houses and offices. It was a prison of state: in his pit he was beheaded in 1822 Don Giuseppe Andreoli. Along the main street the Renaissance Palazzo Sacrati, already of the Boiardos, now town hall, opposite the eighteenth-century church of the SS. Annunziata, then the parish church of the Ss. Donnino and Biagio (1703-18), the former convent of Palazzo Rainusso and the civic and bell towers of the sixteenth century.
The Vermentino di Gallura told and tasted.

The centre retains its medieval appearance, with winding alleys, squares and arches, enclosed by walls with eighteen towers and three gates (St. Nicholas, St. Mary, St. Francis). The walk on the walls leads to the old wash-house square, to Porta San Francesco and the Posterula with its staircase, with views of the Ciociaria hills. At the entrance of the village, in Piazzale Granatieri of Sardinia, a monument recalls the battle of 1861 between the Kingdom of Italy and Bourbons.

Ancient settlement on the Via Mercatorum, connected on foot with the nearby Cornello: medieval houses restored according to the original architecture, arcade alleys, stone portals and wooden balconies. In the church of Carmine there are works by Carlo Ceresa and under the porch a great painted Saint Christopher to protect the travelers of the ancient road. Visitable all year round; there pass also the Via Mercatorum and the Ciclovia of the Val Brembana.

After the earthquake of 1783 the city was rebuilt under the name of Philadelphia, wanted by Bishop Serrao to love the inhabitants as brothers, and with the scheme of the Philadelphia by William Penn: two large arteries that cross form four quadrants, each with a church (San Francesco di Paola, San Teodoro, Santa Barbara and Madonna del Monte Carmelo), around a large square; the population distributed in the quadrants according to the social class.
The scenery of the village.
Relief that overlooks the village, destination of hikers, mountain bikers, knights and climbers.
The best preserved castle of Lunigiana, built from 1340 on towers prior to 1200: antique furnishings, paintings, legend of Bianca Maria Aloisia walled alive and the tradition of Dante's stay in 1306.
Red cliffs, sheltered bays and coves on the small promontory; walks from Punta Righini to the marina through the Pineta Marradi.
The Via Flaminia told from his finds.
Parish church built in the second half of the nineteenth century on the site of a more ancient cult building, in the center of the village.
From the Paleolithic to the late antiquity in a tower.
The marine history of the archipelago.
The Lombard origins of the village on Liri.
400 meters long, they connect Piazza del Grano to Piazza Duomo and host the town's shopping centre.

Small village of Aquila mentioned as "Perello" in a document dated 787, which grew around the church of San Benedetto Abate, a three-nave basilica of Longobard plant; the municipality also houses a museum of material culture.
According to Let's Marche historical center, monuments and museums are only partially accessible: check first
The baroque village of velvet.

Municipality of the Iblei near Lake Lentini, stop of the European Path E1 and land of red oranges; on the hills shared with Lentini stood Leontinoi, a calcidese colony of 729 BC, of which in the territory of Carlentini remain the South Gate and the fortifications; in the municipality there is also the frescoed Byzantine chapel of Santa Margherita.

In the old town, next to the parish, since 1990 he has exhibited ex-vote, rings, bracelets, daggers and pins from the Middle Bronze Age of the Iron, bronzes of tenderers and warriors from the sanctuary of Abini (including a figure with four eyes, four arms and double shield), the neolithic female idol of the plateau of Atzadalai and finds of the Mandrolisai; there is also the life-size reconstruction of a hut of S'Urbale.

Villa noble of the seventeenth century, residence of the last doge of Venice, with a park of trees from all over the world; there is preserved the original furnishings of the room of Napoleon, which here in 1797 signed the Treaty of Campoformido. It hosts great events and concerts and an Infopoint.

Borgo dell'alta valle del Potenza dominated by the pentagonal fortress built by Gentile da Varano after 1274; opposite, in a 14th century palace, the Museum of natural history with fossils and minerals, and in the territory the sanctuary of the Madonna delle Macchie with frescoes from the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries.
Built in the 11th century and rebuilt in the 16th century, Minervino was a bishop's seat.

Each of the 17 districts (Aquila, Bruco, Chiocciola, Civetta, Dragon, Giraffe, Istrice, Leocorn, Lupa, Nicchio, Goca, Onda, Pantera, Selva, Tartuca, Torre, Valdimontone) has its museum with the drapellons and memories of the Palio.

Ancient residence of the Doges and seat of political power, today the cultural center of the city with exhibitions and events; the Grimaldina Tower was jailed of political prisoners, including Jacopo Ruffini and Niccolò Paganini.

The largest trullo of Alberobello and the only two-storey one, with internal staircase in masonry: nucleus to the left of the early seventeenth century, the rest built in the first half of the eighteenth century for the family of the priest Cataldo Perta. The dome of about 14 meters dominates twelve minor cones; among the first trulli built with mortar, national monument since 1923. Vintage furnishings and garden.
Ossario in an ancient tufa quarry on the hill of Materdei with the remains of about 40,000 victims of the plague of 1656 and of the cholera of 1836, center of the cult of the "pezzentelle souls."
A short panoramic tour of the castle and arid meadows.
The civic collection of the sanctuary with furnishings, silver and works related to the cult of the Madonna della Ghiara.

Country of the hinterland the regiment dominated by the hill of the Norman castle, garrison disputed between Swabians, Angioini and Aragonese; in the district Ronzo you can visit by reservation the protohistoric necropolis with grotticella tombs dug in limestone, discovered by chance in 1953.
Archaeology and contemporary art in the same building.
The fortified heart of the village.
Sand and stain under the tower.

Built in 1625 on a pre-existing chapel, just outside the walls under the hill; Renaissance outside, with a Latin cross with cylindrical dome, and Baroque inside, where there is a 16th century fresco of the Madonna del Latte.
The Risen in olive wood.
The religious heart of the village on the Arno.

Under Martin V the village was surrounded by walls and towers, partly preserved. The Palazzo del Comune, Renaissance, has a loggia with five arches with the coat of arms of Pope Martino V Colonna joined to the Farnese and a plaque for Giuseppe Garibaldi. You enter from the Porta di San Martino, with a panoramic terrace, and from the Porta Magenta, designed by Vignola, called "Maskone" for the face carved at the top.
The giant bench everyone can actually get on.
Over one hundred artificial cavities dug into the tuff under the hill: tunnels with niches that sometimes end up in a circular hall. The origin is still being discussed.
A white sandy cove with a view of Serpentara.
The largest railway model in South Tyrol.
A 17th century cloister intact along the walls.
The village of origin of Pineto, on the hills.
The frescoes of San Vito Vecchio.

Bastión complex that dominates the village, reachable on foot in about half an hour: from the porch after the Venetian Bridge starts the Scala in Telvana, which passes from the monastery of the Clarisses and the Franciscans and continues along the mule track of the castles.
Renaissance Latin cross church, built around 1400.
Route between galleries, mining buildings and mineral fusion plants, with museums and information points between Valpelline and Ollomont.
A plain garden park with a museum of distant peoples.
The Annunciation of a 17th century Lucanian painter.
The cellar is carved into the rock of the Dormisch brewery.

On Piazza Garibaldi, with Romanesque façade dated 1199 that bears engraved the names of the architects; inside a 16th century baptismal font and a wooden Madonna of the eighteenth century. Near the cloister of the former convent of Santa Maria Maddalena.

In the historic centre the murals of the street artist Giuseppe Caruso transform vico Leone into an open-air museum, between narrow alleys and steep staircases of a village among the calanchi of the Marchesato.
The Sannite peasant civilization.
museum under construction in the new premises; information Municipality 0881 592022
The MiC card (updated to March 2021) is closed every day; tel. 095 921615

Park that recreates the life of the workshops of the past: 15,000 artefacts distributed in 42 artisan workshops, preserved in their original context without the "decontextualization" typical of the collections.

With about 43 km2 it is the largest municipality in the Val Fontanabuona, from Passo dell'Anchetta to the Ramaceto massif; in Calvari the Museum of Legacy Cuneo tells about the life and crafts of the past, and from the valley bottom start trails towards the Alta Via dei Monti Liguri and Monte Ramaceto.
The Vizzinese house of Verga, stage of the Verghian places.
A small medieval monastery built by the Benedictines of Montecassino, according to Visit Lazio in the 11th century, on a hill west of the village; the feast of the saint is held on June 12.
A Lombard Romanesque cloister on the lake.
Museum dedicated to bergamot, the citrus of Reggio whose essence is protected by the DOP "Bergamotto di Reggio Calabria" (Bergamot of Reggio Calabria) "Essential Oil."

Municipality of the province of Barletta-Andria-Trani with a nineteenth-century center: in Piazza Trieste the former Palazzo di Città of 1847, now the museum seat, and the Matrice Church, the "Church Grande" rebuilt on a project by Marino Marrone and reopened to worship in 1963.

The thermal town on the Tyrrhenian Sea, founded as Thermai by the Carthaginians in 407 BC: the Civic Museum of the Baldassare Romano in an ancient hospital of the fourteenth century, the seventeenth-century Cathedral, the Municipal Villa with the remains of the Roman curia, the spa with the Grand Hotel and, in Buonfornello, the archaeological area of the Greek colony of Himera.
The Spinelli literary salon.

Designed in 1911 by the Anonymous Theatre Society, with the works interrupted by the First World War, opened in 1933 and in 1934 it was named after Antonio Salieri; it replaced the ancient theatre of the fortress, abandoned in 1903 and destroyed by the bombs of the Second World War.
Oneglia's living room.

Azzone Visconti had it built in memory of the victory in the battle of Parabiago on 21 February 1339; entrusted in 1481 to the Order of St. Ambrose ad nemus, had a Cistercian monastery next to him since 1699-1705, then became a school. The current church, rebuilt and consecrated on 19 April 1713, has a bell tower of about 40 meters of 1723 and the organ of 1716 B. Reina with C-carvings. Bossi; preserves canvases by G.B. Sassi and Pietro da Pietra, a altarpiece of the Lampugnani di Legnano, frescoes by T. Formentini and a Gothic inscription in the choir.

Historical, ethnographic and naturalistic eco-museum founded in 1982 by the Association Amici della Val Codera and recognized by Regione Lombardia, divided between the villages of Codera and San Giorgio: domestic life, weaving, breeding and milk, chestnut, school, handicrafts and minerals (aquamarine and garnet) in the House of Valle; in San Giorgio the historical section, with the Thirty Years War, and the outdoor reconstruction of the work of the picapreda. You can only reach it on foot; free admission.
Frescoes and a Via Crucis in the church of the village.
When fashion marries art.

Borgo della Valle Arroscia, the site of the archaeological laboratory of the territorial museum "I volte dell'Ubagu" (The Faces of the Ubagu), from which starts a naturalistic, speleological and archaeological path towards the valleys Pennavaira and Ferraia, between the caves (the arms) inhabited since prehistory and the ruins of the castle.

To the south-west of the village, it is one of the oldest churches in the area of Città di Castello: early Christian basilica built around the crypt that guarded the tomb of San Crescenziano, a legionary martyrized here under Diocletian, with a bas-relief of the 8th century of the saint who kills the dragon.

The walled village was founded in the fourteenth century by Charles II of Anjou on the site of the ancient Aequa, whose name is linked to the Latin aequus (the plain) because it rises on a flat stretch of the cliff; you visit on foot, left the car at the margins. From the village a steep path descends at the foot of the tuff cliff, towards the beaches of Marina di Equa and Marina di Seiano.

Between Monterosso and Riomaggiore, the village of the Cinque Terre with the only marina, the church of Santa Margherita d'Antiochia on the sea and the tower Doria, the most beautiful village in Italy; in the municipality also Corniglia, the only one of the Cinque Terre not facing the shore.

Roman maritime colony founded in 296 BC on the right bank of Liri-Garigliano, with Appia as the maximum decuman. You can visit the republican forum (II century BC) with the Capitolium and the theatre, the imperial forum with remains of curia and basilica, the macellum and the baths with mosaics, in the aspect of the city of Ariane. Since 1984 the Antiquarium, in the ambulances of the theater, exhibits the "gallery of the statues" with Augustus, Livia and the Muse, the lapidarium and a series of togati. Closed Monday and Tuesday; free on the first Sunday of the month; Cassino-Minturno €8 integrated ticket and cumulative of the state sites of the province of Latina €12.
A stop in the area of prehistoric finds.
The country's stage door.

Surviving section of the seventeenth-century fortifications in the lower part of the city, near the Po, made of brick and superimposed stones; the rest was demolished at the will of Napoleon to recover the material.

Benedictine monastery at the foot of Mount Longina, between the Middle Ages, late Gothic and Renaissance; the abbey church of Santa Maria Assunta has been a minor basilica since 1954. Three of the four cloisters (botanical, double and wall) are of the second half of the fifteenth century; in the monumental refectory a  "Crucifixion" by Bartolomeo Montagna of the late fifteenth century and paintings by G.B. Zelotti. Guided tours without reservation from the concierge (weekly except Monday at 15 and 16 in winter, 15.30 and 16.30 in summer; Sunday and holidays afternoon); closed on Monday and on some holidays; offer for restorations, with at least €5 you receive the photo guide.
Built at the end of the 19th century, during the Republic of Salò, he hosted Mussolini's offices, who chose another villa further north, in San Faustino, as his personal residence.

Former military refuge of the Alpine Valley, today a cultural space between art, history and memory with exhibitions, guided tours and events in its corridors; above the village, about 10 minutes walk.
The bohemian district of design and shops; every third Sunday of the month it is animated with the craft market.

The historic centre preserves in architecture and artistic details the most recent history of the village, gathered around the Castello de Falconibus and the church of Santa Maria La Nova, which preserves a reproduction of the cave of Lourdes.

The park on the slopes of Posillipo with the Roman doumbarium traditionally called the tomb of Virgil, the mausoleum of Leopardi of 1939, a stretch of the Augustan aqueduct and the entrance of the Crypta Neapolitana.

Two-storey public building, typical of the reconstruction followed by the earthquake of 1908 in southern Calabria, with two lateral bodies slightly protruding and cantonal smooth rustic. Open Monday to Friday 8-18.
The facade covered in coats of arms.
The Romanesque bell tower of the bishop's city.
To be verified: exhibitions by Fondazione Modena Arti Visive
A walk in the English park of a 19th century villa.

Stone village recovered from the almost total ruin by Giancarlo De Carlo as one of the first telematic medieval villages in Europe: caruggi, piazzette, terraces and white windows, with views of the valley.
The wild area.

Country of vineyards and hazelnuts on the hill of the Valtiglione, south of Asti, with the motto "Hospes veniat, fugiat hostis"; probably born as a fortified village of Longobard, preserves the remains of the castle of 1160, the parish church of San Biagio, the neoclassical town hall and two civic museums, the MUSarMO of modern art and the Museum of Vine and Wine.
In front of the former municipal palace, the scans and the armchair of the sixteenth-century Vallaise court.
The collegiate of the Grail legend.

Romanesque church with two naves in Moltrasino stone, in the locality of Vignola along the ancient Via Regia: dates back to the 11th century, a document of 1197 attests to a charity dedicated to the saint and in the 17th century was used as a lazzaretto. Outside the images of St. Agatha and St. Christopher, protectors of the travelers; inside sixteenth-century frescoes including the Christ Pantocrator between the Saints Rocco and Antonio Abate (restored in 2006) and a Renaissance wooden crucifix. Next to the churchyard is the nineteenth-century chapel Lucini Passalacqua.

Second century B.C. marble slab (70 x 74 cm), found by chance in the seventeenth century in San Pietro, linked to the Roman road from Capua to Reggio, of which it appoints some stations; it had to be at the base of a commemorative monument of the street. The Municipality indicates it as the most important Roman testimony of the Vallo di Diano.
Sanmicheli in the square.

Copper mine already exploited by the Nuragics and then by Phoenicians, Carthaginians and Romans (there remain galleries, a ingot and the remains of an imperial miner); excavations since 1517, flotation plant since 1920, mining village since 1936 with school, infirmary, shop and church, about 300 workers in the 1960s and closure in 1983, when nineteen miners occupied the wells for twenty days to 400 meters deep. Open to the public since 2020 as an area of the Geominerario Park: you can visit the Phoenician and Roman galleries, the laundry left as it was on the last day of work, cable car, trains and village, with former miners such as guides and helmet.

Opened in 1989 in the former Carmelite monastery of Santa Maria Maddalena dei Pazzi, it exhibits prehistoric and protohistoric finds of excavations started in the territory since 1980 and, in the most recent rooms, medieval and modern materials. In a large room the skeleton of the Woman of Ostuni, a twenty-year-old lived about 25,000 years ago in the Paleolithic, buried with the fetus in the womb in the cave of Santa Maria di Agnano. The adjoining church of San Vito Martire, known as the Monacelle (1750-1752), marks the beginning of the rococo in Ostuni.
Contemporary art at the border.
In the former Franciscan oratory, works of the churches of the territory, including the Terracotta Complaint of the workshop of Baccio da Montelupo and an archaeological section.
Crossed by many itineraries where you can observe marmots, chamois and many species of butterflies; in Champorcher a visitor center informs about flora, fauna and visits.
Fossils of a hundred million years in the Fortore.
Our Lady of Trapani.
About 5 km from the historic centre, it is the original site of the village, razed to the ground in the 12th century.
Church of ancient origin rebuilt in 1879 in neoclassical style, with three portals facade and circular windows; the bell tower is 36 meters high.
It houses Neolithic finds from Sabucina, Gibil Gabib, Monte Capodarso and Monte San Giuliano.
Example of a two-storey medieval house with external staircase, two large round arches on a central column and a decoration of arches on shelves.

Città dei Caetani sull'Appia, with the castle of the fourteenth century that houses the Civic Archaeological Museum, the Palazzo del Principe, where in 1378 the Antipope Clement VII was elected, the Jewish district of Judea and the stretch of Via Appia Antica towards Itri, UNESCO World Heritage since 2024; between Fondi Lake and Blue Flag beaches.
A path of valley floor with slight difference in altitude; around the lake Pellaud a ring that can be crossed with the stroller.

The main port on the east coast, with a marina of about 650 berths; it is the starting point of the boat trips to the coast of Baunei and the Gulf of Orosei, between Cala Goloritzé, Cala Mariolu, Cala Luna, Pedra Longa and the caves of Fico and Bue Marino.
A curiosity about the variant of the Renaissance Ring.
The city that made the accordion its industry.

Baroque courtyard building that houses library, historical archive and civic museum, with artifacts from the Eneolithic to the late Byzantine, a vast collection of paintings and a room dedicated to a contemporary artist Mazarese with aqueforts, aquatin and reliefs. The municipality indicates it as accessible free of charge (October 2026).
The royal wedding sanctuary of 1832.

Borgo dei Monti Aurunci known as the village of longevity, seat of the Ente Parco; the medieval center is closed by a wall integrated with twelve cylindrical towers, crossed outside from the Passeggiata dell'Amore, and dominates the landscape up to the Gulf of Gaeta.

Romanesque church of the 11th century with late Dogotic portal of 1472, decorated with sculptures with ornamental, vegetable and anthropomorphic motifs; in the bezel a fresco of the Madonna with Child and two saints, one with a grindstone around the neck, symbol of martyrdom.

Dedicated to Moto Laverda, whose plant was located south of Villa Malvezzi from the second post-war period to the seventies, exhibits over 100 motorcycles. The city guide indicates this as it was inaugurated in 2022.

Founded in 1957, it is indicated as the first winery born in the whole province of Bergamo; it has vineyards in Almenno, Pontida, Palazzago, Mapello and Scanzo, cultivated mainly in Merlot, Cabernet, Manzoni and Chardonnay. It produces red Valcalepio and IGT San Martino, a Blanc de Blancs of Chardonnay only with charmat method in autoclave and, since the end of 2021, a red from Merlot vineyards with more than 25 years. For visits and tastings contact the cellar (tel. 035 795035).
Industrial archaeology in the green of the Dauni Mountains.
The early Christian tombstone.
A bourgeois house in the 19th century.
The wooden Pietà di Del Maino.
Renaissance Palace of the sixteenth century built for Margherita d'Austria on a project by Giacomo Della Porta; it houses the Museum of Contemporary Art and the Pinacoteca Cascella.

To celebrate the victory of January 1797 and honor the fallen, Napoleon had it erected in 1806, on the height that dominates the plain of the Adige, a Doric column about 20 meters high; in 1814 after its fall, the Austrians demolished it and some pieces remain at the foot of the white marble base. In the plain of Canale today there is a mausoleum, near the remains of the French fighters. Free access.

Golden sand dunes modelled by the maestral, up to 60 meters tall, that push for kilometers inland; the beach is about seven kilometers long and from 2018 a stretch of about 800 meters is naturist beach. Clear seabed that descends quickly, with the wreck of an English ship about 200 meters from the shore; sea often moved, frequented for windsurfing, kite and surfing even in winter. Secular, lentisque and olive ginepri; on the shore nest the sea turtles.
Walk in the woods around the hermitage with a view of the Apennines.

At the foot of the hill of Madonna d'Itria, it was built in the first decades of the sixteenth century by the Carafa with quadrangular plant and central light well, then equipped with four corner towers; in the seventeenth century Vespasiano Spinelli transformed it into a fortress and a noble residence. Since 1845 it belongs to the Sabatini family, from which the name; from the plateau the look reaches the coastal towers.
The cemetery of the popes.
The bell tower symbol of Varazze and a Cambiaso.
Eagle from above.
Ideal on the first day, to get the picture of the city.

The historic centre preserves the Renaissance Palazzo Martini, which belonged to the Jesuits and then to Monsignor Gürtler, with frescoed rooms; on Corso Roma the façade of Palazzo Rosa with the dial of a 24-hour mechanical watch; Piazza Garibaldi, formerly Piazza San Vito, was created in 1780-1791 during the episcopate of Gürtler. The village overlooks the Fortore valley, whose waters form the dam of Occhito.

Built between the 12th and 13th centuries on a rocky spur 1233 meters above the valley, with a hut façade, Gothic bell tower on the fence of the old cemetery and portal under a large Romanesque arch. Inside, cycles of four painters: an anonymous master of the second half of the fourteenth century (Christ throne between Saints Peter and Paul, the twelve apostles, the Evangelists on the blue vault), a second artist in the chapel, a perhaps Lombard master of the first fifteenth century in the minor apse (Nativity, Adoration of the Magi, Dormitio Virginis, with a rare shepherd playing the bagpipes) and a painter of the first sixteenth century. The key goes back to the Locanda Al Torch, in the hamlet of Paschero.
A thousand-year-old tower on the Panicale trail.
The oldest university garden in the world.
Underground Roman aqueduct about seven meters deep under the old town, still in operation: it feeds the Old and New fountains.
For a Renaissance shrine with works of three centuries.
Stone alleys and an elephant-shaped rock.
The entire old town, rebuilt on a new site after 1693, is part of the UNESCO site of the late Baroque towns of Val di Noto.
Museum dedicated to the history and art of photography, with a collection from the pioneering period to today, thematic exhibitions, temporary exhibitions and workshops for adults and teenagers.
Frescoes of the sixteenth century and silver sacred.

Country of origin of the family of Salvatore Quasimodo, autonomous municipality since 1816: the Literary Park dedicated to him occupies the ancient railway station with vintage cars, and the fifteenth-century Saracen Tower, sung by the poet, hosts a permanent exhibition; in the church of the district Botteghelle the poet was baptized.

Popular seaside resort from the second half of the nineteenth century, with fine sandy beaches, Blue Flag sea, a long seafront and the Pontile della Sirena; on the border between Pescara and Chieti begins the Costa dei Trabocchi. In Palazzo San Domenico the MuMi houses the great paintings by Francesco Paolo Michetti and the works of the Michetti Prize.

Ancient via della trashumanza 211 km long, that crosses 4 regions, 6 provinces and 41 municipalities connecting the Abruzzo montano to the Tavoliere Apulia; it is subject to archaeological constraint, and transhumance is registered since 2019 in the UNESCO List of the Cultural Heritage Immaterial. From the village you can reach Campo del Monaco, about 5 km.

The town unites the two villages of Gazzada and Schianno, between the high plain and the morainic hills that go up towards the Prealps; in Gazzada stands Villa Cagnola, romantic residence with English park and a precious collection of gold-bottom paintings, while in Schianno the church of the Saints Cosma and Damiano preserves the only bell tower-portico (clocher-porche) of Lombardy.
The town fortress whose construction worked Gian Giacomo dell'Acaya, author also of Porta Napoli; you can visit underground and secret.

Museum spread all over the valley, made above all of paths to walk to know its characteristic places and natural and human history, with the participation of the community. Visits every day only by reservation.

Medieval village of the upper Maceratese among woods and streams, leads to the Karst plateau of Montelago and the Scurosa Valley: the tower of Da Varano, the museum of agricultural tools in the castle, the waterfall of Scarzito in the village and the Enchanted Wood in the public gardens.

The medieval refuge (I Rusèt) rises to the west of the castle on the same hill, of an elongated north-south shape with an overhang to the west: there were preserved crops and in case of danger there were sheltered families and animals. The houses are in stone split up of the hill; in the Torre Porta d'accesso you can still see the tracks dug by the Saracinesca. You walk freely from the streets of the center; the buildings are private.
The Habsburgs district.
The finds of Privernum in the center.
Three-nave church with Romanesque bell tower, awarded the Blue Shield for the protection of cultural heritage: it houses the fourteenth-century icon of the Madonna delle Grazie and numerous frescoes.

The brick tower, built in 1370, dominates the centre from the top of a steep hill and controls the valley; it is the only trace of the castle of Corata, whose massive walls opened with Porta Maggiore or Porta dell'Angelo. The route along the ancient walls of the old town, with a medieval atmosphere, arrives at the Torrione, from which you can enjoy the view of the Vibrata Valley; from the benches of the village you can see the teraman coast and the Laga Mountains.

He collected the works of the futurist sculptor Regina Cassolo, donated to the city by her husband Luigi Bracchi: 52 sculptures and about 500 drawings, temperas and collages. The route goes from the Futurism of the thirties to the Movement concrete art.
5,000-year-old graves, World Heritage.
Built between 1543 and 1548 with the Franciscan monastery, it is indicated as the first Renaissance building on the island.
Wide beach south of the port that extends to the hamlet of Marcelli, with bathing establishments and services designed for families.

Borgo del Salento about 40 km from Lecce, surrounded by countryside and olive groves in the territory of the Parco dei Paduli, dotted with pajare. The heart is Piazza Cito with Palazzo Cito and the sixteenth-century Chiesa Matrice di San Leonardo; not far away is the Doge's Palace and the crypt of the Madonna della Consolazione. Every March 19, the rite of the Tables of St. Joseph is renewed.
The oldest church in the country, remained open to worship even after the suppression of the Dominican monastery.

Where the daunio settlement of Tiati (IX-IV century BC) was located, allied with the Sannites against Rome and then linked to Rome after 318 BC, the Romans concentrated the municipality of Teanum Apulum between the Mengoni Cup and the Church's Pezze. At the edge of the city, in the imperial age (I-II century AD), the amphitheatre was built with irregular elliptical plan, probably obtained on the slope, brought to light by the excavation of the Superintendence of 2020: part of the cavea remains, a passage turned towards the arena and a stretch of arena bordered by parapets in brick, for about 442 m2. About 500 m to the west remains the tower called "Church of Civitate" of the medieval fortified town (XI-XV century); the area is protected by ministerial decrees of 1990-1997.
The parish church of Prato, cited in documents since 1098, consecrated in the present form in 1718 and sanctuary since 2019.
A rare Byzantine sign.
In the house of the Nobel laureate.
The seventeenth-century village of the Justinians.

Common spread of the Alpe Cimbra with the karst lake loved by Sigmund Freud and the Fort Belvedere-Gschwent (1908-1914), between the Austro-Hungarian fortresses best preserved in Trentino, today Museum of the Great War; in Slaghenaufi the Austro-Hungarian military cemetery.
The arches of the aqueduct, in the archaeological area between the arch of Augustus and the castle.
To understand Bova's greek identity.
The church and lindens of the capital.

In the district of Nubia, in a seventeenth-century lamp where salt was worked (the Casa Salaria), it tells centuries of salt culture of western Sicily; next to it there is a large windmill that raised sea water and ground the raw salt. It exhibits the original tools of the salt-salters, a vine of Archimedes, sacks of jute, millstones, mill blades and photographs in black and white; it was born on the initiative of Alberto Culcasi with the provincial body for tourism, the Municipality and the faculties of Letters and Architecture of the University of Palermo, and is part of the project Via del Sale.

Rococo church started on May 5, 1747 on a project by Giovanni Mariani, then revised by Giuseppe Morgese, and consecrated on October 22, 1775; the façade in 37 meters high limestone has the high relief of St. Martin who divides the cloak with the poor. Inside the main altar of Sanmartino and Varriale (1773) with the Saint Martin of Stephen of Putignano (1518) and the statues of Abundance and Charity, the Christ to the wooden Column of 1622 and the Hat of the Sacrament with paintings by Domenico Carella; Minor Basilica since 1998.
In the sixteenth century convent of the Capuchins: drawings, objects, tools, weapons and clothes of the peoples of Ethiopia collected by Cardinal William Massaia during his mission.
In Piazza Beverini, neo-Gothic façade with black and white bands; probably founded in 1271, rebuilt in the first half of the fifteenth century and modified several times in the twentieth century.
The Lombard baroque.
The peasant life of the Gargano told by his objects.
The Marche peasant world in eight halls.

Reserve established in 2009, indicated as the largest protected area of Lombardy: an almost flat valley floor between granite walls, suitable for all, with the Qualico pond shortly after the entrance and trails towards the Cascina Piana (1,092 m), the Playa di Rasica and the Alpe Pioda. You enter on foot from San Martino (parking space about 20 minutes; in the parking lot with charge 7 euros per day), with a summer shuttle to Panscèr.
The treasure under the Temple.
Stucchi and a table of the sixteenth century in the mother church of the village.
A rocky town with very remote origins.
The place of Maria Bricca's feat in the war of Spanish succession.
The artifacts of the culture of Golasecca in the country that gives it its name.
The griffins returned from Getty, masterpiece of daunia art.
The deco temple of Galileo Chini.
Monumental basement building with horseshoe, dated between the end of the 1st century BC and the Augustian age, to which you can access from the garden on Piazza Giovanni XXIII.
The remains of the imperial palace on the sea.
The sky as a ceiling.
The civic heart of old Bormio.
The eighteenth-century Barboglio church, now in the municipality.
One of the largest towers on the coast.
The cathedral of the Pope.
To understand the Black Rooster.

Walled village of the Vallesina with rectangular plan, with square and cylindrical towers: in the Renaissance Palazzo Marcelli is home to the Telephone Museum, with over 200 antique appliances; around the churches of San Marcello and Santa Maria del Rosario.

Borgo dei Monti Dauni, Orange Flag of the Touring, dominated by the Castle of Aquino with the ogival tower "a bow of ship" with the church matrix eighteenth century by the majolica bell tower, numerous fountains and, outside the village, the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Pozzo.
Walking between pine forests and the sea to the most beautiful beach of Gargano.

Built in 1936 in neo-Gothic style, it has three aisles with reinforced concrete Y-pillars, singing hallway, flat apse with large neo-Gothic window and marble floors. It houses a polychrome tabernacle in green marble of Gimigliano embedded in the high altar, the statue of the patroness attributed to the school of the Droses of Satriano, paintings and liturgical furnishings. Unvisible during functions.
A balcony on Casentino.
The tools of peasant life ciocaria.

The castle is documented from 1092, when it was part of the monastery of San Benedetto in Perillis; purchased in 1377 by the Cantelmo, who held it until 1579, then passed to Pietro Pietropaoli and the Grand Duke of Tuscany Cosimo de' Medici. The current Medici castle-palace of the 16th century has a rectangular plan around a courtyard, a quadrangular tower to the north, imposing walls, crenellated tower and medieval and Renaissance windows; it dominates the village and is now a private residence of the De Sanctis family.
The mother church.
A medieval castle above the lakes.

In the Castle of Torre, from the Paleolithic to the Renaissance: Neolithic villages, castelliers, the Roman Villa of Torre, late Dolomite necropolis, fifteenth century ceramics and the findings of the UNESCO site of Palù di Livenza, with the history of the castle and Count Giuseppe di Ragogna.
From the beacon tower of the lake to the panorama of the plain.

Opened in 2005 in the east wing of Palazzo Rospigliosi, on about 1,400 m2 it exhibits more than 800 pieces, about one third of the collection, which tell the story of the toy in Italy in the last century, with European and American productions (brands like Lehmann, Märklin and Bing), ordered for themes that bind the game to objects and social life; three rooms host temporary exhibitions. Free under 6 years, reduced from 6 to 12 years and over 65 years; closed on Mondays and from 10 to 24 August, with seasonal times (in winter Tuesdays and Fridays 9-13 and 15-18, Wednesdays and Thursdays 9-13, Saturdays and Sundays 10-13 and 15-18).

Galatina lived the greatest splendor between the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries under the Orsini del Balzo, which is due to the Basilica of Santa Caterina d'Alessandria with its cycle of frescoes. In the ancient village, between three doors and eighteenth-century palaces, the Mother Church of Saints Peter and Paul and the Chapel of Saint Paul tied to tarantism; here the pastry was born.
Two churches of popular devotion.
Like the oil under the ground.

Perhaps of the year 1000 and repeatedly rebuilt, the last in 1921, in white stone and basalt; it rises in the site of a medieval village destroyed by Saracen raids in the fifteenth century, among vineyards and olive groves.
A medieval village in Liguria remained pedestrian.
The sky of Alto Molise, with planetarium.

Castello di origine Longobarda dei Ricasoli since 1141, considered the oldest winery in Italy: you can visit the garden, the museum and the ramparts, with tastings and guided tours; the residence of the baron remains private.

In the palace of 1554, recently restored, the civic museum and the art collection of a private collector: above all landscapes and views, with a pastel self-portrait of Rosalba Career, a portrait of Cosimo III de' Medici embroidered in silk and a sketch of Giuseppe Nicola Nasini.
The arches of the bridge that led the Via Emilia on the Parma stream, today visible in the underpass of Via Mazzini, in the center of the city.
A villa with garden away from the chaos of the center.
The castle of the bishop-warriors of Campaldino.

The southern gate to the Matese massif was a centre of wool and textiles production between the sixteenth and eighteenth centuries thanks to the energy of two springs; in the historic center there are the Dominican complex of San Tommaso d'Aquino with the MuCiRaMa civic museum, the chapel of San Biagio frescoed and the Palazzo ducale dei Gaetani.
The square on the path of the Via Emilia romana, with Palazzo del Governore and the sundial, starting point for Strada Cavour and Piazza Duomo.
A path to listen to.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione del Monferrato built around the remains of the castle, with a view of the Alps and the Sacro Monte di Crea.
Studies of the future Sixtus V.
Unique in Italy, opened in 2001 and renovated in 2023 in the former glass factory Boschi: it tells the workmanship of glass from medieval origins (vetreries known from 1331) to lead crystal of 1963.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Loffredo, on two floors, from the previous phase of Greek colonization to the Roman conquest: furnishings of the necropolis of Vaglio with armour and jewelry between the end VI and mid-V century BC, and the materials of the sanctuary of Rossano di Vaglio of the fourth century BC, rebuilt in a hall.

Built in the thirteenth century to replace the first church of the castle, considered too small, it was renovated from the end of the seventeenth century, when the loggia was added to the façade; the bell tower is from the nineteenth century and the current appearance dates back to the second post-war period. With the castle forms the core of the country.
Bobbio's symbol, beautiful at sunset.
The university museum of anatomy, reported by Visit Tuscany among the attractions of Pisa.
It starts from the top of the hill of Marturano, near the Castle Ruffo, and leads back to the marina and the port through countryside and greenery.
Collection of weapons and relics of the world wars and of the twentieth century, which can be visited free of charge during the morning guided tours of the Fortress.
The memories of Garibaldi.

One of the oldest theaters in Italy: a "Teatro della Comunità" is mentioned in the Austrian cadastre of 1750 and the origins are traced back to a painting by Ambrogio Viarana of 1614. Renovated in 1832-1838 by the architect Luigi Sottili with the consent of Maria Luigia, he has three orders of 18 poplar stages with paintings trompe-l'oeil and horseshoe platform; around 1930 Giuseppe Moscardini painted the ceiling with the Music and medallions of Donizetti, Rossini, Verdi and Giovanni Rinaldi, grandfather of Nino Rota. Restored after the 2012 earthquake.
The panoramic balcony on the Reggiano Apennines.

An example of the medieval low-plan military architecture, with corner towers and central mast of 1242; Reggiolo was a fortified outpost of the Municipality of Reggio from the 13th century and passed to Gonzaga in 1432. Damaged by the 2012 earthquake.

In the Palazzo Comunale, a permanent exhibition of 47 works, mainly of religious theme, by the painter Carlo Sismonda, whose style is inspired by the great artists between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, from impressionists to fauves. Freely accessible from Monday to Friday, 8:30-12:30 (better check opening before).
The art of the village.

A first fortress rose in 1113 at the behest of Beatrice di Canossa and a document by Matilde of 1114 quotes the castle; the present mast is of the second half of the thirteenth century, the ditches of 1437-38. The Estensi turned it into a noble residence (since 1638 Prince Louis d'Este lived there); the central crenellated tower, about 35 meters high, houses the municipal library and offers views of the village.
Church, convent and crypt fifteenth century.

System of caves and corridors discovered in 1898 and visited since the beginning of the twentieth century, with stalactites and millenarian stalagmites: the tourist route is spread over 3 km of galleries distributed over 4 overlapping floors, still inhabited by numerous bats. Constant temperature of about 9 °C; visits by reservation, inside the Mondolè Park with adventure park.

Two historic neighborhoods of villas: Vittoria Apuana, with elegant villas in large parks and views of the Apuan Alps, home to antique markets in winter; Rome Imperiale,  the green and tree-lined garden city, ideal for cycling.
An entire Roman city.
The Doria Palace with a Roman mosaic.
Ancient myths carved at the entrance of the old city.

Castle on a steep hill above Cavriglia, confirmed at the counts Guidi in 1191; in 1251, it was occupied by ghibellines and German knights and in 1252, after a winter siege, Florence took it and razed the walls to the ground. Today it is a small rural village with the church of San Silvestro, cited since 1299, with neoclassical nineteenth century facade and stretches of medieval walls incorporated in the back; wide view of Cavriglia and the valley.

The agricultural center of the inland Palermo welded to San Giuseppe Jato, at the foot of Mount Iato, where stood the ancient Iaitas: theatre, agora, Hellenistic houses and an antiquarium in Case D'Alia.
A Franciscan monastery dedicated to Campani inventors.
The CIMBRA house was the way it was.
Next to the imposing bell tower.
Reopening announced for 2026: check before visit

Massiccia porta turrita today used as a bell tower and clock tower: originally open towards the inside and without cover, with a bertesca, round arch, wounds for the boltoni of two drawbridges (carraio and pedestrian), hanging arches and ghibelline blackbirds with swallow tail. The twin tower-door, the ... torrion, was demolished in 1750 and gives the name to the street; visible from the road.
The origins of Bologna.
The church of Santa Maria dei Servi, born around 1250, with the chapel of San Pellegrino by Giuseppe Merenda and the painting by Simone Cantarini based on a design by Guido Reni.
Consecrated in 1723, it preserves a precious altarpiece.
Medieval alleys above the sea.
Wood of spruce and wolves.
Understand the mountain and its cave before going up there.

The estate was founded in 1855 as a private residence and transformed by the Pallavicino di Genova into a neoclassical villa; since 1952 the Marquise Luisa welcomed animals from all over the world. The park of about 20 hectares combines centuries-old trees and botanical garden with over 50 species of mammals and birds (dain, blade, Tibetan goats, zebras, kangaroos) and the Fattoria area; since 2017 it is part of the Borromeo Lands. Open every day from May to September, 9-18.

Just below the village of Stulles, presented as the third highest waterfall in Europe: a first jump of about 112 meters and then about 230 others. Good points of view are Breiteben, the road of the Passo del Rombo and the path of the gorge of the Passirio.

Built in 1633 on medieval structures and consecrated in 1652, on a project by Giovanni Battista Lantana, author in 1604 of the Duomo Nuovo di Brescia. Classic façade with four columns and tympanum, and statues of the saints holding in two niches. Inside the altarpiece of the Madonna with Child and saints of the Morettian school in a frame of Carlo Dossena, carvings of the Pialorsi called Boscaì di Levrange in the presbytery, altarpieces by Antonio Gandino and Francesco Paglia on the side altars and a sixteenth-century wooden crucifix by Maffeo Olivieri on the holy arch.
Walking along Via Tragara you arrive at the viewpoint from which you can see the Faraglioni, the symbol rocks of the island, admirable also from the sea with the boat tour.

Officially recognized as a shrine in October 2014, immediately after the canonization, it brings together the parish church, the Chapel of Peace (Maria Regina della Pace, with an altar coming from the ancient Basilica of St. Peter and a polychrome inlay of the pope), the Garden of Peace and the Crypt "Oboedientia et Pax" under the church, where a large shrine holds the cast of the pope's face and right hand, the one that signed the "Pacem in Terris" (Pacem in Terris) made by Giacomo Manzù. Open every day 8-12.30 and 14.30-18, Saturday and Sunday with continuous hours; the nearby Casa del Pellegrino offers welcome and guided tours for groups.
A day in the trees, even with the children.
The Baroque mother church that dominates the city.

A teaching ring of about 5 km that crosses Monterosso, named after the Sarvanot, a mythological little creature that traditionally lives in the woods of the village. Along the route about fifty signs with local stories and news about the trees, and wooden benches in the panoramic points.
The Roman city of Tabula alimentaria.
Villa of 1855 with garden at the foot of the castle, municipal since 1989; houses the museum with prints, maps, posters and Napoleonic vintage notices.
Where the "Cigno di Pesaro" was born.
A basilica above the catacombs.
Medieval bridge and springs of Belbo.
The golden ginkgo foliage in autumn.
The baroque portal on the square.
At sunset on the terraces.
The civil and religious heart of the village.

Founded in 1966 by the Archaeological Group "Cavriana" inaugurated in 1969 in the medieval tower next to the parish church and transferred in 1983 to Villa Mirra, it retraces about 7,000 years of history of the Upper Mantovano in eight rooms: four prehistoric, two Romanization, one for the most recent and the last periods, where Napoleon III stayed during the battle of Solferino, of Napoleonic history; among the finds, ancient enigmatic tablets. There are also a didactic module and Stables for exhibitions; audioguides in five languages. Open Tuesday-Friday 9-12, Saturday, Sunday and holidays 9-12 and 15-18.
The blade moved by the creek.
One of the most richly frescoed churches in Milan, the highest expression of Lombard painting of Leonardo school; it can be visited with the volunteers of the Touring Club.

A labyrinth of alleys and stairs: from Piazza Orticelli, going up Via Cerro, you will encounter the remains of the Tower and Castle, Piazza Lago, the Tower of Via Ripe, the Long Quarter with the Porta di Mezzo, the parish church of San Nicola and Piazza Roma with its stone staircase.
Water in the old town.
The village of tuff between the Middle Ages and the Renaissance.
View to the sea.
Terre di Pisa indicates it is closed at the same time.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Villabruna, opened in 1928 with the setting up of 1954 by Francesco Valcanover, preserves the mantle of Charles IV and paintings by Gentile Bellini, Quentin Metsys, Vittore Belliniano, Cima da Conegliano and Lorenzo Luzzo; it is in transformation into an archaeological civic museum.
Born from the free donation to the city of the personal collection of Professor Mario Morelli, who chose the birthplace of his master Aleandro Curatolo: paintings and valuable objects.
The Vignola Palace and the Visconti Citadel with the art gallery, the Tondo di Botticelli, the Etruscan Bronze Liver and the Museum of the Bodies.
The bathroom in the natural pool.
Church of the seventeenth century with frescoes by Borsetti and Peracino; on the Corso Matteotti rises the stone bell tower and lime with a massive profile.
The treasure of Lucera's cathedral.

Wanted by Maria Teresa of Austria and built between 1777 and 1780 by Giuseppe Piermarini as a summer residence for his son Ferdinando: plant in U, path of 28 rooms, the apartment of the Prince of Naples, the Royal Chapel, the Round of Appiani and the Teatrino of Corte.
The ruins of a medieval guest.

Country chapel near Borgo Soave, next to a river of resurgence, of ancient foundation. Inside frescoes of about 1430, largely attributed to Dux Aimo (Aimone Duce), commissioned by Giulio de Giuli; a paper of the apse vault dates back to 1474. Above the portal an Annunciation and outside a St. Christopher of the first half of the sixteenth century. Around the Naturalistic Wood of Mission, with picnic tables.
The hunting traditions of Val Vibrata.
Borgo del Casentino dominated by the Count Guidi, where Dante found refuge during the exile.
The tombs of the sailors of the Roman fleet of Miseno.
One of the best preserved medieval villages in the Euganean Hills.
the source does not indicate timetables or how to visit (open for Spring Days 2018 FAI)
The hill symbol of Rome.
A treasure dug into the rock.
Alpeggio with the chapel of Notre-Dame-des-Neiges at 1680 meters and the refuge suitable for star observation; more on the hill with 360° panorama.
The Bourbon bridge dedicated to the queen.
The castle of Paolo and Francesca.
The female Benedictine monastery still inhabited by nuns, in the southern part of the city near the walls.
The castle that dominates the valley.

Solid 15th-century cadorian building, opened as a house-museum in 1932; the restoration of 1928-30 removed an 18th-century addition and brought back to light original doors and windows. On the ground floor reproductions of drawings by Tiziano degli Uffizi and documents on the painter, on the upper floor five rooms where probably spent his childhood; the Magnificent Community signals you exposed the Pala di San Tiziano, painted by Tiziano and workshop in the sixties of the sixteenth century for the altar of the Vecellio.

Scientific dissemination center opened in 2007 on the hill of Pino Torinese, next to the Astronomical Observatory. The four-storey interactive museum makes us experiment with the laws of the cosmos (simulated gravity, speed of light, gravitational vortices, great structures of the universe) and retraces the history of space exploration; the digital planetarium, in a sphere that evokes a red supergiant star, offers projections for all ages, with workshops, conferences and telescope observation evenings. Free with Museums and Torino+Piemonte Card subscription; online purchase recommended.
Milan capital of the empire.

In the eighteenth century Palazzo Stabile, in the cultural complex next to the Basilica, exhibits liturgical furnishings of very high crafts (calici, ostensori, reliquari, piviali, dalmatici, pianete), liturgical books and Gregorian chant on parchments and documents of about five centuries of history of Martina and his Collegiate. Guided tours and café.
MiC card indicates closed every day and the church is in MiC database of abandoned cultural assets with mediocre conservation status
In the building that after September 8, 1943 was headquarters of the SS of Kappler, with the cells and graffiti of the prisoners of the Roman Resistance, many then killed at the Fosse Ardeatine.
Liqueurs and culatello in the cellars of the fortress.
A tomb of giants saved from the freeway.

Late antique site with the remains of a mansio, imperial stopover station with change of horses, amphora bubbles of the Praedia Galbana and a recently excavated thermal complex with calidarium, tepidarium and suspensurae.

Founded by the Orsini and already habitable at the beginning of the fourteenth century; the windows of the first floor with polygonal columns are of the second half of the fifteenth century, under Count Roberto Orsini, and the Colonna then replaced the Orsini coats of arms with their own. The cap contains late-Gothic frescoes with stories of Christ.
The village on stilts is a patrimony of humanity.
The popular music of the Aniene Valley.
The Festival Theatre.
The comic book building.

In the Villa Patt renovated by the Province, the route follows for almost a century and a half the history of the 7th Alps, since its foundation in 1887, with photographs, documents, weapons and finds from the former Museum-Sacrario of the barracks Tommaso Salsa di Belluno: 160 weapons, 148 relics, 271 documents and 33 private donations.
The ancient Nepi.
The great design museum dedicated to the collection of the Compasso d'Oro, with spaces for workshops and events of the design community.
The painted ceiling and the portal of 1307.
Town shrine with a bell tower that houses 55 bells.
The wool that made rich Arpino.
A church born of a discovery.

The castle on the gulf and the art of interweaving.
The sea is just a stone's throw from the center.
Cycling a campaign designed 2,000 years ago.
The figure of D'Andrade, restorer of the Piedmontese Middle Ages.
On the hill of Castagnola, in the middle of a large park, it borders to the south with the ancient Romanesque church of San Remigio.
Walk through the remains of the Greek colony of Naxos.
The Himalayas in the heart of the Amiata.
The church is marked in the official map of the historic centre, in the district between the Duomo and the Palazzo dei Musei.
The Provincial Museum houses the archaeological finds of the history of the city; it is also located in the Bourbon Prison, wanted by Ferdinando I and designed in 1826 by engineer Giuliano De Fazio.

The eighteenth-century monastery, designed by Andrea Vici, has the appearance of a fortified structure; in the adjoining rooms the Museum of Liberation of Ancona collects photographic material on the passage of the allied front in the Marches and on the battles of the Second World War for the liberation of Ancona.

13th century chapel (built around 1200) in the cathedral churchyard, which houses the Venzone mummies, dated between 1348 and 1881. From the tombs of the cathedral were extracted about forty, starting from the mummy of the hunchback found in 1647; the natural mummification is attributed to a mold, Hypha bombicina Pers., which dehydrates the tissues.
Birdwatching on the reed of Cherio along the bike path.
Neapolitan Baroque on the temple of Saturn.
A public and open Renaissance garden.

The village, rebuilt by the Longobards in the 8th century on the ruins of Pollitium, preserves small noble palaces of the 18th to the 19th century in the stone of Manoppello and the castle donated in 874 by the emperor Ludovico II to the abbey of San Clemente in Casauria. To see the church of San Nicola (XIV century) with its portal, the SS. Annunziata beside the former convent of the Clarisse and San Pancrazio.
National monument since 1901.
The art of the twentieth century and today.

In Asten, on the steep slopes below the Nid-Schupfen, lead and fluorite were extracted until 1890 and remains a tunnel under the Sulzspitze; on the Toten (Silberberg) were excavated galena, blenda and pyrite especially in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, with activity attested by an act of donation of 1140, and the entrance of the Johanni gallery is well preserved.
Baronial palace and ruins of Castellaccio.
The bell tower of the cathedral, symbol of the city, with the museum dedicated to the measure of time and the view over all Cremona.
A tower of the walls that was jailed.
On the top of the hill, it was started in 1686 by the Spanish viceroy of Naples and the troops engaged in the fight against the brigandage were lodged there.
To get to know plants and animals of the Apennines before a hike.
One of the few Roman towers left in northern Italy, frescoed by nuns and UNESCO heritage.
The Austro-Hungarian military cemetery, opened in 1915 and then dismantled, is today the Park of Peace, memorial of all wars; in the wall remains the statue of the Kaiserschütze that guarded it.

In the upper part of the village (Cotronianu and susu), the parish church of São Paulo dates back to the 12th century and houses paintings from the 17th century; around it the historical centre developed between the 17th and 18th centuries.
The Lapidary Museum and the Duomo Museum with original metopes, codes and treasures of the cathedral.
The neoclassicism of a painter from Terlizzo.
Testimony of the Jewish community of Sabbioneta.

Museum dedicated to the memory of the peasant civilization, in particular that sharecropping linked to the farm system of Tuscan farms, with educational activities for schools and research on the peasant world between the nineteenth and twentieth centuries.
Climb into the city's symbolic towers.
One of the most beautiful and intact villages of the Langhe, surrounded by the hills of great wines.
Evening chirps.
39 meters high, built in the 12th century in Lombard Romanesque style next to the cathedral.

A hilly country between the middle Tiber valley and Orvieto, known for its three small active volcanoes 265,000 years ago and for its Venanzite, a rare rock that bears its name: in the center the Park and volcanological museum, Villa Faina with its public park and medieval tower; around Mount Peglia, UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, with the Park of the Seven Friars and the Etruscan excavation of Poggio delle Civitelle.
A medieval stone village-refuge.
About 4 km from the center on the road to Bevagna, built in 1926 in the place linked to the Preaching to the birds; from the seventeenth century comes a procession from the center of the village.
Six centuries of childhood.

An interpretation centre of the Ecomuseum of Stone in the former complex of the Salesian College: it documents the material and immaterial heritage linked to the stone of the Solano Valley, with sections on stone in the landscape, medieval architecture, legends and tradition of stonemasons of Strada in Casentino, and offers thematic routes in the territory. Every two years, in the first days of September, the town hosts the Pietra Lavorata exhibition with stonemasons and sculptors from all over Italy.
Romanesque masterpiece of the 13th century where the municipal assemblies of three hundred members were gathered, with the monumental 16th century loggia on the ground floor.
The 18th century organ of the Vici.
The village of one street.

On the side of the castle there are about fifty artificial caves, carved by hand, connected by stairs and narrow streets in the rock: each was a small house of one or two rooms. It's an open-air ethnographic museum.
In Piazza IV Novembre, with stuccoes and baroque altars and an eighteenth-century painting of the Annunciation.
15th century frescoes above the roofs.
The ancient village on the hill.
The Etruscan necropolis overlooking the village.
The mills of the green basin.

Memorial church built between secular olive trees next to the southern entrance of the cave, after the demolition of the chapel of Byzantine origin that stood inside, eliminated to make room for the road. In Ferragosto there is celebrated the feast of St. John with folk bands and launeddas players.
The most spectacular canyon of the Beigua Geopark.

Church documented since 1339, with the current structure due to the restorations of the architect Giovan Battista Vergani in 1829 and 1831; the facade, with large arches, is from 1921 in hammered concrete. The interior has three naves, coffered ceilings and transept; its bell tower faces the town hall tower.
One of the four palatine basilicas of Puglia is the heart of the historic centre and is located on the same square as Palazzo De Mari.

Borgo della val Neva founded in 1248 by the Marquises of Clavesana, all along a single porticoed road between two gates, with the castle, the Romanesque bridge and the route of the Roso towards Castelvecchio.
Built in Romanesque forms between the 13th and 14th centuries.
Egyptian artifacts in the Marches.
The prehistory of the Verona plain in a church of the sixteenth century.
The 15th century wooden Madonna of the village.

The path connects the entrance of the Val Zemola, to Erto, with the village of Casso, along the path where once the vegetable coal of the valley woods was carried on shoulder; it crosses the village of San Martino and tells local legends like that of the castle of Queen Claudia. From Erto also start the spectacular itineraries of the Val Zemola.
13th century sources under the loggia of the Palazzo dei Marquisi.
Statue of Guido Galletti laid in 1954 on the bottom of the bay of San Fruttuoso.
The medieval palace overlooking Piazza del Popolo.

Founded in 1834, it has more than 460 paintings from the 14th to the 19th century, sculptures, fabrics, jewels, coins and the treasure of the Cathedral; since 1952 it has been located in the former episcopio next to the Duomo.
The life of the Roman legionnaire a stone's throw from the camp.
The UNESCO monument of the Longobards.

Downtown of the lower Sand Valley crossed by the river Churches and the Canal Naviglio, with districts arranged in a ring between the hills; to see the Civic Archaeological Museum of the Sand Valley in the historic center, the seventeenth-century convent of the Orsoline, the "isolo" on the river and the medieval hamlet of Sopraponte.
Trails between the dune and the lagoon.

The spa Liberty of the Belle Époque, extensively renovated, reopened in December 2014: frescoes, columns and ceilings from the early twentieth century coexist with contemporary design installations. Over 6,000 m2 indoors and 3,200 m2 outdoors in the Fountain Park offer over 30 routes, panoramic and sensory pools, waterfalls, saunas, Turkish baths, salt and ice rooms and a hydrotherapy area with inhalations, mud and balneotherapy. Each evening the "Aperiterme" is by the pool.
The village and the memory of Blessed Pierina.
The fourteenth-century walled village and the viewpoint.

Patron parish church, perhaps from the sixteenth century: a plaque on the portal bore the date 1533, probable restoration or extension, destroyed by the earthquake of 1805; restored until at least 1822, rebuilt in the roof after the collapse of 1874. Facade with a hut with bell tower on the left, a single nave of 30 m with four marble altars; it is located next to the former ducal palace, today of the family Venditti.
The museum of peasant civilization with the stone mill.
The marble gorge.
A panoramic hike.

The municipality of the Potentino, perhaps of Sannita foundation, prosperous between the Middle Ages and the modern age as shown by the noble palaces of the historic center; in the hamlet of Lagopesole stands the castle of Federico II, which houses the Museum of Lucana emigration.
Built between 1674 and 1678 to guard a tile with the image of Our Lady with Child.

Among the historic residences of Lazio, built around 1880 near the station and purchased in 1902 by the painter Alessandro Morani and his wife Lili Helbig; from the window of the studio you can see the landscape that the artist painted. He hosted D'Annunzio, Pascarella and the artists of "In Arte Libertas" .
The ancient heart of the city.

The oldest church in the city, begun in 1726; in 1787 received an organ by Gaetano Callido and conserves a baptismal font in marble of the eighteenth century, a wooden statue of the patron saint of the seventeenth century and frescoes of the ceiling dated 1829. Next to it stands Villa Contarini-Carrer, the oldest villa in Porto Viro, built in the seventeenth century by the Venetian Contarini family.
To get to know the Arbëreshe culture of Caraffa.
Porticos and courtyards to discover on foot.
From the sea to the woods.

Started in 1570 by the Obizzi as the seat of representation, it was enlarged in the nineteenth century for the court extended in exile and became hunting residence of the Habsburgs; on the noble floor the forty squares frescoed by Giovanni Battista Zelotti with the history of the family. Park with free deer, gardens with fountains and fish ponds and panoramic terrace on the hills.

One of the city's symbols. It is linked to the miracle of 17 April 1555: according to tradition the Child Jesus painted by Gregory Zavattari on the façade of the little church of St. Nicholas detached himself from the fresco to play with three children, one of which, deaf to death from birth, would recover hearing and speech. It is remembered by the Feast of Forgiveness, from Thursday after Easter to Sunday, with processions at the Madonna del Santuario and popular celebrations.
The ROF house.
The bridge, built in 1685 and decorated with marbles in 1762, is guarded by two lions in stone of Istria; in the nearby square the column Vigo is surmounted by a lion nicknamed "el gatòn" .
Iron and glass on the course.

The seventeenth-century cathedral is embedded in the clock tower, wanted by the Knights Gerosolimitani: it preserves the great canvas of the Last Judgment (1629) by Giuseppe Salerno, the Zoppo di Gangi, inspired by the Judgment of Michelangelo in the Sistine.

In Palazzo Rogati, the artistic nativity scene created in 1961 by the patron Luigi Rogati and the work of Juan Marì Oliva from Barcelona with Angelo Stefanucci from Rome: Palestinian and Eastern setting with camels, dancers, shepherds and stage scenes, and four figures with the faces of the Rogati family. In the other halls a collection of fossils of the Cretaceous (between 135 and 63 million years ago), with the rudist, mollusk with a coral-like appearance up to almost a metre long, photographs and local memories, an anthropological section and a wing on the zampogne.

Appiano is the largest wine-growing municipality in South Tyrol, with 941 hectares of vineyards and about 300 days of sunshine a year, along the South Tyrolean Wine Road; in autumn the tradition of Törggelen is renewed and every year Spatium Pinot Blanc is held, dedicated to the European white Pinot.

Isolated on the left bank of the Arroscia, with the portico frescoed in 1488 (Passion, Scenes of St. Pantaleo, Resurrection of Lazarus) and inside the Blesseds, Hell, the Riding of the Vizi, a great Saint Christopher and the Months of the early sixteenth century.
Four rings in the woods above Lake Orta.

Built around 1171 by Umberto III of Savoia, destroyed in the 13th century and rebuilt, then enlarged in the mid-sixteenth century; since 1599 it belongs to the Provanas, to which Charles Emanuel I granted the feud and the comital title of Collegno. The architecture is attributed to Filippo Juvarra, the current facade is by Giuseppe Talucchi. The park opens to the public during the patron saint of San Lorenzo.
In a wing of the Palazzo Monte dei Pegni, next to the Bellini Museum: wooden statues, paintings of saints, objects and sacred vestments, with works by Moretto.

Park established in 1999, over 1,600 hectares of ponds with different salinity (Bellarosa Minore and Perdalonga of fresh water, Bellarosa Maggiore and the pond of Quartu first basins of the former state salt pans), with pink flamingos, swamp falcons, garzettes, avocette and sultan chicken; you visit on foot, by bike or with guided birdwatching trails, better in spring and autumn.
Almost three thousand meters of Dolomite panorama in a few minutes.
The city of the philosophers from the Pink Gate to the acropolis on the sea.

Medieval village of the high valley of Sagittario, 604 meters away, with the ruins of the Norman castle where d'Annunzio set the torch under the moggio, the churches of San Marcello and Madonna delle Grazie and the Gole del Sagittario; in the hamlet of Castrovalva the panorama that inspired a lithography of Escher.
The story of a post-unitarian minister of Italy born in Soresina.

The ancient heart of the village, formed by seven Saracen alleys similar to a casbah around the fortress of Zabut, with Navarro Square, the purres (ancient tuff quarries), Palazzo Amodei, the Rosary church with courtyard of 1752 and, at the top of the hill, the Matrix Church, closed to worship since 1968 after the earthquake of Belice.
The marble Madonna of John of Augustine.
The parish church sang by Carducci.
The plateau of Pian dell'Elmo, about 1,000 meters between the beech woods, under the summit of San Vicino (about 1,479 m), with views, paths and great variety of species.
The territory around the village offers woods and paths that can be walked in every season on foot or by bike, with views of the Montago and Matese.

Built in 1500 and surrounded by secular oaks, it includes a restored church and convent, now a period residence; in the church a altarpiece by Bernardino da Longiano and in the refectory a fresco of the Last Supper.
Built between 1599 and 1618 for the Dominicans, with works by Fiammenghino and Julius Caesar Procaccini and the facade with four statues by Giuseppe Argenti.

The lower part of the village, partly depopulated, preserves the church of Santa Maria delle Grazie with an 18th century Baroque altar, the Clock Tower and the Mercante House decorated with carved stones.
Abbey of the IX-X century, outside the historic center, with crypt; it was run by the Benedictines until the end of the fourteenth century.
Borgo della Gherardesca on the hill, linked to the poet Carducci, with the Viale dei Cipressi that leads to Bolgheri among the vineyards of Sassicaia.
The port penetrates into the heart of the city, with buildings overlooking the docks since the Middle Ages and alleys that go up towards the cathedral.
Oasis managed by the WWF that extends over about 440 hectares in the municipal territory, towards Capo Saragnano.

On the former promontory called Lakinion Akron, overlooking the Marine Protected Area of Capo Rizzuto: the shrine of Hera Lacinia, linked to the Greek colony of Kroton, of which only one column of the great Doric temple remains on the edge of the cliff; next to a more ancient place of worship, a building for banquets, a Roman-age settlement and baronial villas of the eighteenth century.
The paths of the Paradise Gulf.
View of the peninsula.

It is reached from Piano San Michele, site of an ancient church destroyed before the earthquake of 1910, climbing the staircase next to Palazzo Mirelli; the premises of the village, built on the castle collapsed in 1694, have been restored by the Superintendence of Salerno and Avellino.
The Basilica of Tresoldi next to the Romanesque of Siponto.

Considered the most important Romanesque monument of Piedmont, it has been documented since 1095 (the foundation by Charlemagne in 773 is only legend) and combines Romanesque and Gothic forms. The façade alternates bricks and sandstone bands with statues of the archangels Michael and Raphael and of Christ; inside the pier of the late 12th century brings the bas-reliefs of the 35 patriarchs and stories of Mary. The cloister, one of the best preserved in Piedmont, has frescoes from the 13th and 15th centuries; since 2015 the complex has been entrusted to the Museum Pole of Piedmont.
Museum dedicated to the landing of allied troops on the Salento coast during the Second World War.

Castle on an islet at the mouth of the Astura, connected to the mainland by an arched bridge: it was built by the Frangipane in 1193 on the Roman remains, including a fish pond that emerges with water and luxury villas; in 1268 Corradino di Svevia was sheltered. It is often film set (The Adventures of Pinocchio).

Opened in 1996 in Palazzo Vinciprova in Pioppi, it houses about one hundred marine species in tanks distributed in three rooms that recreate coastal habitats of Cilento, with a tactile tub; on the upper floor the Museum of the Mediterranean Diet dedicated to Ancel Keys, with its library. Since 2013 it is managed by Legambiente with the Mare Nostrum Association and the Municipality.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione 1200 metres in the Valle di Viù, on the border with France, among Romanesque testimonies, alpine lakes and the tome of Lanzo.
Temporarily closed for earthquake damage 2016
The historic wineries of Marsala in the center, including Florio, Rallo, Donnafugata and Pellegrino.
€5, 14-18 years old €2, free under 14

Born from a group of scholars of the Cultural Research Centre of Lusevera and reopened in the former dairy factory after the long closure due to the earthquake of 1976, it was re-arranged with experts of the Gorordning Muzej of Nova Gorica: three rooms with domestic tools, tools of craftsmen and peasants and tools for the dairy and dairy production, almost all donated by private individuals of the upper Torre Valley.

Museum in three sections: the mill, with three millstones and the machinery to produce flour; the ethnographic section, with the reconstruction of the shoemaker's workshop and the old crafts; a section of natural sciences. Open only by reservation, to be sent at least 15 days before (tel. +39 0171 767108).
The best preserved fortified village of Valdambra.
The church for which Raphael painted Our Lady Sistine, today in Dresden, rich in frescoes and 18th century decorations.

Already a Benedictine monastery, with the vault frescoed in the sixteenth century by Orazio Sammachini and a cloister of Bramante's forms; the Lauretano Museum preserves the act of birth of Claudio Monteverdi.
The starting point for all Pavesian places.

Cathedral Basilica founded in 1094 by the Grand Count Ruggero I d'Altavilla, next to the bishop's palace: it houses the sarcophagus of Queen Adelasia, wife of the Count, and a Adoration of the shepherds attributed to William Borremans; the façade has lava stone and white marble decorations and a portal in Arab-Norman style.
On a rocky step just below the castle.
An intact vasarian cycle in the heart of Molise.
The oldest church of Giulianova, dating back to the 12th century, with terracotta façade and a portal of the 14th century with eighteen engraved tiles.

Sanctuary on the hill north of Luzzogno, reached with a short climb on a cobbled road; the small churchyard is a viewpoint on the village and the Alps. Every three years, in September, it hosts a party with torchlight from the village and bonfire.

The village preserves short streets and medieval steps that go down to the provincial. The Palazzo Pelliccioni-Marazzini, known for its arched terraces, houses the municipal library and houses finds from the Bronze Age attributed to the Ligurians of the upper Serchio valley, with Roman and medieval relics.
The picturesque alley parallel to the promenade and the promenade along the beach, indicated for sunset.
Stressful tower and Pallavicino residence in the green on the Oglio.

The oldest museum in the world dedicated to Egypt, founded in 1824 by the union of the collections of Drovetti and Carlo Felice: more than 30,000 finds among statues of pharaohs, sarcophagi, papyri and mummies, renovated in 2015.
The wooden choir carved in the eighteenth century.

The city of Teodolinda and Corona Ferrea, with the Duomo and its Treasure, the Medieval Arengario, the Royal Villa of Piermarini and one of the largest enclosed parks in Europe, which houses the National Racecourse.
A medieval village of Fermano.
