Since 1956 in Palazzo Barberini, built on the cavea of the sanctuary: on the ground floor the cryptoporic with sculptures and inscriptions, on the first floor the materials of the cult of Fortuna (the colossal statue of Iside-Fortuna, the relief Grimani of Augustan age), the second mirrors and bronze cysts and votive terracotta, at the last the great Mosaic of the polychrome Nile, view of an Egyptian landscape during the flood, among the major Hellenistic mosaics preserved. At the entrance, a 1:50 scale of the shrine. Touring hours: every day 9-20.
Fortress of the city indicated by the Region among the monuments.
€6 full, €5 reduced, €2 from 18 to 25 years; free on the first Sunday of the month
A place linked to the history of the Republic of Salò.
Dedicated to St. Nicholas, patron saint of the city, it dominates the historic centre; inside frescoes, sculptures and works of sacred art, and hosts religious ceremonies and cultural events.

The complex of 26 buildings and 17 villas designed by Gino Coppedè between 1915 and 1927, with Piazza Mincio, the Fountain of the Frogs, the Palazzo del Ragno and the Villino delle Fate, set by Dario Argento.
The Civil Cerreto of the early eighteenth century.

City of art on the northern edge of the Tavoliere, several times the capital of the Capitanatata and rebuilt in Baroque forms after the earthquake of 1627: the historic center with the cathedral and churches of the seventeenth century, the Teatro Verdi and the MAT - Museum of the High Tablekeeper in the ancient convent of San Francesco.

Benedictine abbey complex of municipal property, at the entrance of the village at the foot of the Fortress, where stood the Roman settlement of Forum Vibii Caburrum. Restored in 1037 at the behest of the bishop of Turin Landolfo, it was destroyed in 1592 by the French troops of Lesdiguières and rebuilt in Baroque forms in the eighteenth century, smaller than the original; the early Christian crypt, with vault on Lombard columns of recovery, preserves the altar considered the oldest of Piedmont. The building of the vats, where the grapes of the monks were worked, is now an exhibition hall. Open Saturday 15-19 and Sunday 10-19, week by reservation.
Seven hundred objects to understand life in the mountains.
The panoramic ruins of the castle above the village.

Main square of the village, closed on two sides by large porticos, with the Town Hall and the church. In the center is the statue of Hercules Benefactor carved by Jacopo Sansovino in honour of Hercules II d'Este, finished in 1553 and here since 1727; on the sides are the bronze statues of Don Camillo and Peppone of the sculptor Andrea Zangani, for the 50th anniversary of the first film.

In the ancient bishopric residences of the Episcopio, next to cathedral and baptistery, sixteen rooms of paintings, sculptures, furnishings and sacred vestments that tell the story of the Christian community osimana. Entire 3 €, reduced 2 €.
The largest covered food market in Italy, in the district of San Benedetto: fresh fish, meat, cheese, cakes, fresh pasta, fruit and vegetables.
Liberty on the lake.
The capital of the watermark.
15th century church that houses a polyptych by Agostino Casanova from 1547. St. John the Baptist is the patron saint of the municipality, celebrated on 24 June.
A Renaissance building born of a fortress.
outside the period April-October only by appointment; the MiC card (updated to December 2020) reports "closed" in every day
15th-century residence of Blessed Osanna, the city's companion.

Fortified village on the Trebbia at the foot of the first Piacenza hills covered with vineyards, gathered around the castle, closed to traffic and paved in pebbles, with parking for cars and buses nearby. With Statto, Montechiaro and Rivergaro, it controlled the access to the Val Trebbia along the Caminus Ianuae, the road to Genoa and the sea; the Trebbia cycle path connects it to Piacenza.
A fifteenth-century Pietà in the sanctuary of Cantogno.
The highest point of the Irpinia roof.
Maiolica on the altar.
It occupies about 1,000 m2 in the lower Anglona, just over a kilometer east of Martis: fossilized and siliconized tree trunks, linked to volcanic activities of about twenty million years ago.
Moscato told in the castle that dominates the Langhe.

Along the Marmolaio torrent, between Castellina Marittima and Santa Luce, it is the only alabaster tunnel quarry in the area of Scaglione (locally known as "venella") still existing, one of the best qualities of alabaster.
Outdoor art.
The noble house of the village, home to the Cultural Center that collects evidence of the ancient productive activities and the history of the Fieschi family.
A little-known collection.
Under the College Palace, the remains of four churches from the 8th to the 17th century of the Benedictine monastery, the Romanesque crypt and medieval capitals and sculptures.
The Lincei Palace where Galileo stayed.
The house of a rich merchant family of the fourteenth century, with frescoed rooms and period furnishings.
The streets of the mint of a Pope's fief.

Borgo dell'Alta Valle Arroscia in the Regional Natural Park of the Ligurian Alps, with medieval structure of winding and archivolti streets: the inhabitants have transformed it into an open-air museum, and in the former town hall is the museum of medicinal herbs

On the outer wall of the Mother Church, in Via Alfieri, the mosaic of the spouses Michele and Angiolina Sposito of Ferrara tells the history of Calabria from the graffito of the  "Toro di Papasidero" to the society of farmers and fishermen; in October 1999 there was added a panel with the "Immaculate."

34-metre tower on Piazza III Novembre, documented in the thirteenth century to guard and defend the city; on top the golden angel-signavento "Anzolim de la Tor" is one of the symbols of Riva. 165 steps up to the panoramic terrace on the center and lake; free under 15 years.
The consular road told where it ends.
A church with a troubled history.
Next to the Ducal Palace.
Location of the circuit of the Museo delle Storie in Bergamo, which houses the Museo della Fotografia Sestini and the section dedicated to the twentieth century.
Three thousand years of Verona plain in three rooms, with free entrance.
The memory of a medieval monastery.
The ruins of the monastery of Santa Maria Alborense in the woods of Uccellina, documented by the Middle Ages and recently restored; it is reached with a walking itinerary of about 8 or 17 km.
The golden façade and the frescoes of Signorelli.

Protected coast to walk only, with five marked trails, coves like Cala Tonnarella, Cala dell'Uzzo, Cala Marinella, Cala Beretta, Cala Disa, Cala Capreria and Cala del Varo, and five museums on traditional activities such as tuna fishing and interweaving. It has two entrances, north from San Vito and south from Scopello; there are no refreshment points.

In the Renaissance palace of the second half of the fifteenth century, opened in 1981: about 130 works by Alberto Burri from 1948 to 1989 in twenty halls, from tars and sacks of the fifties to wood, irons, plastics and large cellotex.
The first WWF oasis in Italy, with trails, educational lakes for flora and fauna, observation points and picnic areas.
Two thousand years of Brianza's history told with award-winning multimedia equipment.
It exhibits finds from various archaeological sites around the village and allows to rebuild life in Etruscan and Roman times.

Seaside town north of Bari, with the ancient centre on a promontory surrounded by walls of the fifteenth century, dominated by the Romanesque Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, and the large square Vittorio Emanuele II with the Triton Fountain. In the hinterland, about 6 km, the Dolmen of San Silvestro testifies to the human presence since the bronze age.
Skating where the 1956 Olympics were held.

One of the largest state forests in Sardinia, about 4,600 hectares in the heart of the park of Monte Linas, Oridda and Marganai, populated by Sardinian deer and mouflon; it is reached along the lake of Leni and the pine forest equipped with Campus de Monti. The CAI trails start from the former Canale Serci mine (cassiterite, 1866-1946) and the Cantina Ferraris refuge: 113 leads to Piscina Irgas, 109 to the Muru Mannu waterfall, over 70 metres.

Church of the historic center with the glazed altar of the Annunciation realized in the twenties of the sixteenth century by Mattia Della Robbia; the hermits of San Girolamo built a furnace in the hermitage to cook the terracotta.
The lighthouse on the archaic stones.
The medieval old town, largely preserved intact, stands on a cliff of leukic lava at the bottom of a small gulf, secondary crater of an ancient volcano.
The church that opens the bridge on the Aso.
After the earthquake of 2016 Let's Marche indicates the museums of the Municipality partially usable
Open lawns for an open day.
The rooms where the young Raphael grew.
The monument near the port, one of the symbols of the city.

In the homonymous hamlet, rebuilt in 1539, restored in 1633 and modernized in 1875, then consolidated after the 1980 earthquake. Baroque church with a single nave: the stucco vault has three paintings by Angelo Solimena from 1654, and on the main altar there is the Martyrdom of Sant'Andrea attributed to Francesco Guarini (1642), with other paintings in the nave.
The houses of the Romans of Caralis.

A symbolic fortress of the Valbelluna, linked according to the legend to the Gothic Gothic (VI century) and his twin sons, from which the name "castrum zumellarum" reached the maximum extent in the 12th century, was destroyed in 1196 and rebuilt by Rizzardo da Camino in 1311. The ecomuseum of about 15 hectares includes the castle, the medieval walls, a 36-metre tower, the church of San Lorenzo and a forest botanical garden, with guided tours and a tavern.
The paintings from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century of the collection of Giuseppe Stuard and the Congregation of San Filippo Neri, with the artistic heritage of the Municipality.
Brick pillar of 1375 that marked the medieval border between the territories of Padua and Venice.
Woods and fossil caves above the country.
A 16th century fresco in a Romanesque church.
The landscape of the orange trees at the foot of Montiferru.
Small church in an elevated position north of the historic centre, reached by a staircase adorned with flowers, with views of the lake and the village.
It preserves the equestrian statue of San Giorgio of 1596 of the Lo Cascio brothers; the original orientation of the church was rotated 180 degrees.

Born from the donation to the Municipality of the collection of Oreste Coni, it is located in the cultural center under the porch Gonzaghesco, next to the Giacometti Theatre and the library. Cameras and cameras draw an overview from the 1920s to today: the first section follows with captions the origins of photography and cinema, the second collects projectors and a laboratory that introduces to audiovisual, photographic, direction and assembly techniques. Open Monday, Wednesday and Friday 15.30-18.30 and Saturday 16-18; guided tours by reservation (tel. 0376 924030).
Sculpted stone and baroque painting.
A walk in the historic woods.
The white maze that made Ostuni famous.
Sculpture in porphyry 4.50 meters high by the artist Mario Ricci, inaugurated in 1991, a few steps from the Town Hall.
The castle of bishops.

Filatoio built in 1820 and later became the College of St. Joseph; the Municipality indicates it as a remarkable nineteenth century example of industrial archaeology linked to the woolly tradition of Follina.
Built in the seventeenth century just outside Pieve Torina on a plot belonging to the Lateran Basilica; sober façade with arched portal and Lateran coats of arms, roof with hut in pairs.
Refurbished in the fifteenth century by Luca Fancelli, with the thirteenth-century statue of Virgilio in a chair on the façade.
The epigraphs of the capital of Italics.
Bring them in granite and noble coats of arms.
The octagonal Romanesque tower of Oriago.
The Clock Tower is the gateway to the medieval part of the village, with preserved sections of walls and houses placed on each other on the tuff cliff.
The only island on the lake, among Romanesque ruins.

On Mount Miglio there is a Sannitic fortification with three walls of polygonal walls, the Cyclopic walls testifying to the presence of the Sannites, reachable with marked paths of different difficulty, duration and starting point.

Church of Gothic origin remodelled in the seventeenth century: the coffered ceiling of 1604 is the work of the Florentine Giovanni Balducci and in the chapel of the transept there is the altarpiece "Christ tempted by Satan" by Mattia Preti.

Angevin fortress with circular bastions, almost entirely surrounded by the sea, the fulcrum of the twelve towers and bastions that surrounded the island; in 1269 34 rebel barons resisted against Charles I of Anjou for seven months.
The Baroque parish church of the village.
Five villages downhill.

Four ring paths starting from the centre of the village, each marked by a color and a theme, which can be walked, by mountain bike or on horseback with different levels of difficulty; cross the woods and the protected area of Mount Mesma. The Indaco Ring hosts an educational WWF tour of local flora and fauna.

Small mountain municipality of the Val Sangone, autonomous since 1272: the paths from the villages go up to the Colle Braida with a view of the lower Valley of Susa, the Lakes of Avigliana and the Sacred of San Michele, touching the 'pietrefitte' of the Colle di Castiglione.
Built in the 17th century and renovated in the 18th century, it is preceded by a staircase with balustrade and has a tympanum portal dated 1724.

The San Daniele ham, known all over the world, matures thanks to the microclimate of the hills, where the humid winds of the Tagliamento meet with the air of the mountains; it is tasted in the ham shops of the city.
The historic core of the city, where you can find the birthplace of D'Annunzio and the Museum of the Genti d'Abruzzo.

Heart of the city, with the cathedral, Renaissance buildings and shop houses; the southern porch is 1474. On the side of the Palazzo Pretorio a municipal palace is already attested in 1211; Torrazzo, Palazzo Comunale and Palazzo Pretorio were rebuilt between 1525 and 1555, while the Palazzo della Notaria (1548-49) was donated to the future diocese as a bishop's residence.
A journey in the eighteenth century, defined by Giacomo Leopardi     Â a small Versailles Â .
A tower that tells the ancient history of the country.
In the Castle of Marano, it preserves numerous prehistoric, picena and roman artefacts from the territory.
Memories of the Orsini in the oldest church.
The village reborn after the earthquake.
Since September 30, 2025 partially closed for works; the Antiquarium remains open

The fish pond that collects the waters of the Fiora and the small church of Pescina with frescoes by Francesco Nasini and the glass floor under which flows the spring; near the gallery of the springs.

A very characteristic thirteenth-century village, with the gate of the ancient ricepto dated 1210 and the remains of the walls: in Via Flecchia, the ancient main street, the surviving tower of curtain is an apse to the chapel of the Confraternita dei Disciplinati, near to parts of the crenellated walls; the moat was fed by the sources of the Serra. The tower of San Giacomo, circular with swallow-tailed blackbirds, is in a private garden.

The facades of the village are decorated with the murals of the painter Liliana Cano, dedicated to local life and to Renaissance subjects. In July the event sa domu de perda is dedicated to paintings.
The swords that made Gromo's fame.

Small museum with numerous Roman finds emerged from the excavations of the Roman archaeological area of the municipal territory, housed in the building built in 1927 that also houses the Anselmi Theatre and the library.

In a building of the middle seventeenth century run by the Park, tells the Escartons, an autonomous federation that from 1343 to 1713 managed administrative and fiscal affairs: it houses a wardrobe of the sculptor Guido Ronchail with seven keys, symbol of the agreement between the communities, the archive of Remigio Bermond and a library of about 3,000 volumes. Open by reservation.

Medieval village on the Tiber Valley, dominated by the Ducal Palace of Mattei with its 365 windows; in the center the chapel of San Rocco and the 18th century parish church, and the Walk of San Valentino towards the ancient Roman river port.

The first of the extensive delights, begun for Niccolò III around 1435 and called the "Versailles degli Estensi"; the museum has archaeological, Renaissance sections in the Vigna Room, modern art and industrial archaeology.

One of the capitals of the Apulian majolica, overlooking an immense gravina: the MuMa in the Palazzo Marchesale, the galleries of the ceramists in the historic center and the Oasi Lipu on the Gravina di Laterza, 12 km long and up to 500 meters wide.

Probably of Norman origin as a defensive outpost; an inscription of 1504 reminds the owner Heronimo Centurione, then passed to Michele Vaaz, founder of the village (1609), to Antonio De Ponte (1677), who made it a noble residence, and to Caracciolo (1779); in 1860 the façade was rebuilt in neo-Gothic style and between 1991 and 2002 was restored. The museum, founded in 1968 by Professor Dino Bianco, exhibits over 5,000 agricultural work objects, crafts, domestic life, traditions and games between the nineteenth and early twentieth centuries, in nine rooms on three floors. The Municipality indicates opening from June to September Friday, Saturday and Sunday 18-22, free admission.
The three-arched bridge over the river that Caesar crossed with his troops ("Alea iacta est"), rebuilt after the destruction of 1944; the dating is discussed between the consular age and Augusta.
The monument symbol of the Lanzo Valleys.
The top that dominates the Biellese and the Canavese.

Baroque Basilica of the seventeenth century commissioned by Francesco I d'Este on a project by Bartolomeo Avanzani, a Greek cross with central dome and two bell towers; on the parish church the bronze statue of John Paul II and, next to, the archaeological area with the remains of the ancient castle destroyed in the seventeenth century. Patronage party on September 8th.

The complex is divided into three parts: the ancient courtyard, the Baronial Palace and the Romanesque Clock Tower. The Palazzo dei Colonna, in dark basalt, rebuilt much of the ancient castle between two corner towers of the urban belt; abandoned in the eighteenth century, was restored in the early nineteenth century. The 36-metre-high Romanesque tower was transformed into a bell tower.

The palace, built in several phases with the oldest part perhaps of the twelfth century, houses in the Hall of the Coat of Arms the "Madonna del Rosario" by Lorenzo Lotto, originally painted for the church of San Domenico.
The castle walled above the Tronto valley.
The hunting castle of Frederick II.
You can still see the ancient prisons.
The Dantesque tower of Ezzelino, with museum and viewpoint.

Described by the city guide as one of the most beautiful squares in Veneto, it is closed on the east side by eighteenth-century buildings and dominated by the bell tower; there are buildings from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century. On the square stands Palazzo Brogliati, built in the seventeenth century, renovated in 1748 and donated to the Municipality by Giovanni Brogliati in 1834, now Town Hall, and the sixteenth century Palazzo Aviani, restored at the beginning of the eighteenth century by the Fioravanzo. From here start almost all the walking routes of the municipality.
The eighteenth-century palace where Vittorio Alfieri was born, home to the National Centre of Alfierian Studies and a small museum with relics of the writer.

The oldest sacred building in Arese, built in 1558 at the behest of the Lattuada family on a pre-existing perhaps Romanesque structure; the two side aisles were added at the beginning of the twentieth century. In the apse it preserves a baptism of Christ of the late sixteenth century, with references to Gaudenzio Ferrari, and a wooden statue of the Madonna del Rosario of the early eighteenth century.
The Rose Reflection.
The ideal starting point.
The centre preserves examples of the local stone processing, such as the portals of Palazzo Citino with the traditional masks and residences overlooking Piazza Matteotti.
A nineteenth-century museum as it was.

Complex built on the ruins of a thirteenth-century castle, made of vaults and narrow corridors in living stone; the chapel preserves paintings of the Umbrian school of the fifteenth and sixteenth centuries and numerous frescoes, and the name would come from the Christ frescoed in the apse.
The 19th century Palermo.
The village on the Aquacheta reached by the curves of the Passo del Centoforche, classic stage of the itineraries by motorbike and bike of the Tuscan Romagna.
From Riomaggiore to Manarola on the sea.
Sentinels against pirates.
The terminus of the historic valley railroad.

Municipality of Val Prino with the hamlets Tavole, Valloria and Villatalla, born around the castle built in the 12th century by the Marquises of Clavesana on the spur of "Petra Lata"; Valloria is the village of the painted doors, Villatalla and the parish church of San Giovanni del Groppo preserve the polyptychs of Agostino Casanova.
The medieval core and the nineteenth-century face of the city.

The ideal city of the Renaissance, home of Raphael and UNESCO historical center: the Doge's Palace of Federico da Montefeltro with the National Gallery of the Marches, the frescoed oratories and the Fortress Albornoz.
A small castle with a Garibaldi story.
The monastery of the Villanovian museum.

Catholic Church of the Leumann Village, wanted by Napoleon Leumann for his employees although he was Protestant, and is still in use. Designed in an eclectic style by the architect Pietro Fenoglio; windows and interior decorations are by a team of painters and decorators directed by Prof. Poirino emery.
The Orsini Loggia.

The seventeenth-century church of the Confraternity of the Battuti (of the Gonfalone), so called for the white clothes of the confreres, on the north side of the country; the interior has a four-leaf plant.
The frescoes by Francesco De Tatti.
The fifteenth-century cloister in the heart of the city.
The Fieschi castle.
Dates of millers engraved since 1770.
Easy river nature, suitable for families.
The untouched medieval village of the Ciociaria.
A trace of the Albanian community of the Dauni Mountains.

On the hill Pancrazio, probably built by the Saracens on the remains of a brute fortress, restored by Ruggero II in 1130 and restored by Frederick II, who in 1239 added the octagonal tower; you can visit the Angevin corridor, the arms room, the throne room and the nineteenth-century bastions.

An eighteenth-century country with an orthogonal plan founded, according to tradition, in 1726 with a colony of Albanian Greeks: in Piazza Garibaldi the church of San Prospero and the Regional Archaeological Museum with the findings of Monte Castellazzo, the ancient Mytistran, and Balate-Valle Oscura; there is also a Museum of Rural Civilization.

The castle is the nucleus from which the historic center has developed, decorated with frescoes inside and outside; it houses the Civic Museum "Federico De Rocco" with a vast collection of artifacts and works of various eras.

In the former Chancellery of the castle complex, created by the Municipality with the Dzogchen Community of Merigar: over 5,000 oriental art objects and ethnographic finds of the Namkhai collection and documents of Himalayan cultures, with panels, multimedia and interactive installations, soundscapes and videos.
A castle with an archaeological site at the gates.
Rebuilt after the earthquake of 1688, the patroness Madonna della Libera was venerated there; here Padre Pio celebrated his first mass.

Built by the Visconti around 1370, after Galeazzo Visconti took Sartirana to the Counts of Lomello, it is the largest castle of Lomellina: quadrangular plan in red bricks with moat, inner courtyard covered with ivy and four angular towers, dominated by the cylindrical tower of north-east. About 1462-1463, under the Sforza, Aristotile Fioravanti strengthened him by adding to the tower the dodecagonal base and the terracotta bells; restored in the nineteenth century with eclectic decorations, since 1975 he is of the Foundation of Studies of Lomellina. Beyond the moat, to the north-west, a garden connected by a crenellated catwalk; next to the parish church and the gun square rise.
One of the largest collections of prehistoric statues.

Founded in the mid-eighteenth century with the collection of the Marquis Scipione Maffei, who called it "Veronese Museum," it was open to the public when almost all the collections were private; it preserves a vast collection of epigraphs.

The patriarchal basilica was born from the union of two churches, one of the sixth century, next to the monumental cemetery of the Verano of 83 hectares where Mameli, Trilussa, De Filippo, Gassman and Sordi rest.

Sixteenth century building in shale, mud and chestnut wood in front of the parish, maximum security prison until the 1940s; in 1793 there were French officers imprisoned during an attempt to disembark Napoleon. The name comes from the vaulted underpass, In the male and female cells restored the permanent exhibition "Bruxas" on witchcraft in Sardinia between the fifteenth and seventeenth centuries, with ritual objects, a section on the Inquisition with instruments of torture and the sanbenito; in the courtyard an ancient sundial. From September to May Tuesday-Sunday 10-13 and 15-18, from June to August 10-13 and 16-19.

The village of the films of Don Camillo and Peppone, with Piazza Matteotti, the church of the talking crucifix and three museums between cinema and Brixellum Romana, the colony that controlled traffic on the Po.

Promontory of granite with clear beaches and transparent waters, sheltered from the islands of Tavolara and Molara and the islet of Proratora, so that the sea remains calm with every wind; the vegetation is Mediterranean maquis. It is part of the marine protected area Tavolara-Punta Coda Cavallo, about 15,000 hectares from Capo Ceraso to Punta s'Isuledda, with diving sites such as the Pope's Secca and Molarotto. Around there are Baia Salinedda, Cala Suaraccia (Beach of the Butterflies) and Cala Ghjlgolu. Free admission from the SS125.

Country residence that Mecenate donated to Orazio between 33 and 32 BC, in the center of an estate of about 40 hectares: a domus italica of Republican age to one floor, 107 m long and 43 wide, in cross-linked work, with residential sector, large quadriportico and spa extended in flavia age, flanked by a porch garden. Digged by Angelo Pasqui since 1911; the artifacts are at the Oratian Civic Museum. Free visits by booking with Aniene Turismo.

The ancient tratturo of transhumance crosses the village and is frequented for horse riding and trekking; on the first Sunday of September Zungoli celebrates the Festa della Trashumanza with tasting and sale of typical products.
The facade of Piermarini on the square of Maggiolini.
Nature of the Gennargentu around the lake.
visits only by reservation (tel. 0924 21578)
The island in the Tiber, the river where according to legend the history of Rome begins.
€8 full, €6 reduced; free up to 12 years

Near the village, the wood Vetruscelli is known for its blooms and black truffle; the river Fortore is born on the east side of the village and flows into the valley. The Frassati Trail, about 50 km between five villages of the Dauni Mountains, you can walk, by mountain bike or on horseback.

The town stands on a rocky spur still partly surrounded by the medieval walls; the Palazzo Comunale, an ancient palazzo dei priori restored in the eighteenth century, houses the accordion museum. Among other attractions Italy.it indicates Porta Marina, the aqueduct tower and numerous churches.
The symbol church of the city.
Canneti and water lilies in a small protected lake.
The story of Dogliani from the Celtic head to the Roman glass.
The village on the marina.
The largest panorama of the internal Sicily.
The little secret revealed by the restoration.
The palace-ship and the terrace gardens on the lake.
€6 in full; €2 reduced

On the way down to Borgo San Pietro, rises where in 1562 the Virgin appeared to a girl named Persiana. The bas-relief of the apparition is carried in procession the evening before the feast, the last Sunday of May, the day when cherries are blessed.
12th century tower, part of the defensive walls of the medieval village and the Castle of Aquino.

Construction dating back to 1710, founded by Fulvio Verdiano, an illustrious citizen of Amantea; the perimeter walls remain standing, without cover, with the characteristic triple crowning of hembrics in a small object.
The bridge over the Neva next to the homonymous door, always a favourite subject of visitors.

Centre with medieval structure with numerous churches, including the cathedral, the Basilica of Santa Maria delle Grazie, bishop's seat of the diocese of Avezzano; it dominates the tower created from the remains of the Old Rocca of the Piccolomini. In the territory also the Torre di Venere dei Marsi of the 13th century and remains of cyclopean walls.
The findings of the Roman colony on the site of the excavation.
The twentieth century of Castilian artists.
The Gothic Castle district.
The lions' fountain.
Of Byzantine origin, it overlooks the main square dedicated to St. Nicholas and guards the body of the saint with his clothes and vestments.

To the north of Cala Jannita, a natural area with Mediterranean maquis (mirt, lentisco, pines and holm oaks) that descends to the sea; the sandy beach and pebbles look at the islet of Santo Janni and where the bottom is low forms a natural swimming pool between the rocks.
Fortified village of Lunigiana that dominates the plain of Magra and Luni, the last village before the sea; Orange Flag since 2014.
Walk in the hamlet of lava stone.
Nineteenth-century villa overlooking the lake, in a large park with centuries-old trees and picnic areas.

The oldest fishing village on the island, reachable only from the sea or on foot along various steps: houses with bright colors arranged amphitheatre on the sea, domes, arches and stairs, fishing boats and nets lying to dry, without car. The best view is from the Belvedere dei Cannoni.
Peaceful stone and coats of arms in the square.

Born in 2010 after the discovery, in 1989, of a protohistoric piroga in the lake near the island of Bisentina, it tells the navigation in the inland waters from the antiquity to the twentieth century, with finds from the lake of Bolsena and boats from Bracciano, Fondi and Posta Fibreno; the route illustrates the naval architecture of fresh water and the activities of fishing, communication and trade. Timetable indicated by the Municipality: Monday-Friday 8.30-13.30 (tel. 0761 872437).
A stone giant in the woods.
Municipal Museum dedicated to the work of the fields and craftsmen of the country.
open only Saturday 15-19 and Sunday 10-12 and 15-19, closed from Monday to Friday, according to the Municipality
A small trompe-l'oeil of three aisles.
The bathroom and walks in the glacial lake.
Visiting times and methods not published on readable sources; the Ministry of Culture announces extraordinary openings at events.
An opera by Andrea da Jesi.
The basilica of the patron of Busto.
A defensive tower with an eighteenth-century majolica clock that hides the 11th century Romanesque bell tower, with stairs illuminated by mirrors and 360° panorama at the top.
The barbaric pirates told by the protagonists in hologram.
MiC card (updated to December 2020) is closed every day: check opening 0872 757126
Museum of the Lombard Apennines of the Four Provinces set up in the castle tower: it preserves tools, tools and machinery of the local agricultural and craft life.

The cove of clear waters on the state road to Portofino, with a small sandy beach equipped with lush vegetation, the castle of Paraggi (nineteenth-century adaptation of a Genoese fortress), restaurants and clubs. The seabeds, suitable for the growth of red coral, attract divers, which can also see a ship sunk in 1917; since the twelfth century the hamlet had numerous mills, some still existing in the locality Acqua Viva. The walking path from Santa Margherita to Portofino passes through the bay and Cervara.
A singular collection of popular devotion.

Frazione between Massa Martana and Todi, of which there are some high towers, with underground cavities and the Romanesque church of Santa Maria di Agello; it is known for the Cicotto di Grutti, Presidio Slow Food cooked in wood-burning ovens.
Church of the XI century, also called San Pietro in Veteribus, with the bell tower overlooking the rock, a fifteenth-century frescoed room and a crypt.

The ancient nucleus, mentioned as Civitella from the 11th century (first Petrarolo) and from the 15th century seat of a barony of the Column, is surrounded by fortified walls still well preserved; the streets, called "rue" are flanked by houses with stone portals carved by local chisels, coats of arms and religious symbols on the architraves and votive newsstands dug in the walls. Among the noble palaces, Palazzo Colonna, Ferrazzilli, Villa and Libri.
The cathedral between Romanesque and Gothic.
The lava stone alleys inside the walls.
Rebuilt largely after the earthquake of 1706 and reopened to worship in 1728.
The reserve of woods around Radicondoli, where geothermal steam puffs rise above the green; deviations to the villages of Anqua and Belforte.

City of the Brescia plain between Brescia and Bergamo, born from a village of Lombardy circular shape and surrounded by walls up to the Venetian age: the Cathedral of Saints Faustino and Giovita with the civic tower of 55 meters, Santa Maria Maggiore, the Morcelli Repossi Foundation, the City Museum, the market documented since 1406 and the liberty Villa Mazzotti with its park.
The large Franciscan church with the tombs of Michelangelo, Galileo and Machiavelli, the chapels frescoed by Giotto, the Pazzi Chapel of Brunelleschi and the Crucifix of Cimabue.

In the historic barn next to the church, rebuilt in 2000, the Enzenberg collection: wooden models, paintings, mining maps, documents and finds of the mines of Predoi, with an exhibition on the life of miners and their families.

Of medieval origins, it collapsed in part in the earthquake of June 3, 1781, during the Mass, with 73 dead; rebuilt since 1790, it has been basilica since 1982. On the unfinished façade the two portals of 1842 by Michelangelo Boni, pupil of Valadier; on the left side remains a Gothic portal of 1424 of the ancient cathedral. Inside three aisles 54 meters long.

Museum on the outskirts of the village with wooden frames and Sardinian textile artifacts (mats, tapestries, blankets), including five eighteenth-century tapinu de mortus, on the eight known in Sardinia, and the affaciadas exhibited during the Corpus Domini.

The small capital of the Riviera dei Cedri, on the Cosentine High Tyrrhenian Sea in the regional park of the same name, linked to the Cedar of Calabria DOP that every year the rabbis gather here for the Jewish feast of Sukkot; to visit the Museum of the Cedar, the archaeological park of Laos and the medieval complex of the Abatemarco.
the source indicates opening only in July and August (Saturdays and holidays) and visits by reservation from May to October

Built in 1560 for the Friars Minor by will of the will of Giulia Acquaviva, wife of Pier Bertoldo Farnese; it includes a garden of about 5.000 m2, the cells of the nuns and a guesthouse. The church contains frescoes from the early sixteenth century, including that of the wedding of Galeazzo Farnese and Isabella degli Anguillara (1514-1518).
Science for children and boys.
Site of Community Importance Interesting for nature lovers and wildlife observation.
A Guinness tea museum in the heart of wheat Sicily.
The frescoed study of a humanist cardinal.

The 13th century complex consists of a church and a convent with cloister, which some sources attribute to Saint Francis himself. Tradition indicates the rock anfratto where the saint would rest; in sacristy an inscription contains the Gospel verse "Faciem tuam lava" (Matthew 6:16-18).

In the Palace of the Ferrini family (completed in 1606), passed to the Municipality in 1715 provided to host a monastery, with monumental facade designed by Ferdinando Fuga since 1739. The museum, opened in 2002 and re-equipped in 2012 with the Chiomenti-Vassalli collection, exhibits among other things the Magdalena penitente by Guido Reni, the Andromeda by Francesco Furini, the Parabola of the blind by Pieter Bruegel the Younger, works by Pietro da Cortona, Pompeo Batoni, Gaspar Van Wittel and Magnasco, and the Immaculate Conception attributed to Masucci. You can also visit the 18th century monastic kitchens with original stone fireplaces.

Built in 1604 for the Confraternity of the Gonfalone and rebuilt several times, with a single nave: two wooden statues of the seventeenth century (Madonna and Archangel Gabriel), small paintings of the Evangelists, a large eighteenth-century canvas of the Risen Christ and a small precious organ in the apse.
Medieval alleys and towers linked to the castle.
On the trail of the front with the Garda under the feet.
Since 1991 it has kept the fresco of the Madonna del Parto painted by Piero della Francesca for the church of Santa Maria a Momentana: the Virgin pregnant between two angels opening a pavilion.
A Romanesque cloister in the woods.

Arbëreshë village (Shën Kolli) founded in the first half of the fifteenth century on the watershed between the valleys of Neto and Lipuda, with a medieval stone centre, apotropaic masks on portals and windows, the churches of St. Nicholas and St. Dominic and the Museum of peasant civilization.
The village on Monte Barro overlooking the lake.
Garibaldi to Marsala.
Byzantine frescoes in Salento to see up close.

Founded in 1976 in an 18th-century manor house, home to the UNLA People's Culture Centre, it collects over 2,000 work tools and everyday objects donated by the families of the country, in 11 of the 23 rooms of the building. The halls are arranged for crafts: farmers, shepherds and charcoal makers, artisans' machines, viticulture, cheese-making and mill, spinning and weaving, work and party clothes, transportation and hydraulic machines; panels also illustrate songs and children's games.

Chapel north of the village, with origins indicated in 1118: it preserves the canvas of the Annunciation (1717) commissioned by Cardinal Orsini to Giuseppe Castellano; restored from 1863 to 1903, in 2008 it had ceiling and six lunettes frescoed by Annunziato De Rubertis with the life of Mary.

The village rises on a hill of the reserve, established in 1979 as the first regional nature reserve of Italy: about 800 hectares between Castelnuovo di Farfa, Fara in Sabina, Montopoli di Sabina, Nazzano and Torrita Tiberina, around the wetland born between 1953 and 1955 from the barrier ENEL sul Tibere, Ramsar area since 1977 and among the best places in central Italy for birdwatching.
The cable car to the ridge.
The parish church preserves a painting attributed to Palma il Giovane and a characteristic wooden altar called "Altar of the Rosary."
visit only by reservation

Cittadina dell'Alto Mantovano from the Renaissance heart, capital of a Gonzaghesque fief since 1511, with the texture documented from the thirteenth century and today textile district; on Piazza Mazzini overlook the prepositural of Sant'Erasmo, the Gonzaga-Acerbi Palace, the Municipal Palace and the Tower of Castelvecchio, a stone's throw from the MAST city museum.
after the earthquake of 2016 historical center, monuments and museums are partially usable (Let's Marche); the card of the Park describes the state prior to the earthquake

The ancient nucleus is enclosed by walls with three doors around the baronial palace, born from a first fortress and today seat of the Town Hall. The village is called "the village of the palaces": the most famous palaces are those of Galanti, Capozzi-Giovene, De Nigris-Gioia, De Mariarosa, Bochicchio-De Maria, Gioia-Bernando and Vitelli.
The sacred art treasure of the country.

Inaugurated in 2006 by the park with Italia Nostra in Caprera, it follows in chronological order, from prehistory to today, the history of the sea and the routes of the archipelago with photos, documents, models, remnants of boats, navigation and fishing instruments, a copy of the Peutingerian Tabula and a Granite Mother Goddess.
From the Gate of the Mill you enter the industrial archaeological park with the remains of the mills built by the Cantelmo along the river Gizio.

Mountain village of the upper Seriana Valley, in the Orobie Alps, Orange Flag of Touring: the Baroque sanctuary of the Madonna delle Grazie, linked to the apparition of June 23, 1607, the ethnographic Museum of the Upper Seriana Valley and the Alpine village of Valcanale, leads to the Trail of the Orobie.
Next to the Duomo, eight Flemish tapestries donated by a king of Spain.

On the grounds of Rocca di Frassinello, along the E80, about thirty mounded tombs recovered and restored with a tour of panels and poetic quotations on wine in the ancient world. The documentation centre, in the cellar designed by Renzo Piano with the barricade dug into the rock, exhibits the findings of the necropolis of San Germano and Santa Teresa di Gavorrano on the theme of Etruscan wine, in a project with Superintendence and University of Florence.

Of early medieval origin, it corresponds to the "castellum quod dicitur Besti" quoted in a parchment of 1059. It was restored around 1240 by Frederick II of Swabia in the program of fortification of the Apulian coast and profoundly modified by the Spanish in the first half of the 16th century. It dominates the coast from a cliff above the Scialara beach.
The Romanesque jewel of the Costa dei Trabocchi, with the play of light of the solstices.
The foundations of the ninth century.
In Villa Savioli, the only museum of its kind in the world, he collects the works of Hamlet Sartori and his son Donato, creators of masks for the Commedia dell'Arte.
Hot springs considered therapeutic, in the municipal territory along the river.
Large Roman tomb of the II-III century A.D., then used as the base of a medieval tower; it is the highest point of the village, with spectacular views of Mount Etna.
For lovers of modern architecture.
The largest baptistery in the world, begun in 1153 by Diotisalvi, with the fountain and pulpit of Nicola Pisano of 1260; the interior has an exceptional acoustic.
Antiques among Renaissance buildings.

Archaeological and civic museum inaugurated on December 6, 2023 in the Palazzo Di Stefano, former prison, at the end of Via Borgo in front of Piazza della Torre dell'Orologio, door of Rione Fossi. It collects sculptures and finds first scattered in the municipal buildings, including the archaeological collection of the ground floor of Palazzo Vassalli and the statue of the Goddess Mother, with immersive installations.
In the secret garden of the palace in front of Santa Maria delle Grazie the vineyard of Malvasia cultivated by Leonardo, back to flowering.
The sulphurous waters of Montefeltro.
The unique history of Italian jewelry.

Lake 2,275 m in an ice basin at the highest edge of the valley, on the border with the French National Park of the Vanoise: an almost flat path from the parking lot offers ibex, chamois, marmots, eagles and gipetes, a waterfall and the permanent exhibition on high altitude peat bogs. From the lake starts the road towards the Colle and Piano del Nivolet, plateau of over 6 km at about 2,500 m with lakes and peat bogs; in summer the Park prohibits the transit of cars from Serru to the hill. Recommended period July-September.
Neo-Gothic palace built in the nineteenth century by Guglielmo Rossi on medieval buildings; the council hall has frescoes by Gerardo Doctori from 1948-1949.
The 17th century church.

Country between the Aurunci Mountains and the sea, home of Fra' Diavolo and the Itrana olive (called Gaeta's), dominated by the medieval castle on the hill of Sant'Angelo; along the Appia Antica remain about two kilometers of Roman basolate in the gorge of Sant'Andrea, while on Mount Fusco stands the sanctuary of the Madonna della Civita.
It preserves machines and furnishings of the Fraioli typography, active since the end of the nineteenth century.
Founded in 1100 and rebuilt in the 17th century by the Franciscans.
The statues saved from theft.
Two hundred nativity scenes of Italian tradition.

Overlooking the panoramic Piazza Umberto I, built in 1589 according to the date on the bell tower: it is one of the few Renaissance churches of Abruzzo with a basilica plan, with a six-arched porch and portal and rose window decorated with angel heads. Inside a wooden pulpit with statues of 17th century saints attributed to Bartholomew Balcony and, in the sacristy, a silver Madonna of Nicola da Guardiagrele; behind the high altar the urn of the Holy Child, arrived from Jerusalem in 1760, celebrated on the third Sunday of September. Since 2015 it has been dedicated to the Child Jesus.

Fortress of the thirteenth century, rebuilt in 1371 and enlarged in the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, on the height of Poggio overlooking the center; it houses the museum with the 19 stele statues of the Lunigiana of the Bronze and Iron Age and the finds of the ancient Luni. Walk up or take the urban elevator.
A long beach free from clear waters, the best place for sunrise and sunset and a popular route for the race.
The lava heart of the village.
A small fifteenth-century church with its legend.

Large and harmonious three-nave church divided by a double row of seven travertine columns, with an underground access to a stucco-decorated chapel and frescoed in the eighteenth century. Originally a palatina church, it was part of the area of the Lombard-Norman fortress on the current Piazza Castello.
On the old railway track, a long sinuous bench in colored stoneware made by international artists for the Biennale di Ceramica in 2001.
The Gothic-Catalan portal of Cardona.
The emerald lake.
A curious double church between the road and the Serio.
Green break ten minutes walk from Santo Stefano.
Seaside resort of the municipality, a strong point of marine tourism.
Roman finds of the territory.
The city's civic tower, open on days of visit.
€5 whole, €4 reduced; free with Trentino Guest Card

Longobard fortification (VII-VIII century) transformed into a fortress by the Normans in the 12th century and then into a noble palace. The 1990 restoration revealed a layer of ash from the eruption of Vesuvius in 1944, portals, stairs, ovens, a well and a basement perhaps used as a prison.
The balcony between Valnerina and Reatino.
The view over Monferrato linked to Bianca Lancia and Dante.

Under the presbytery of the upper church there is the crypt dedicated to the patron saint Sant'Oliva, with in a niche above the altar an ancient statue of the saint that, by tradition, cannot be moved heavy hailstorms on the crops. In June, the feast brings in the night procession the Braccio di Santa Oliva, an arm-shaped relic with an olive branch.
A villa of old time among the hotels.
€11 whole; €2 from 18 to 25 years EU; "Secret Room of Michelangelo" €32 upon reservation
The shrine of the Capuchin saint of Leonessa.
Guided tours from €7 (local operators)

Centro della Bassa Modenese documented since about 776 when Carlo Magno donated to the Abbey of Nonantola the church of Camurana, and for centuries a place of commerce on the border between the Duchy of Este, Lombardo-Veneto and the Papal State: today it offers the faunistic oasis of Via Rubadello, the Chapel of the Duke in Villafranca and seventeen ancient country villas; the 2012 earthquake has made unworkable many historical buildings.

In the Rocca Colonna, it is dedicated to the geologist Ardito Desio, who led the first Italian expedition on the K2 in 1954, and tells the geological history of Lazio in five rooms with original finds, globes, plastics, tactile models and sound contents, including fossils of coral reef of about 100 million years ago. Renovated with PNRR funds     . Attritività dei borghi , reopened with the new equipments on August 9, 2025. On request, guided tours continue on the geopaleontological routes reported around the country; there are audio guides and activities for schools and groups.
A little church of the fourteenth century linked to St. Charles.
In Suzey area beyond the village of Ivery, with the ruins of an ancient castle.
It preserves the Ark of San Domenico, begun by Nicola Pisano and completed by Niccolò dell'Arca, with three statues carved by a young Michelangelo.
Small church built on a rock in Campoledro (Mossini) in 1413, with prismatic apse and frescoes on the south side of the aisle.

Built in the second half of the sixteenth century by Ercole San Bonifacio, of the Padua branch of Sant'Agata, family linked by ancient alliance to the House of Este. It is surrounded by a large garden with statues, including Lodovico III San Bonifacio and the Emperor Augustus, and by walls with wrought iron gates; the entrance is between two pillars with Minerva and Mars. It preserves the archive of family San Bonifacio Polcenigo and Fanna, today Ardit.

The museum tells of the role of women in the family and society of the past and the cultivation and processing of hemp, a long source of income for the economy of the valley, with numerous tools and artifacts and the reconstruction of period environments. It is part of the Ecomuseum Alta Valle Maira; open on request (tel. 0171 999190 or 347 1032172).
The medieval symbol of Mompantero.
Church built in 1630 for the end of the terrible plague epidemic.
Two villas from different eras.
The stones of Salento megalithicism.
The great Bolognese pictorial school from the fourteenth to the eighteenth century: Vitale da Bologna, Raffaello (Estasi di Santa Cecilia), Carracci, Guido Reni, Guercino.
Frescoes and a Franciscan library of 30,000 volumes.
The Pollino canyon under the country.
The church of Romanesque origins along the route of the Via Francigena, in the Oltretorrente district.

Municipality of the lower Valsesia born in 1927 from the union with Vintebbio, Piane and Bornate: the museum Don Florindo Piolo in the Castle of Avondo, the seventeenth-century sanctuary of Sant'Euseo, the Romanesque parish church of Santa Maria di Naula and the remains of the castles of Vintebbio and Bornate.
Lesionata dal seismo del maggio 2012; for Emilia-Romagna Tourism several damaged historical buildings are still closed
Pineta with fitness area and paths shaded by pine trees for walks and quiet stops.
The Renaissance fashion of Tuscia in a Farnese palace.

Opened in 1977 in an annex of the rectory (former oven, woodshed, laundry and pigsty), it tells the hard peasant life of the Seven and Nineteenth Century: on the ground floor a rebuilt stube, tools, baskets and linen processing, with a wheat mill of Auna di Sopra; the upper floor is dedicated to spinning and weaving. Open from April to the end of October; welcome offers. Nearby starts the path of the chestnut of Foiana.

On the hill of Toppa Muraglia, under the ancient village destroyed by the 1980 earthquake, the remains of Compsa, inhabited by the Iron Age, then center of Irpino, Roman town hall and bishop's seat. You can see the hole with part of the porch and the paved with traces of the bronze inscription of Quinto Antisio, the podium of a temple, the area of the amphitheatre then occupied by a castrum, spas, a domus and the road network; at the end of the forum the cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta.

Marble known from the Roman era (stiles and altars of the I-II century are at the Sforzesco Castle); from about 1380, via Toce, Lago Maggiore, Ticino and Naviglio Grande, refurbished the Duomo of Milan, the Certosa and the Duomo of Pavia and the Arch of Peace. It is among the first examples of excavation in the gallery; visits only by reservation, in front of the entrance a covered picnic area.

Residential and productive rustic villa built in the middle of the 1st century BC and abandoned in the 3rd century AD after a fire, with representative rooms, mosaic floors and suspensurae heating; so far the eastern sector has been dug. A walkway with educational panels crosses the complex and shows some restored mosaics.
The statues of the serresi craftsmen.
Parish church built in the sixteenth century instead of a church of 1219, with nineteenth-century façade; it preserves the Dinner in Emmaus by Luigi Crespi, signed and dated 1748.
closed from early November to late March, reopens on 20 March 2027 (churburg.com, vinschgau.net)

The church is isolated to the south of Entesano, within the stone wall of the ancient cemetery: a single nave, a hut façade with stone and oculus portal, brick bell tower of 1907. From the first building, from the late fifteenth or early sixteenth century, remains the presbytery, decorated with a cycle of frescoes probably seventeenth century with stories of Mary and Jesus, saints, prophets and angels, attributed by tradition to Matteo Leban from Tolmino. Damaged by the 1976 earthquake and long abandoned, it was consolidated and restored from 2013 to 2016.
The church with a mighty mass completely rebuilt between 1706 and 1722 by Francesco Zondini.

It rises in the large courtyard of Cascina Mocchirolo, very close to the route of the ancient Via Cantura. Dated 1355, it was built by Lanfranco Porro, official of the Visconti; inside there are traces of frescoes attributed to Pecino da Nova, while the original pictorial cycle is today at the Pinacoteca di Brera in Milan. Visits by reservation at the City's Culture Office.

The 17th century church was profoundly renovated in the 18th and 19th centuries, with a single hall with three vaulted bays and a portico on granite columns; in the façade three large mosaics by Don Mino Trombini with Saints Alessandro, Bartolomeo and Antonio Abate, and bell tower with Ghibelline battlements and marble mullioned windows of Vezza. Inside the main altar of Giovan Battista Zotti and the altar of the Rosary of the workshop of Ramus, with a Nativity palace whose shepherds are inspired by the locals.
Cycle path of about 80 km from Spilimbergo to Lignano along the Tagliamento, between woods and open spaces, with different areas equipped for the stop.
Villa noble with Mediterranean park.

A fishing village scattered among cliffs and terraces on the UNESCO site of the Amalfi Coast, famous for the Emerald Cave, discovered in 1932; on the promontory the sixteenth-century Torre del Capo di Conca and, overhanging the sea, the former convent of Santa Rosa where the homonymous leaf was born.
Bagheria's walk.

A 16th century church in Gothic-Aragonese style, rebuilt in neo-Gothic forms in 1789, which preserves two wooden altars of the eighteenth century; feast on 11 June. In the village also the seventeenth-century church of the Madonna del Rosario and the oratory of Santa Croce of the sixteenth century.
Two medieval churches of the Brenner street.
A flat pedal along the water to the old graphite mill.
Palace of the late seventeenth century by Baron Trigona, now home to the city museum.

The centre preserves the medieval castrum, with the two ancient gates of Santa Croce and Sant'Angelo and the remains of the castle walls around which the village grew; there are Palazzo Galloni, formerly of the Colonna, and Palazzo Candia.

Mother church in the center of the village, built in the fifteenth century and enlarged in the sixteenth and eighteenth. It preserves the silver bust of San Zopito (1753-1759), attributed to Giuseppe Sanmartino or to a close collaborator and probably merged by the goldsmith Filippo del Giudice.
ATL describes it under precarious structural conditions

From 1998 he took care in aviaries on the motto of Castel Tirol the wounded raptors until release and welcomed those who could no longer fly; twice a day demonstrations of flight with the experienced Willy Campei and Florian Gamper, and didactic paths in the park. Season 2026 from March 28 to November 8, 10.30-17.
To understand how a swamp has become a city, from the Punics to the reclamation.
Cathedral with Romanesque portal, wooden choir and mosaics.
The alternative Rome.
To be verified; in the Firenze Card
The oldest church in the village, in Castrum Sancti Pauli, which preserves almost intact the original forms: Greek cross plan, wooden trusses ceiling and bell tower of about 1400.
A boundless view.
The view of the Natisone.

Location of the info point and the Galleria civica with the permanent exhibition "Sign and identity of a Community." Great artists of the Novecento Castiglionese. Open Friday 15-18, Saturday and Sunday 9-12 and 15-18.
The former prisons of Asiago, renovated and converted into a museum in 2001, host temporary exhibitions, especially of contemporary art, also set up in the ancient cells.
The carbonai land above the clouds.

Municipality of Alta Val Sangone, seat of the Ecomuseum Alta Val Sangone with the museum of the Resistance of the valley; in the territory you can visit the mine of talc Garida, active until 1968, the giant bench on the Castle Hill and the ski resort of Pian Neiretto.

From the Cathedral Museum you descend into the tunnels of an Etruscan aqueduct, believed for centuries the tomb of King Porsenna: 130 meters up to the Etruscan-Roman cistern of the first century BC and then up to the tower of the twelfth century.

Adriatic seaside resort with Blue Flag beach since 1999, promenade and cycle path of the Adriatic Cyclovia; on the hill the medieval village of Montepagano with doors, church of the Annunziata and Museum of Material Culture, and to the north the Borsacchio Reserve.
The bottom of the valley at a family step.

Urban villa of the first half of the eighteenth century, inhabited by the families Galante, De Vito and finally Loreto, then passed to the Municipality; about 1,500 square meters on three levels, with stone facade, decorated portal, rosette, worked balconies and an eighteenth-century balustrade on the Baroque garden with well. Recently restored, you visit by reservation.
A walk through the woods to the cave.
Calder at the entrance of the city.

Built between 1898 and 1904 incorporating the ancient church, visited by St. Charles Borromeo in 1566: two Renaissance polyptychs, a Madonna on copper by Pietro Mera, the 17th century altar in golden wood and, on the ancient apse, 16th century frescoes with the lion of St. Mark.
Contemporary architecture 4 km from the center.

Among the most venerated sanctuaries of the Amiata, at the entrance of the village, with works of Sienese school: the Virgin in glory between the Saints Sebastiano and Rocco of Ventura Salimbeni and, on the high altar, a Madonna and Child of the first fifteenth century coming from the Palazzo della Capitaneria.
Insects, reptiles and birds.
One of the great Lombard neoclassical parks, with free entrance.
A 19th-century stage room.

Among the smallest theatres in Italy and Europe, in the Public Palace: an inscription in the hall recalls that in 1732 the community transformed the barn of the palace into a theatre, when the young people of the country got to recite comedies at Carnival; it takes its name from the Philo-dramatic Academy of Rustici and continued its activity despite the hostility of the papal authorities. It has 96 seats; on the ground floor of the building a barn and a mill.

To the north of the municipal territory, named after the astronomer of Cantalupo in Sannio, it allows astrologers to observe the sky and has a planetarium that reproduces the celestial vault with 20,000 sidereal bodies.

Large sunny alpine pasture north of Antronapiana, at the entrance of Val Loranco. At the beginning of the seventeenth century there was already a chapel dedicated to St. Bernard of Menton, protector of the Alpine people; the oratory was built around 1650 after the landslide, had the bell in 1661 and carved by Giulio Gaglio in 1702-1703. It was a destination for pilgrimages in droughts and a stop towards San Lorenzo di Bognanco.
Wine village between Perugia and Assisi, at the confluence of Tiber and Chiascio: the Wine Museum in the Palazzo Graziani Baglioni and the Olive and Oil Museum in an ancient oil mill.
Nero's golden palace.

A small museum born from the collection of Emilio Serra, who for about forty years has been searching for finds in the mountains of Val di Sole, the theatre of fighting from June 1915 to October 1918: weapons, everyday objects, uniforms and equipment, especially skis, crampons, snowshoes and the straw overshoes of the sentries. A soundroom in surround tells the letter of a soldier to his mother; the museum, fully accessible, organizes guided tours of the Fort Strino and the forts Zaccarana, Mero, Pozzi Alti and Presanella on request.
A shore of the lake almost intact, to walk or bike.
The green behind the center.
To follow the reopening.
A monumental Veronese in a provincial church.
A unique museum in Europe dedicated to the art of children around the world.
visits only by reservation, Tuesday and Thursday 10-12 and 15-17, according to the Municipality
Diva shoes.
Church in a panoramic position in the historic center, recognizable from afar for the bell tower and the dome.
The birthplace of Benedetto Croce.

Romanesque bridge of the fourteenth century with five arches in sandstones, on Roman foundations of the first century A.D.: known as "Pons de trabe Bonantis" was one of the main post stations of the Lauretana street, where the roads from the South to Norcia and Visso continued towards Camerino, and the main access to the valley of Pievebovigliana, between the castle of Beldiletto and the convent of San Francesco.
A fresco in the circle of Perugino.
An island on the lake where the first palafittic inhabitants of the Alps lived.

Ethnographic Museum opened in 1995 in Macchia di Giarre to preserve the memory of rural life: five large rooms reconstruct a farmhouse and a peasant house of the last century, with agricultural tools, a spindle and a cone of 1750, a frame, traditional clothes (tailories, wedding dresses, party and Sunday), embroidery and ancient daguerrotypes. Designed as a museum, it hosts activities that revive customs related to popular festivals; guided tours available.

Medieval town on the right of the Tagliamento which preserves the moat and three access towers; around the porch Piazza del Popolo overlook the Palazzo Altan-Rota, the Antico Teatro Sociale in the old loggia, the eighteenth-century Cathedral and the church of Santa Maria dei Battuti frescoed by Pomponio Amalteo, while the Palazzo Tullio Altan houses the Museum of Rural Life "Diogene Penzi" .
The thirteenth-century reliquary cross.
The ruins of the Arborea judges.
Padua seen from the water.
The history of cycling in one museum.
A historical theatre in the municipal loggia.

Pieve cited in 1204 and national monument since 1880: the wooden coffered ceiling has twenty canvases by Cesare Vecellio (1577-1579) with stories of the Virgin and the Polyptych of the Assumption, with eight saints, is of the workshop of Titian. Three aisles on local stone columns and works by Palma il Giovane, Giovanni da Mel, Pietro Liberi and others.
The signs of the seventeenth century in the city.
Unpublished times: MiC card indicates closed every day; tel. 0981 952185

Ring that follows for a stretch the path of the Lake Spina, with a wide panorama of the hills and the Alps, then deviates to the sanctuary of Spina and returns to the starting point; along the path signs report the Beatitudes.
The gorge of the mills a stone's throw from the center.

Born in the 18th century as a private theatre attached to a country house of the Vitelli family, it passed to the Municipality in the 19th century; after the damage of the earthquake of 1917 it was restored with a gallery in Art Nouveau style. Re-opened in 1991, it has 99 seats. For visits the source indicates the Pro Loco (tel. 075 8592237).
One of the great monasteries of the Alps, including art, library and wine.

Built in 1737-1739 on the old church of San Francesco, with bell tower of 1780: it contains six octagonal paintings by the brothers Antonio and Vincenzo Manno, a wooden statue attributed to Domenico Noffo (1670) and a canvas by D'Antoni from 1857.

Considered the most intact aqueduct of Sardinia, dated between the 1st and 3rd century AD and restored or rebuilt between III and IV: it brought water from the sources of Cabu Abbas to the thermal baths for about 3.5 km. You can see a section of about 100 meters with a rectangular cistern; other remains in Via Canova and Via Nanni.
A moving path.
Inaccessible interior after the earthquake of 2016
Mimmo Rotella and the art gallery.
The mountain of the city south of Belluno, with biotopes such as the Faverghera-Col dorsal and the valley of San Mamante and a network of paths.
A sixteenth-century mechanism that still marks time.
Sea and view around the lighthouse.
13th century cathedral, heir to the ancient diocese of Sulcis, overlooking the square of the historic center.
€4, reduced €2; during the exhibitions €7, reduced €5
The Great River, its fish and crafts.

The tower was built between the end of the sixteenth and the beginning of the seventeenth century, 16 meters high with a base of about 22 meters, on a promontory about 30 meters above sea in visual connection with the towers of Calasetta and Carloforte; in 1767 it was guarded by an alcaid, an artillery and five soldiers, it was disarmed in 1851 and, restored, it is now of the Municipality. Inside once a dome on four ribs; the original entrance was 5 meters high, with spiral staircase in the wall thickness. It hosts exhibitions, events and conferences.
The Greek Palinuro.
The sea and the yards of Viareggio.

Masterpiece of the Roman provincial architecture of the High Empire: the southern facade 22 meters high, lightened by three orders of arches and windows; the cavea housed almost four thousand spectators.

Pinnacles and pebble towers cemented by clay and clay limits, shaped by erosion, rust-coloured walls. You can reach it on foot from the dam of the lake: about 6-7 km round trip, 200 m of difference in altitude and about 3 hours, first on dirt road and then almost always in the shade of a holm oak; alternatively you start from the viewpoint of the Ruffella passing through Fiegni.
Seven centuries of glass inside the old furnace.

Frazione that preserves the remains of a furnace for live lime, from which perhaps derives the name, and, along the Pianelle Fosso, an ancient water mill restored and transformed into a dwelling with Liberty details. Legend has it that the fairies, surprised from dawn after dancing with the local youths, left their footprints on the side of Mount Vettore; the village staged the representation "The descent of fairies."

Museum on the territory dedicated to rural civilization, crafts and the brick industry, of which Marsciano is the largest Umbrian center. The main pole is Palazzo Pietromarchi, 14th century noble residence of the Counts Bulgarelli, with the section on the brick and a fresco of the first sixteenth century school of Pinturicchio (Madonna on throne with Child and Angels, San Silvestro and San Rocco).
The large reed of the lake, for birdwatching and walks.
A 19th century family archaeological collection.

Among the oldest churches in Umbria, built in the VII-VIII century on a Roman building along the Via Flaminia; three-four-century façade with rose window, interior with three naves with cinerary urns, inscriptions, Roman fragments, a large Corinthian capital, an altar stone and frescoes. Around the Vicus Martis Tudertium, a village built in the state of Martis della Flaminia: about seven hectares, with well-preserved perimeter-walled buildings brought to light by excavations.
Just outside the country, founded around the year 1000 by the Camaldolese monk San Romualdo; it is owned by the Sovereign Military Order of Malta.

55 metres high, it is the highest tower in the province of Reggio Emilia: it was built after the destruction of the fortress in the battle of Luzzara in 1702, it was started in 1724 with the materials of the old fortifications and thanks to collections of wheat, wine and money, and completed in 1780 with the cross surmounted by the pike, emblem of the country. Eleven floors, four bronze bells, 147 steps to the bell cell; in the twentieth century it was also aqueduct tower. It is admired from the outside: the climbs to the bell cell are rare, on special occasions.

The collection was born in 1869 to accommodate the works of closed cult buildings, almost all between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries; it is located in the neoclassical building of 1923 in the gardens of the municipal villa.

Built between 1871 and 1875 in neo-Gothic style by the Turinese Luigi Formento, in the space destined to the presbytery of the abandoned Antonellian project. Inside the main baroque altar coming from another church in the village, windows of the 1930s, two large paintings by Elio Torrieri and a golden wooden statue of Our Lady of 1792; in the tympanum of the facade of Christ and the Saints Peter and Paul by Renzo Igne.
The picene roots of Pollenza.

Considered the most important wetland in Italy, it is a web of canals, water mirrors, reeds and swamps populated by many species of aquatic birds, residue of the ancient lake Prile; you can walk or horse.
The door to the Julian Pre-Alps Park.
The Neapolitan majolica.

Small Franco-Provençal municipality of the Lanzo Valleys, between 750 m of Boschietto and 2,345 m of Monte Bellavarda, with the sanctuary of Santa Cristina on the rocky spur above the village and the ancient mine of talc Brunetta.
They were seen by the painters of the Grand Tour.
China and Ande inside a monastery in Garda.

Dedicated to the patron Saint Famiano, celebrated on August 8, at the foot of the historic center; it has a raised presbytery of great artistic value. It is a stage of the Way of Light, variant of the Via Amerina.
A noble palace in the centre.
In the sixteenth century Palazzo Amalteo, collections of geology, paleontology, zoology, botany and entomology with attention to local ecosystems.

The Teramano hill centre mentioned already in 1173 in the catalogue of Norman Barons, with a nucleus gathered inside a ring of ring of ring and overlooking the valley; in its territory stands Santa Maria a Vico, a Romanesque church of the tenth century considered the oldest monument of Abruzzo almost intact.
The origins of ancient Siberene.
Waterfalls under the Gran Sasso.

The capital of the small county of Gonzaga from 1371 to 1728: the Fortress with the Gonzaga Museum and the theatre, the sixteenth-century portico square with the Collegiate Church of Lelio Orsi and, outside the village, the Valli and the country residences of the court.
Quiet in the stain.
Fortified village on a tuff cliff dominated by the Fortress Orsini, with Etruscan and medieval Sovana in its territory.
Kilometers of dunes on the Gulf of Asinara.
An ogliastrina house as it was, with the culurgiones made before you.

Natural cave on the north-eastern side of the Majella, frequented by the Middle and Upper Paleolithic until the high Middle Ages; at the entrance remain the remains of a church perhaps risen on an Italian temple. From the place of worship are the bronze statue of the ...Dea of Rapino , today at the National Archaeological Museum La Civitella of Chieti, and Tabula Rapinensis, lamina with a sacred law in Marrucino dialect which appoints the ...Touta Marouca , and the cult of Ceria Iovia: for this reason it is considered the main sanctuary of the Marrucini.
Five waterfalls (Vaccinello or Cascata del Moro, Arenile, Braccio di Mare, Ospedaletto and Mola) reachable with easy paths suitable for children from the new cemetery of Cerveteri.
Caffè storico frequented by Giacomo Puccini and Arturo Toscanini, designed by architect Alfredo Belluomini with ceramics by Galileo Chini, the first stage designer of Turandot.
The pure Renaissance among walnuts.
Born in 1747 on a project by Giovanni Battista Zaist, destroyed by a fire in 1806 and immediately rebuilt as Teatro della Concordia, from the early twentieth century entitled to Amilcare Ponchielli.

The oldest part dates back to 1290, when the Municipality of Asti had it built as a fortification; in the seventeenth century the counts Amico transformed it into a residence and at the beginning of the eighteenth century Benedetto Alfieri, uncle of Vittorio, made it a baroque residence, with a large central niche façade similar to those of the palaces Mazzetti of Asti and Ghilini of Alexandria and a terrace on lowered arches. The Salone Verde, with hand-painted Vietri ceramic floor, hosts exhibitions and chamber concerts; the Salone Rosso, an ancient hall of representation, is the seat of the City Council.

Small cobblestones at the bottom of a blade of Mediterranean maquis, between two spurs of rock: Blue Flag and 4 sails of Legambiente. You descend from a rocky slope (serve suitable shoes); free parking on the road above.
The peasant life of the Tidone Valley in a ducal villa.

Small centre of Val Trebbia, 176 metres, gathered around the castle Anguissola, home to the archaeological museum, and the millennial parish church of Sant'Antonino overlooking the river; in Sant'Andrea the park of the Neolithic village, one of the most important prehistoric sites of northern Italy, and above the valley the ophiolitic rocks of Pietra Perduca and Pietra Parcellara.
In front of the Rock of the Elephant, well preserved and dating back to the last phase of the Nuragic age, with main tower almost 9 meters high and diameter of 11 meters.
Historical building inserted by the Municipality among the main palaces of the city.
The lake overlooking Caprarola and Ronciglione, signposted among the medieval destinations of Tuscia.

House museum wanted by Father Tarcisio Rondinelli, Franciscan friar of the Custody of the Holy Land, who since 2010 lives in the restored building of the Pendino district. Upstairs, the friar's study and a room dedicated to Francavilla, St. Francis and the Franciscan Order; on the ground floor, exhibitions on non-Catholic Christian confessions and non-Christian religions and a "Pantheon" in the former stable, with pyrographies by Father Rondinelli, graphics by Lina Ruperto and models by Lello Torchia. Open Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday 9-12 and 16-19.
The castles on the islets of the lake, reachable only by boat.
A scenic park and a museum in Africa.
Born in the 1970s for sustainable tourism, it has bowling courts, areas equipped with benches and tables, services and parking, the Koliba restaurant and since 2000 a weekend of summer concerts.

The gateway to the Maritime Alps Park in the Gesso Valley: the sulphurous thermal baths at 1,370 meters wanted by Vittorio Emanuele II, the Valderia botanical garden of the violet of Valdieri, the eccomuseum of rye in Sant'Anna and the necropolis of the Bronze and Iron Age.
Protected area, waiting for recognition as regional or national park, frequented for walks and trekking often organized by local associations.
The shelter became a museum.

Karst plateaus about 900 meters between Monte Altuino and Monte Scalambra, in the Simbruini, with a damp and green side and one of bare slopes; fir woods, beech over 800-1000 meters and chestnut woods on the slopes of the Scalambra.
The great neoclassical temple reborn after the earthquake of 1887.
Active plant since 1877, with salsobromoidic and sulphurous waters, in the thermal park.
The columns that measure bradisism.

Fortified village documented by 1063, feud of the counts Guidi and the first fourteenth century of the Fridolfi Ricasoli; in the thirteenth century the castle was surrounded by walls with three gates, in 1529 the castle was conquered by the troops of the Prince of Orange and around 1550 it became the seat of the League of Havane. To see the church of San Pietro with the main bell of 1322 and the silver votive lamp of 1571 for the victory of Lepanto, the Porticciola (the only surviving door) and the coat of arms of the Municipality of Montegonzi in via Bartolo.
The widest white beach on the coast of Pulsano.

Roman rural village (I-VI century A.D.), one of the largest in the region, discovered during construction works at the state road 42 with excavations between 1986 and 1996 and preserved under a supermarket: over 1,000 m2 buried by about four meters of Drion deposits, with stone walls and lime, rooms, floors and fireplaces preserved for about one meter and three construction phases. Farming, cereals and weaving were lived; a walkway above the excavation, interactive totems and panels guide the visit, with exhibits. Open Wednesday 9-12,30, Saturday and Sunday 15-18, other days by reservation.

Designed by Asti architect Filippo Malabayla and built since 1646; in the early seventeenth century he took the parish functions from San Lorenzo. It was painted by Paolo Gaidano in 1892, a painting of the Moncalvo school on the altar of the Rosary, a great crucifix of 1690 on the high altar and two paliotti of 1682-1683; the bell tower was raised in 1905 up to about 30 m.
The Gothic Line bunkers in Apennines.

Under the castle, it has a Baroque shape from the reconstruction of 1728 on a 14th century plant expanded in the 16th century; the restoration after the earthquake of 1980 brought to light Romanesque structures. It preserves paintings of the Neapolitan school of the seventeenth century, wooden statues, altars between the fifteenth and eighteenth centuries and a crucifix dated to the thirteenth century.
In Piazza Piloni the visitor centre of the national park established in 1990, about 30,000 hectares in 15 municipalities: Belluno is the only capital with part of the territory in a national park.
Three centuries of Apulian life next to the sanctuary.
A reborn mountain village and the creeks of the Park.
Romanic bichrome cousin of Saccargia.

Named after Umbro Apollonio, to which refer the catalogues published between 1983 and 1990, it contains about a hundred works made between 1970 and 1980, divided into three sections: cinetism and perception, module and series, color. It is dedicated to optical art, neo-constructivism, kinetic and programmed art and the collectives of the sixties and seventies; the works are exhibited in the council hall of the City Hall, with opening inaugurated on 30 November 2024. Photographic reproductions of the works are not allowed.
Sulfural source and alpine fauna.

Early twentieth-century building of liberty and eclectic taste, with three-level turret, on the right bank of the Naviglio d'Ivrea, built to measure the flow rates of the channels born after the Cavour Canal and regulate the distribution of water; it worked little for the failures caused by the silhouette of the Dora Baltea. Relying on the Consorteria Canali Cavour, it is a pole of the Ecomuseo delle Terre d'Acqua and is visible only from the outside.
