Cultural space of the Lunigian Centre of Dante's Studies on the link between Dante and Lunigiana, opened in 2003 as the Museo Dantesco Lunigianese: occupies the noble floor of the last house-tower of the thirteenth century walls, with Renaissance trifora and wooden ceiling with traces of sixteenth century friezes. Showcases with historical books of the Dante tradition, library and educational panels. Visits only by reservation.
Fresh air after the beach.
The historic market of the city.

Wood of beech trees of over 400 hectares below 500 meters of altitude, along the road that descends from the village in the countryside, with many species of plants and animals, including the Alpine Rosalia; area equipped with tables and barbecue and nature trails.
Reconstruction of the beekeeper's house, the workshop where the hives were prepared and honey extracted from the bee-buyers; guided tours.

The village, about 514 meters away, was surrounded by walls for defence, incorporating a more ancient watchtower, one of the many fates on the Tyrrhenian coast between the XI and XII century against pirates and Saracens. It is the only one of the Waldensian settlements of Cosentino that has preserved the ancient Occitan language and, up to recent times, the traditional costume; in the center are held rites like the Bèlla Stela of Epiphany, torched from the convent square to the parish church.
A painting box from the first fifteenth century.

Built around 1218 by the Franciscans, it is considered the first Franciscan church in the north-east of Sardinia; in 1227 Honorius III raised it to a minor basilica, the first in Gallura. In squared granite and Romanesque forms, it retains the three-nave system; it was rebuilt in the eighteenth century, when it obtained the privilege of the Holy Door, and enlarged in 1912. It preserves the wooden Madonna called "Queen of Gallura," frescoes with the Baptism of Jesus and Saints Nicolò and Trano; the bronze door of Luca Luchetti (1970s) opens every seven years for a year, September 8, the feast of the Nativity of Mary.
The castle of the queen of Cyprus became theater.
Wine cellars dug in the local stone called "moltrasina" which are ideal for preserving wine; the typical dish of the village are the missoltini served with polenta.
The shrine of the patron saint in the woods.

Borgo on the hills of Valdarno in the center of the mining basin: the extraction of lignite caused land collapses and the village was permanently abandoned due to lack of security, with the inhabitants transferred to the new mining village of Santa Barbara. Today it houses the MINE museum; near, the artificial lake in the former mining area, now green oasis.
The avenue from the station to Piazzale della Vittoria, with buildings from the 1920s and 30s: an open-air museum of twentieth century architecture.
Listing in extension: the guide covers for now 0 of the 4 places of culture recorded by the Ministry of Culture in this municipality, as well as churches, squares and nature.
Baroque Sanctuary in the village of Lezzeno, in a very panoramic position above the lake.
The birthplace of Giovanni Branca.

Presented as the first museum in the world dedicated only to portable padlocks: over 3,000 specimens of different forms and epochs, from Europe, China, Africa and Asia, collected in sixty years by Vittorio Cavalli and set up by the Center Studies of the Valleys of the Termina with the Municipality. Open only by reservation.
Decorated with frescoes from the Giotto school.
€8 whole; €2 from 18 to 25 years; single ticket €10 with Civic Museum, Gipsoteca and Avia Pervia
Villages of the middle Champorcher valley at the confluence of Ayasse, Brenne and Manda, the village of bridges between wild gorges.
The eastern gate of the city between two mighty square towers, which has come to us intact: one of the best preserved doors of the Roman world.
The civil life of the ancient city.
The convent of the young Bell.
The golden façade of the eighteenth century.

The villa commissioned by Federico II Gonzaga and built by Giulio Romano between 1525 and 1535, with the Hall of Horses, the Chamber of Love and Psyche and the Chamber of Giants; it houses civic collections and exhibitions.
Included in the Pilot ticket: €18 full, €2 from 18 to 25 years

With its 1,378 meters it is the northernmost peak of the Lepini Mountains, covered with beech, maples and oaks; you climb with an easy excursion from the sports field of Segni and the top offers a spectacular view.
Natural area protected since 1995, with a rich landscape and environmental heritage; there live foxes, weavers, martens, wild boars, squirrels and hares. Fossato di Vico is inside the park.
Pinacoteca, library and Neapolitan nativity scenes.
In the Renaissance Palace Della Rovere, it exhibits statues, epigraphs and materials emerged from the excavation campaigns of the archaeological park of Suasa.
From the lake to the beech and back, with views of the Fortress of Angera.

The capital of the Ciociaria dominates from above the plain of Sacco: the viewpoint of Piazza Vittorio Veneto, the Cathedral with its bell tower, the church of San Benedetto, the Roman amphitheatre and the archaeological museum; at Carnival the historic Festa della Radeca.

Spezieria cinquecentesca with antique tools for the preparation of medicinal products and 238 vases modeled in 1580 in the Urbino workshop of Mastro Antonio Patanazzi, decorated with biblical, mythological and historical scenes and with the coat of arms of Cesaro Candia. The kit was purchased at the auction in Messina in 1628 by Don Gregorio Bottaro for 400 onze and donated to the Brotherhood of the SS. Sacramento, who rented it to various herbalists until 1852, when the spices store ceased its activity.

City of the Vercelli plain along the Via Francigena, surrounded by rice fields and famous for the historical Carnival documented since 1328: the Cathedral of Sant'Agata with the Romanesque crypt of Santo Stefano and the 12th century bell tower, the church of SS. Trinità, the village of Vettignè with its fifteenth-century castle and, in the countryside, the hydraulic works of the Cavour Canal.
Birdwatching and bike ride with views of the two lakes.
Fortified village at 288 meters, whose ancient parish church preserves a table of Bartolomeo di Gentile, the Madonna with the Child and saints.
The panorama of the first basin.
Colonel Beckwith's schools.
The neo-Gothic Sabaudo overlooking the plain.

The municipality north of Lazio on the Francigena, which owes its name to the waterfalls towards the Paglia: the cathedral of the Holy Sepulchre, the castle of Torre Alfina and the reserve of Monte Rufeno.
The passage to the river.

Borgo della piania Brescia with a castle erected around the 1000 against the Hungarians and destroyed several times, under Venice from 1428 to 1797 and crossed by the Fossa Magna Viscontea; to see the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Castello with paintings by Francesco Maffei and Pietro Ricchi, the parish church of San Giovanni Battista and the Romanesque parish of Santa Maria in Carpino.
History and panorama of the old border.
Hand-worked wrought iron.
Listen to the echo inside.
The tower that the Valperga wanted higher than that of rivals.

Granite village of Gallura on the slopes of the Ghjuanni Mountains, between Tempio Pausania and Palau, Luogosanto has 22 sanctuaries between village and country: in the center the basilica of Our Lady, the first Franciscan church of the north-east Sardinian, just outside the hermitage of San Trano. Nearby there are the ruins of the castle of Balaiana with the small church of San Leonardo and the Palazzo di Baldu in the ancient villa of Sent Steva.

The town of Bassa Friulana, Torviscosa was founded in 1937-1938 at the ancient Zuino Tower around the SAICI plant of the Snia group, which obtained cellulose from the gentle cane on land reclamation, and was inaugurated as a village in 1940; in the square dominated by the tower is the CID, which houses archives and collections.

Federal Sanctuary of the Lucans dedicated to the goddess Mephyte, deity of the waters, and to the god Mamerte, next to a still active source; renovated in Roman times in the second century BC and abandoned in the first century AD, probably due to landslides that transformed the area into marsh.

In Palazzo Barracco, Italian art from the second post-war period to today, with works by Mimmo Rotella, Bruno Ceccobelli, Mario Merz and international artists such as Vanessa Beecroft and Jannis Kounellis.
The bridge that named the village.
From chestnut wood to abetina on Aspromonte.
An eighteenth-century shrine in the park of the same name, among the cork groves.
The tower that hangs over Trasimeno.
Around the abbey the monks cleared, reclaimed and watered the lands creating rotten areas; today the territory is part of the Ticino Park, between rows of poplars, irrigation channels and wetlands.
Merano's story in a building.
Gaudenzio out of town.

Established by the Municipality in 1996 and dedicated to the nature of the Camuno-Sebino territory, it bears the name of the naturalist priest who in the nineteenth century introduced the lake of Iseo; it exhibits birds, mammals, shells, butterflies and minerals. Open from Tuesday to Sunday 15-18.

Roman arched bridge with all sixth in square work on the stream Bagnatore, along the Valeria Nova street of the time of Nerva (97 A.D.); from the taxes protrude five shelves that held the wooden centers of the building. It takes its name from the nearby monastery of San Giorgio, of which the ruins remain; the Superintendence restored in 2008-2009 the nineteenth-century viaduct.
Vallone easily accessible for trekking and mountain biking.

Country of the Modena Apennines among chestnut and beech woods, grown around the thirteenth-century fortress that today houses the Historical Museum and the contemporary sculptures of the Artis Forum; in the hamlets the collection of Iola and the fourteenth-century frescoed oratories.
Hiking and mountain biking trail along the valley, curated by associations active in the area.
The surviving Romanesque tower.
The paper made like in the nineteenth century.
the MiC card (updated to June 2020) shows discordant prices (€5 full and €2.50 for 19-64 years) and the ticket office as closed, in contrast to the timetables
The medieval heart above the coast.

Two small halls behind the last step of the Shrine display war materials, relics, photographs of the first shrine on the Colle di Sant'Elia, documents and paintings of Ciotti decorating the first tomb of the Duke of Aosta, with reconstructions of military posts. Not far, at an altitude of 89, an observatory with the plastic of the front line at dawn of 24 October 1917. It depends on Onorcaduti (Ministry of Defense); the MiC card (2021) indicates Tuesday-Saturday 9-17 with pause 12-14.
Karst cave known for the beauty and therapeutic effects of its vapors, a sort of natural sauna in a secular park; symbol of the thermal tradition of Monsummano, which dates back to the Roman era.

The Palazzo Giardino, known as "Casino" (Casino), the centre of Gonzaga's private life, was built between 1578 and 1588 and decorated by artists led by Bernardino Campi. Next to it, the Galleria degli Antichi (1584) is a unique hall 96 meters long with an external porch; in front, in Piazza d'Armi, the Column of Minerva holds a statue of Roman imperial age.
visits only by reservation, closed on rainy days
Museum of fabric and costume with paths dedicated to perfume; unique ticket with Ca' Rezzonico and Casa di Carlo Goldoni.
Cathedral of the sixteenth century with a Deposition and a Spanish Nativity and a early Christian sarcophagus.
€6, reduced €2
From the sea to the Sibillini.
A Venetian village on the two banks of the river.
Abandoned at the beginning of the twentieth century and then reborn thanks to the artists, with winding pedestrian alleys overlooking the reddish tuff holes, shops and houses dug in the rock.
The frescoed dome of the village church.
The regional park where the fort stands.

Opened in 1993 in the seventeenth-century house Francioli to exhibit documents, reordered in the sixties by Ugo Francioli, on Giovanni Nuvolari and Carlo Francioli, figures of the Risorgimento mantua; he also exhibits tools and objects of rural life and a section on life and work in rice. Open on Sunday 9-12; guided tours only by reservation.
One of the cast fountains.

Country of the Val di Fiemme at the foot of the Latemar, with the Geological Museum of the Dolomites, seat of the MUSE, the museum of the Alpine School of the Guardia di Finanza and, on the road to Passo Rolle, the visitor center of Paneveggio in the Forest of the violins.
Appennino air on the Via Francigena.
Along the road between Sottoguda and Palue, the craftsmen work iron and wood: hand-painted wrought iron butterflies and beech and crystal jewelry.
Walk in one of the UNESCO baroque towns in Val di Noto.
The town's important building, remembered for hosting Giuseppe Garibaldi; today it houses the historical environmental museum of Val Cavallina.
Small characteristic church, destination of pilgrimages, reached with a simple walk through a green corner of the village.
The covered bridge over Ticino, perfect place for a walk at sunset, which connects the city to Borgo Ticino.
Sanctuary of Ceriana indicated among the places to see.

Venue of the National Roman Museum dedicated to urban archaeology, a journey of over two thousand years in the history of a block of Rome from ancient times to the Middle Ages; closed for excavations and restorations since 2023, with guided tours "open cantiere."
A memorial to the Great War.
White stone of Majella and noble palaces.

Cited in a papal bull of 1148, it was rebuilt from 1432 (date engraved on a brick) and consecrated in 1500; the facade and the current layout of the three aisles entirely frescoed dates back to 1846. Inside the "Trionfi" of Saints Faustino and Jovita of the Flemish (1621-1633), two altarpieces of Pompeo Batoni (1750 and 1763) and the mausoleum of Stefano Antonio Morcelli of Gaetano Matteo Monti (1828); the crypt of Sant'Agape is visited on request at the parish office.

City of the high plain of Treviso, capital of the sports footwear district: you can visit the Sportsystem Foundation Museum in Villa Binetti, the MeVe, multimedia memorial of the Great War in the complex of Villa Correr Pisani, and the Museum of natural history and archaeology; to the north you can reach the Bosco del Montello.

In the fifteenth century Palazzo Elti rebuilt after the earthquake: paintings and sculptures by Friulian and Venetian artists, including Cima da Conegliano, Pomponio Amalteo and Pellegrino da San Daniele, works of the seventeenth century and of hegemonic painters; open on Sundays.

Two granite blocks complexes, called "stones" or "stones," on a plateau near the highest peak of the Serre, reported in 2005: trilite structures with estimated blocks over 200 tons, pillars sometimes engraved with pictograms and possible walls. The investigations have not clarified its origin, perhaps anthropic, and are classified as geosites.
Thermal buildings on terraces overlooking the gulf; it includes the so-called Temple of Mercury, a room of Augustan age indicated as the first known case of large dome in cement.
The "delicacy" baroque Este, summer residence of the dukes, with frescoed rooms by Jean Boulanger, the fish pond and the park.

In Piazza della Pomposa, the church of Santa Maria della Pomposa rebuilt by Lodovico Antonio Muratori, parish priest since 1716, with works by Bernardino Cervi and Jean Boulanger; in the canon where he lived, the museum opened in 1931 with manuscripts, the writing desk, the librarian chair and numerous portraits.
It dates back to the 16th century and rises in the district Busache 'e josso, about 80 meters lower than the first nucleus of the village; the festival falls in mid May.
15th century frescoes in an oratory saved by the community.
Provence in Stura Valley, early summer.
In Villanova, the museum of civilization that took its name from this place.
Baroque altars in a cloistered monastery.

The island of the Faraglioni and Piazzetta: the imperial villa of Tiberio on Mount Tiberio, the 14th century Certosa of San Giacomo with the archaeological museum, the Gardens of Augustus above Via Krupp and the villas of the great foreign guests of the 20th century.

The town of Cicolano overlooking Lake Salto, the largest artificial basin of Lazio, created in 1940; above the village the Cenci Rocca, while in Borgo San Pietro rises the monastery of Santa Filippa Mareri, rebuilt stone for stone after the submersion, with its museum and works by Giorgio De Chirico.
The most beautiful view on port and coast.
A chapter in the history of architecture to be read with a critical eye.

In the underground spaces of the ancient Convent of San Domenico, it tells the seismic phenomena with attention to Calabria and Italy, from historical, anthropological and architectural perspectives. Designed by Schiavello Architects Office with architects Ciconte and Prestanicola, it has a room with corrugated wooden ceiling of more than a thousand pieces and a second environment, Scuri, with barrel vaults; it also hosts exhibitions and events.

Medieval village in a panoramic position about 19 km from Asti, known for the thermal springs of the Valley of the Fonti and the hills of Monferrato. Of the castle, destroyed in the seventeenth century, remains the tower rebuilt in Piazza Castello, now overlooking the vineyards up to the Monviso.
closed for restoration work according to Umbriatourism
according to the Touring open Tuesday-Friday 9.30-12.30, Saturday and Sunday only on request
Walk over a spring.
The Napoleonic ruins above the valley.
Memory of a country of emigrants.

In the capital of Balzo there are the round, circular palace of 1883, the Town Hall with the monument to the fallen of the Great War in bronze and marble and the adjacent Palazzo Taliani of 1834, and the Palazzetto Branconi of 1640, with the inscription "Invidia God" and not compassion on the architrave. The Palazzetto houses the Park's Environmental Education Centre, with museum, tour centre, nature trail and library.
Church with simple lines in the medieval old town.
A Cistercian abbey with 15th century frescoes.
From Himera lions to Bernini in a medieval hospital.

To the west from the tower follow Sa Tuerra, Porto Campana with its dunes, De su Sali and Su Giudeu, considered the most beautiful: light sand, dunes with centuries-old junipers and an islet reachable on foot thanks to the bottom; it is often set of films and commercials.

In the sixteenth century Palazzo Mocenigo, which includes part of the fourteenth-century walls of the Carrara castle, exhibits protohistoric finds of the Iron Age and Romans from the excavations begun in the second half of the nineteenth century in Este, Lozzo, Arquà and in Lower Padua, in a chronological and thematic path (daily life, cults, funeral rites) that closes with a small medieval and modern section. Among the main pieces the Situla Welcome, symbol of ancient Venetians, the funeral set of the noblewoman Nerka Trostiaia, a gold medallion coined under Augustus in 2 BC and the Madonna with Child of Cima da Conegliano (1504). Hours: Monday 8.30-13.30, Tuesday to Saturday 8.30-19.30, Sunday 14.30-19.30.

On the Piazza del Pistornile, in the upper part, it was born in 1817 from the transformation of the sixteenth-century college on a project by the architect Giuseppe Marchesi from Pavia. Façade in travertine slabs, bell tower half Romanesque and half Gothic, interior with three naves with frescoed central vault (restored in 1972) and 18th century main altar surmounted by a marble temple. Organ of the Lingiardi brothers, two eighteenth-century paintings, baptistery in polychrome marble, fifteenth-century sacristy with Gothic ribs and a Romanesque plaque in the wall of the rectory.
Built in the nineteenth century, it preserves the remains of Saint Gerard.

The 7th-century rock church, accessible from the churchyard of the sanctuary of the Madonna della Scala. The frescoes include a Virgin of the Good New Odegitria type of the late thirteenth century, a Christ Pantocrator with Deesis and a triptych with Saint Lucia, Saint Vitus and Saint Catherine of Alexandria.
Mount Peglia, biosphere reserve.

Water town on the first basin of the Lario: the Duomo with the dome of Juvarra and the Broletto, the Romanesque of San Fedele and Sant'Abbondio, the Voltian Temple, the House of the Fascio of Terragni and the walk of the villas to Villa Olmo.
The top of the valley.

Village of the Nebrodi on Monte Castro, overlooking the sea and the Aeolian Islands, with twenty-two churches in the historic centre and the local red marble everywhere: the temple of Hercules under the church of San Marco, the ruins of the castle of Roberto il Guiscardo (1061), the Badia Piccola with the Byzantine-Norman Museum and the churches with stuccoes of the Serpottian school.

The village with its suitcase, Roasio tells in the Museum of the Emigrant the departures of its inhabitants from the late eighteenth century, especially towards Africa; on a hill above Roasio San Maurizio remain the ruins of a medieval tower of the XII-XIII century.
Castrovillari, at the foot of the Pollino massif, is the largest urban center of the park and starting point for excursions and guided tours.

Municipality of the Riviera dei Fiori with the hilly village of Lingueglietta, among the most beautiful villages in Italy, feud of the Lengue: turned caruggi, the civic loggia and the church of San Pietro transformed into a fortress.
Among the most beautiful views in the world.
Main church of the village, at the top of the village, recognizable for the two unusual bell towers; it was built by the Counts of Tuscolo at the end of the 11th century and still dominates the town.
Messner and the Dolomites in altitude.
In the center of the village, 18th century building with monumental facade and richly decorated interiors.
The protected area of the Furlo Gorge extends also in the territory of Fermignano, with a landscape partly hilly and partly rough and rocky.
The oldest story in Elba.

The civic centre of Borgoricco is a multifunctional space designed by Aldo Rossi, one of the most revolutionary architects of the twentieth century: the project takes up the multifunctional role of the Venetian villa and its geometric shapes as well. It houses a large theatre and the Museum of the Roman Centuration and is barrier-free. In 2026 the project Visit Camposampierese proposed free evening openings on reservation with guided tour of the architecture.
The only remaining part of the sixteenth-century castle leading to via Pretoria.
At the end of summer, the Metaphysical Days offer guided tours

Theatre completed around 20 BC by the magistrate Gneo Satrio Rufo, capable of about 6,000 spectators, in the late-republish district of Guastuglia; the lower order of arches and some arches of the upper gallery remain standing, with the Antiquarium.
In the footsteps of pilgrims.

The only surviving part of the castle destroyed in 1216 by the Piacenza troops, rebuilt and sold in 1691 to Barnaba Belcredi; the tower in local stone blocks, attributed to the 14th-XV century, has a window at the top with the ancient inferriata. Tradition has it that it has long been a prison: inside were found strains of torture. It is private property, visible only from the outside from the highway.

In the Piacenza plain near the Po, Villanova sul'Arda is the land of Giuseppe Verdi: in the village of Sant'Agata there is the villa where the Master lived and worked, today passed to the State and temporarily closed, while in the village the monument to Verdi stands in front of the hospital he wanted; complete the visit of the church of Cignano and the river park of Isola Giarola.
The mountain where the snow was kept.

Heir of the Roman colony of Sinuessa, founded in 296 BC along the Appian Way, Mondragone preserves the remains of the city submerged at the Vagnole, the Fortress Montis Dragonis on Mount Petrino and an archaeological civic museum with finds from the Paleolithic to the Roman age.
Monastery with Romanesque pronao and single nave church with majolica floor.
The huts of the shepherds in dry stone.
Stone pedestrian bridge, one of the most picturesque in the Valle d'Aosta.
The Doria castle that acts as a theatre at the Festival of Harps.
Castlein Carnival masks.
The thirteenth-century church of the village.
The 15th century cross and the former vows of the lake.
From the first century BC, a rare example of a bridge with a single span (36.65 metres of rope, 5.82 wide), which can be walked from Via Roma; next to the Museo del Ponte Romano.
The culture of the stone of Ausonia.
One of the most evocative monasteries in Tuscany.
The historic center of the neighborhoods.
The city seen by the water.
The king's house.
€5, reduced €4; with Basilica €8, reduced €7
The tree-lined avenues with 84 busts of garibaldini of 1849, the monuments to Joseph and Anita Garibaldi, the lighthouse of 1911 and the cannon of noon fired since 1847.
The medieval village of Via Mercatorum.
The double façade on Piazza Cavour.

18th century villa with avenues and gardens of the 17th and 18th centuries, among the most important historical parks in the region; it houses the Institute of Agrosilviculture of CNR and, in the former lemon house, the PAAO Visitor Centre (CEA) with the faithful replica of the paintings of the Tomb of the Hescanas. The park welcomes horse riding, dog shows and the national juggling rally every year.
A nuraghe at a well-preserved altitude.
Squares and alleys of a Sabino village.
In a hidden courtyard the 28-metre-high spiral staircase, the most spectacular of Venice, with a view of the domes and bell towers.

Built in the fifteenth century on the wall: its bell tower was part of the defenses and under it passed the road of ringing. It overlooks Tschurtschenthaler Square, starting point of the historic tour.
For the organ of the eighteenth century.

Inaugurated on May 9, 1981 after a city delegation proposed on TV, at ...Portobello, to collect ancient accordions; it celebrates Paolo Soprani, who in 1863 founded Castelfidardo the first Italian industry of the instrument. It occupies over 500 m2 in a restored seventeenth-century wing of the Palazzo Comunale and exhibits 100 instruments chosen from a collection of about 500; according to Italia.it also houses a collection of Giuseppe Panini, the inventor of figurines.
Woods, hot springs and a path for all senses.
A Renaissance house.
A strong castle with frescoes from the fifteenth century.
At 1,272 m below Monte Porrara, it dates back to the fourteenth century, built by the Celestines, probably where Fr.Pietro Angelerio, the future Pope Celestine V, lived for three years.
Walk from abbey to abbey.

Set up in 2005 in the nineteenth-century premises of the former town hall and named after the archaeologist who studied the territory in the seventies and eighties, he exhibits funerary furnishings from the necropolis (on about 250 excavated tombs) from the VII to the fourth century BC, with indigenous geometric ceramics, red figured Lucan vases and a bronze helmet from the beginning of the fifth century BC. The Roman section includes loricated and togata statues and a female bust of the first century BC, stele and a funerary cippus with the Lucanian wolf.
The Walser village in the valley headboard, leads to the park.
€12, reduced €9, children 6-16 €6

Two distinct communities that form a single municipality, on opposite sides of the landslide of Mount Toc, with rosé local stone houses and spontaneous architecture; Erto is part of the Authentic Villages of Italy. In Erto for centuries, on Good Friday, it represents the Passion for a vow made after a terrible plague epidemic.
For a fee: rates on the official website

Canyon of the Matese Regional Park between Mount Erbano and Mount Cigno, excavated by the Tierno in limestone with walls in some points over 30 meters; a path with wooden walkways follows an ancient track Sannita and touches the Grotta dei Briganti, the Grotta delle Fate, the Grotta delle Streghe, the Belvedere, the Mulino di Zì Fiore and the Bridge of the Mulino, an ancient arched bridge used to reach the mill until the 1950s.
Built by Ruggero II on Mount Consolino, you can reach it with a panoramic path that starts from Cattolica.
A rare place of rock worship of the Roman age.

Romanesque church founded in 1271 in an ancient feud of the Guidi Counts; it houses an Assumption of the Virgin, a Last Supper of Sebastiano Viti and a Baroque organ. Next to it, the Diocesan Museum of Sacred Art is the center of the itinerary of the sacred art of the Ecomuseo.
Where the violin shop is still at home.
A spaceship of contemporary art.
Byzantine-Norman church of the 11th century with two chapels, a small decorated dome and two Norman portals with acute sixth.
An eighteenth-century church with an ossuary dug into the tuff.
The canyon is rugged and evocative excavated by the Frido stream; from Mezzana itineraries start on foot, on horseback or by mountain bike towards the Pollino massif.

Late Baroque church built between 1792 and 1796, with frescoes by Franz Altmutter, sculptures by Nissl and an altarpiece by Martin Knoller; on the left of the staircase a double gothic chapel of the fifteenth century, with the chapel of Sant'Anna on the upper floor and, below, the chapel of the dead frescoed by Simone da Tesido (open every day 8-17).

Borgo from ancient origins (35 BC), rich in archaeological remains, with a large medieval layout, entrance doors and narrow alleys; the church of San Cerbone is dedicated to the saint who took refuge there from Populonia in the 6th century.
Sand and surf waves on the Riviera.
The war on the Lagorai seen from the valley.
The old town is spread along the slope following the original medieval plant and culminates in the Norman castle, to which you climb for a ramp with the municipal coat of arms in porphyry stone.
Roman antiquities in a red house.
Two coves at the foot of the cliff of Numana Alta.

Open-air museum among meadows and woods born from the vision of the collector Egidio Marzona, who since 1989 invited artists to stay in Villa: site-specific installations made of stone, glass, steel and concrete by Mario Merz, Sol LeWitt, Richard Long, Giuseppe Penone, Bruce Nauman, Lawrence Weiner and Dan Graham, from Minimalism to Land Art, from Conceptual Art to Poor Art. Many works invite interaction and are suitable for children; there are no fences or tickets. It is part of the CarniaMusei network.
The millstone quarry.

Established in 1961 and opened in 1964 in Villa Majnoni, since 1977 it has been in the Municipal Villa of Crevenna; re-arranged in 1999, it tells the Alta Brianza and the Lariano Triangle in eight halls back in time, from the modern age to the geological eras. Among the pieces a fresco by Andrea Gentilino (1490), the wooden pulpit by Sant'Eufemia, a longobard spatha with silver-armed handle found in Parravicino in 1961, a Neolithic pile pole from the lake of Pusiano, remains of the cave bear from the lead hole and about 40 species of ammonites from the Turati Alps.
Valley where a totem marks the geographical center of the UNESCO World Heritage Dolomites; the path passes through the mountain hut of the same name and continues to the Falier Refuge (2074 m).
The eighteenth-century size of the basilica overlooking Piazza del Duomo, sober inside.
Giants' pots.
Cinema and photography in a dairy.
The sanctuary wanted by the Caetans.

Country of the Valley of Cembra 18 km from Trento, on a morainic terrace above the Rio dell'Ischion, known in the world for the red porphyry extracted in its open-air quarries: the Museo Casa Porfido and the square of San Biagio, paved with porphyry between the old church of the twelfth century and the new parish.
The Baroque Quaglio and the palaces of the merchants.
The abbey renovated by Vasari between 1565 and 1573, with its Coronation of the Virgin; it is located along Via Cavour, among the places of "Life is beautiful."
A Barocci in a village church.
The art of the Twentieth century Treviso.
The panorama of Valmarecchia is dizzying.

Built in 1604-1605 as the summer residence of Cardinal Ferdinando Taverna, then of Scipione Borghese, with the nymphaeum and the secret garden of Giovanni Vasanzio and a hanging garden; lived there for a long time Paolina Bonaparte. The Parisi family since 1896, is in the network of the historic residences of Lazio.
The sunrise east of Italy.
Tracks of the ancient ceramic floor.
Walk on the limestones between Maiella and the Sanniti Mountains.
A youthful solimena in an octagonal church.
The Ogliastra sky from one of the major public observers.
Posts from all over the world and 400 stamps never printed.
from December 2023 the archaeological collection of the ground floor of Palazzo Vassalli has been re-arranged in the new MOA (communicato Regione Puglia); check what remains exposed

The 17th century Church of the Immaculate Conception is adorned with baroque stuccoes; the Church of the Crucifix has a majolica bell tower and that of St. Augustine holds a 16th century painting of the Madonna delle Grazie.
The largest Gothic settlement in Italy, overlooking the lakes.

An ancient Roman settlement (statio) and example of thirteenth century architecture, described by the Park as a compact fortress city with walls and doors around church, noble palace and square.
