The Adriatic Sea explained to the little ones.
From buckwheat to pizzocchero.

From the panoramic point at about 750 meters the view ranges from the Ligurian Apennines to the Cozie Alps; coming from the Bricco della Colma along the ridge opens the unreal vision of the village dominated by the castle. It is the stage of the Great Langhe Crossing (GTL).
Pre-Roman walls and a single arch.
regional works on restoration and enhancement of the complex in progress (decree 1° SAL of 13/11/2024): verify access
€6 whole (with the Archaeological Museum); €4 reduced; free on the first Sunday of the month
A Gothic church with a 13th century statue.
The historic neighborhood, lively even in the evening.
Just below the viewpoint, with the Government Palace and the Risorgimento Heroes Monument.
A whole day in the green.

Founded in 1237 and rebuilt after the earthquake of 1349, with portal and sixteenth-century bell tower; the Gothic interior houses frescoes from the end of the fourteenth to the beginning of the fifteenth century rediscovered for a few decades (Universal Judith in counter-facade, Crucifixion and Annunciation in the apse, St. Nicholas who endows three girls), a polyptych of the Annunciation of 1483 maybe by Angiolillo Arcuccio and 16 stained glass windows of 1976 designed by Bruno Cassinari.
Marbles, canvases and the crib crypt.
From prehistory to the Mistrà Varnelli in one museum.
The sea of seahorses.
Restored historical building dedicated to comics, illustration and animation, with permanent exhibition, temporary exhibitions and workshops.
The top of the village, where the castle was.

In the locality Campo, where tradition places the battle of 267 BC narrated by Livio and where the Castrum Trebarum stood. On April 27, 1655, during road work desired by Cardinal Girolamo Colonna, the fresco of the Madonna on the throne with the Child and Saints Peter and Paul re-emerged; the church was consecrated in 1707 and repeatedly restored after the earthquake of 1915. A unique nave with frescoed apse by Luigi Leggeri, a coffered ceiling of the early twentieth century and a double staircase that descends to the crypt with the fresco; the Madonna del Campo has been patron saint of Cave since 1880.
Church founded in the 16th century and rebuilt in monumental Baroque forms, with canvases of Ligari and Petrini. At Christmas hosts the event Christmas Art.
The organ Serassi and the woods of the court church.

The monument symbol of the city, well preserved and decorated with reliefs: it celebrates the Emperor Trajan and marked the exit of the Via Appia Traiana; in the Middle Ages it was incorporated into the Lombard walls.
Romanesque oratory in the shelter.

National monument built from 1609 to 1644 and rebuilt after the earthquake of 1693 between 1699 and 1705: the façade of Angelo Bellofiore has a frieze with fourteen putti, the balustrade of 1754 bears statues of characters of the Old Testament and the frescoes of Pietro Paolo Vasta (1732-1736) adorn transept, choir and dome; among the canvases the San Sebastiano in glory of Michele Vecchio. The museum includes the rooms of the Treasury with silver and liturgical gold and the eighteenth century crypt with vestments, wooden statues and Sicilian paintings.
An open-air sculpture museum.
Sacred art in a 16th century church.
A small chest of frescoes along the Sempione.
The early Christians of the Albani Hills underground.

The tower on the main square was built between 1240 and 1259, when the Templars held the fortress; the clock, moved from the door of the baronial palace, was placed there at the beginning of the nineteenth century. It houses the permanent exhibition "Homo sapiens e habitat" (Homo sapiens and habitats), started in 1978 by the Ecology Centre of the Quaternary: five rooms on the general prehistory and the Circeo, with human and animal bones, instruments and tools from the caves of the promontory.

Considered one of the most important Carolingian monuments in Italy, it is a remarkable example of architecture of that time. It is part of the virtual tour of the historical sites of the municipality, with historical notes and audio narration usable as audio guide on site, also in English and German.

In a manor house of the sixteenth century with loggia on a courtyard closed by a wall, in front of the square of Nadro: educational exhibition on rock art and Camuni culture, with reconstructions and panels and, since 2022, two rooms on neolithic weaving and on ceramics with documentaries and finds reconstructed in experimental archaeology; it houses unique ticket office and information of the Reserve, bookshop, library-archive and refreshment area. Open all year round, closed on Tuesday, December 25 and 26, January 1 and Easter: from April to October 9-17:30, from November to March weekdays 10-14, Saturday and Sunday 9-16; accessible to people with disabilities.
Sanremo flavors.
The sea of Lanusei, between pebbles and mining archaeology.
The frescoes of Lanave.

Built in the 12th century as a Romanesque church for the population, in 1735 it was transformed into a bright late Baroque and Rococo ambience; the Romanesque round bell tower has an onion dome, a spiral façade and statues. The frescoes of the vault, by the Tyrolean baroque painter Christoph Anton Mayr, show theological allegories and scenes of the life of St. Michael.
Cavour Fortress.

It was built around 1332 in Gothic-Catalan forms and preserves from that time the bell tower with two-fold windows and the chapel of the Holy Spirit (1430) with the reliquary of the Sacred Spina (1636). The current Baroque church of 1669, is the work of Angelo Italia and Giuseppe Diamante, with three naves divided by monolithic columns of red marble; the facade is of 1786 (Emanuele Cardona). Between 1735 and 1737, the Flemish Guglielmo Borremans frescoed the vault with 38 scenes; he preserves the Crucifix (1523), the marble triptych (1519) and the "Transito della Vergine" (1529) by Antonello Gagini, the Last Supper by Giuseppe Carrera (1614) and the statue of the Madonna dei Miracoli by Lorenzo Curti (1721), carried in a procession on June 21. Basilica since 1969; in 1995 Paolo Portoghesi designed the chapel of Don Giuseppe Rizzo.
A noble house inhabited, with its collections.

On the cliff overlooking the village, the acropolis was the last stronghold of the city of Circei; polygonal walls are preserved on top and in the historic center, dated from the sources between the VI-IV century BC. (VisitLatium) and the beginning of the third century B.C. (Circle Park).
The Dominican Gothic.
The "city of flowers" of Valdinievole, home of vivaism; in its territory Collodi, the village of Pinocchio.
The dreamer of "Amarcord."
The Domus de Janas World Heritage Site at the gates of the city.
Walk through the city of foundries.
Built with the remains of the temple of the god Silvano, in a centuries-old wood of holm oaks and oaks.
Heir to an ancient 12th century church.
The walled castle of the threshing.

Dedicated to the famous geodes of Tiso, formed for volcanic activity over 290 million years ago, with rock crystals, smoked quartz, garnets and other alpine minerals: it is the collection of a life by Paul Fischnaller. A short film introduces to the formation of the Alps and minerals; on Tuesdays and Thursdays, by reservation, you go with Fischnaller to look for the geodes.
Low water ideal for families.

Opened in 2005 in the former Cornino dairy, it exhibits wooden rakes, wicker baskets, tools and household items produced in the area before the 1976 earthquake, when wicker and rakes were the main craft; sections on cheese making, spinning wool and cooking, sometimes with demonstrations of craftsmen. Open on Sundays, other days upon reservation.
On the same square of the Madonna, the church rich in paintings and paintings next to the town hall.
In a 19th century town hall, opened in 2018: furnishings of the indigenous necropolis of the Locride (Canale Ianchina, Sant'Onofrio dell'età del Ferro) and private collections Scaglione and Candida.

Built between 1513 and 1587 on a project attributed to Vignola, with the fourteenth-century bell tower that was part of the first walls; inside a painting by Domenico Fetti and an ivory box of the fifteenth century.

Built by Acquaviva d'Atri around 1300, damaged in 1447 and rebuilt in 1474 by Giovan Francesco Azzolino with works directed by Baccio Pontelli; restored by Giuseppe Sacconi in the late nineteenth century. Irregular quadrilateral plan with corner towers, central courtyard with 22 meters high well and cylindrical mast; it is entirely open to visitors and houses the archaeological museum "La Fortezza nel tempo" (inaugurated in 2016) and the Museum of ancient weapons.
The Egyptian section also surprises those who do not love archaeology.
Very ancient parish, of which we have already heard since 1143; in its territory, near the hamlet of Villa Oneto, there are the remains of the ancient Abbey of the Nativity of Our Lord.
Built in 1900 on a project by Martin Dülfer, in Art Nouveau and Classicist style; open during the events.

In August 1875 thirty prisoners and seven officers landed in Cala Sinzias to clean up a marshy territory; the colony arrived to accommodate more than two thousand people, with workshops, joineries, hospital, pharmacy and post office, and closed definitively in 1956. Today you can visit the building of the management, which houses on two floors the museum of the territory on the history of the colony and the traditions of the Sarrabus, the prison structures, the villa of the director with garden, the church of San Basilide built by the prisoners at the end of the nineteenth century and the historical cemetery.
The art of the churches of the valley gathered in a palace.
The temple of the Jesuits.
The smallest theatre in the Marche region.

Designed by the architect Romolo Squadrelli with the engineer Luigi Mazzocchi on commission of 1902, it was inaugurated in summer 1904 to attract the clients of Vichy and Carlsbad; among the guests of the Book of Guests are Queen Margherita of Savoia, Pietro Mascagni, Eugenio Montale, Salvatore Quasimodo and Federico Fellini. The central body of seven floors is crowned by a dome and the façade is decorated with frescoes, stone sculptures, wrought irons, caryatids, putti and festoons; the 250 rooms already had elevators, electric light and telephone. Closed in 1979 and bound in 1984-85, it was the subject of a structural restoration planned between 2015 and 2019; it is private property. In front, Prince Umberto Bridge in reinforced concrete of 1924 replaced the temporary bridge of the yard.

Former clay quarry closed at the end of the seventies, with geological layers of marine origin partially rich in fossils; after the abandonment it was reclaimed in the nineties by Colacem with the planting of 8,000 trees. In 1999 the Fossil Park and the Malacological Museum of Clays were born, set up in a farmhouse of the seventeenth century: one of the very few examples in Italy and in Europe of the recovery of a quarry abandoned for scientific and educational purposes.
The stars above Pesaro.
One of the most beautiful and documented images of the Wild Man, figure of Alpine mythology.

It preserves two wooden altars with seventeenth-century anchovies by Fantoni di Rovetta, the main altar in inlaid marble (1743) and in sacristy two fragments of fresco of the fifteenth century with St. Anthony Abbot and St. Bernardino.
The UNESCO walk of the chapels above the lake.
The MiC card indicates closed every day and no source reports the times: contact the museum

The streets of the village are decorated with murals on rural life and on the passion for music; since 1986 the international organ festival is held every August and about 120 mantice instruments are exhibited all year round.

At about 1,000 meters near the Passo dei Casoni, documented from the twelfth century and built around 1100 by the Benedictine monks of Borzone as a monastery and hospice for pilgrims; Romanesque, of the Malaspinas since 1500 and returned to the Church around 1800. Surrounded by a pine forest with a panoramic path from the Apuan to the Apennines and picnic areas; open every Sunday.
Among the Roman sites to see having more days, along with the villa outside the walls.
Going up via Garibaldi, in an ancient building already mill, the museum dedicated to the olive tree and its oil.

The ten villages (Bals, Celle, Chiazale, Chiesa, Fontanile, Masdelbernard, Pleyne, Prafouchier, Ribiera, Sant'Anna) retain traditional stone and wood architecture, with round columns in masonry up to 10 meters high, among woods, pine forests and alpine pastures.
The Romans' writings on the walls.

Park on the Vallone d'Aquino, reclaimed and renovated, with views of the surrounding nature and the local caves of travertine; it is part of the complex of the House of San Tommaso and is open on request.
Built in 1812 in Piazza San Giovanni Bosco, at the end of Corso Garibaldi, it survived the earthquakes of 1894 and 1908.
Romanesque and Baroque intelvese in the same church.
The fine sandy coast with the marina, which is the backdrop to the old town.
The theatre dedicated to the musician from Legnaghe.
€5 whole; €7 during exhibitions (until 9 January 2027)
Amaretti.
The Bourbon city designed in chessboard.
Samnite warriors.
Free beaches; establishments with fee

Baroque church in the district of Lera, rebuilt in the seventeenth century for a vow linked to the plague of 1630; it has three altars in local marble and the altarpiece of the Addolorata of Biagio Falcieri. Around, the historic districts of Fontana, Lera, Vigo and Fontechel with stone houses and rural architectures.

Established by the Municipality in memory of the violins Nicola (died 1978) and Vincenzo De Bonis (died 2013), he exhibits guitars and mandolins of the two brothers and their students. The Biignanese violin garden has its roots between the 12th and 13th centuries and has developed mainly since the 18th century.
The only Moai that exists outside Easter Island, 6 meters high, carved in the local pepper by eleven Maori indigenous.
On Piazza Orsini, it houses the silver palace of Nicola da Guardiagrele and the polyptych of Jacobello del Fiore; the bell tower is about 50 meters high and in the crypt you worship San Berardo.
A peak on the Costa Verde.

City of hemp and ropes founded according to tradition in 850 by refugees of Miseno, Frattamaggiore has its heart in the Basilica of San Sossio, a national monument with Romanesque crypt that preserves the relics of Saints Sossio and Severino and the Sansossian Museum of sacred art.

The castle chapel houses small artistic gems: painted from the 17th to the 19th century with religious scenes that give clues to the owners of the castle. During the restoration there were unknown inscriptions that recall dramatic events of the seventeenth century with at the center a woman venerated as a saint. It can be visited only with a guided tour in German (10-10.30, from May to October); it still hosts celebrations of the liturgical year.
Getting in there is a twist.
Most of it in the plan
Garden designed by landscaper Ludwig Winter, with a rich collection of palm trees.
The Sangallo Palace with prisons and hanging garden.
The painted cloister.
The ambo with Jonah and the Arab majolicas.
A splendid example of the Venetian Renaissance in Piazza del Duomo, seat of the Venetian rectors and today of the Prefecture.

Wash-basin built between 1903 and 1905, where women washed wool: a rectangular block with three arched openings framed in granite and two rows of tanks. On the proposal of Maria Lai it has become a small museum: the frame on the ceiling of the same Lai (1982), the fountain that sounds "by Costantino Nivola (1987), the fountain of the wheat" by Guido Strazza (1989) with the mosaic of the churchyard and "The fountain of the spring" by Luigi Veronesi. From the wash room starts the ring of Sa Tappara, just over 2 km.

Villa Odescalchi Greppi (today Villa Santa Chiara) dates back to the 16th century; the Galaterale, near Piazza Motta, carries the coat of arms with the swan of Parravicini; Villa Ida Parravicini of Persia preserves Baroque frescoes; Villa San Benedetto Menni, built around Villa Bassi Roncaldier, is surrounded by a large Italian garden. The complex of villas was opened for the FAI Days of Spring 2021.
The oldest building in Sottoguda, consecrated in 1486, with bell tower of 1550 and altar of 1616; only to be saved from the fire of 1881.
A Sacred Mount in miniature, with statues of human size.
The rare circular brick plant.
Contemporary art in the Roero.
A rococo urn and a Roman history of the 1800s.
Decorations of the early twentieth century and the cave of Lourdes.
The early Christian mosaics on Timavo.
The lake of the Bolognese mountain.

Trekking from the plain to the Tyrrhenian, from Quattro Castella and Canossa to Luni along the valleys of Enza and Magra, renewed in 2004 by the Province of Reggio Emilia that cares for it with the CAI; marked white-red, has a stage point in Vetto (Crongolo-Vetto and Vetto-Camporella).
€20, reduced €2; free on the first Sunday of the month

Central monument built on the lakefront in the 1920s, designed by Giancarlo Maroni, the architect of D'Annunzio and Vittoriale; an interactive and multimedia route for adults and children explains how water becomes energy. Guided tours by reservation, in Italian, English and German.
Romanesque church of the 11th century, partly rebuilt in the 13th century, reachable from via della Pieve in the village of San Pantaleo.

From the center there are many paths to woods, mountains and alpine pastures; among the recommended are the ring between Malga Cerenedo and Malga Fossa di Bena, 9 km round trip with 300 meters of altitude difference, with shorter or longer variations. In Fossa di Bena you buy goat cheese produced on site.

Fortress already mentioned in a papal bull of 1215, from 1257 of Count Ugolino della Gherardesca, lord of Cagliari, immortalized by Dante; after his death (1288) passed to Pisa, in 1324-26 to the Aragonese and feudal families, until the ransom of Vittorio Amedeo III of Savoy in 1785. It climbs on three levels along the volcanic hill: the door with the surviving central tower, the village with accommodations, stables and cisterns, the cistern tower (the name comes from a spring in the rock) and the mast with drawbridge, underground cistern and terrace with Guelph merlons; in the tower, according to tradition, Vanni Gubetta was imprisoned, accomplice of the betrayal of Ugolino. Visits every day 10-18, without reservation.

Dedicated to the fossils of the Bolca field, studied for centuries: the didactic path explains the techniques of extraction and the process of fossilization, and two aquariums recreate the sea covering the area about 50 million years ago, with a tropical-subtropical coral reef and a warm temperate coast. Open every day 9-12 and 14-18.30; barrier-free (prices updated to 2023).

Devotional path of the end of the sixteenth-early seventeenth century on the slopes of the hill: six chapels designed by Vincenzo Scamozzi and built between 1605 and 1615 imitate the Roman basilicas ('Romanis Basilicis pares') and keep canvases of Palma il Giovane; the path ends in the church of San Giorgio, already oratory of the Duodos, which exposes the bodies of martyrs including Valentine's Day. Hours 9.30-11.30 and 14.30-17.30.

Fortified village built in the 12th century on a hill on the right of the Tenna, of which there are traces of the walls, towers and three original doors; you enter from the Porta di Santa Lucia and go up along the terrace system to the church of San Francesco, passing from the Town Hall and the neoclassical temple of the Clock (Casa delle colonne) next to Palazzo Leopardi. Outside the walls there are sixteenth-century tower houses.
The bridge of Musmeci.
The Gonzaga stage square overlooking the Po.

Symbol of the village, built on the rock and inhabited by Norman lords, Swabians, Angevins and Aragonese, had mainly military function and was declared national monument in 1902. The most imposing part is the Torrione; the towers of the Pier and Parasinno, well preserved, are joined by a walk still accessible. Once surrounded by a moat with a drawbridge, it has a central courtyard with an octagonal cistern for rainwater; legend has it that in the dungeons there was hidden a shaving mill for thieves. Tel. +39 0881 963433

Roppolo appeared in 963 in a diploma of Ottone I as a court with a castle-tower in the center; the Glasses rebuilt it in the thirteenth century adding the porch to two arches, and the coffered ceilings are fifteenth century. Passed to the Savoys in 1427, it was of the Valperga until 1837, when Ignazio Anselmi transformed it into a country residence; from 1981 to 2015 it hosted the Regional Enoteca della Serra. From the courtyard and the terrace you can enjoy the panorama of Lake Viverone and the Canaves lakes.
The baroque inside to surprise.
The oldest stones in the Diano Valley.
An unusual museum.
In Pessione, created by Lando Rossi di Montelera della Martini & Rossi next to the vermouth plant.
The tower started in 1482 to strengthen the defences of the castle at the entrance of the village.

Melegnano, mentioned already in 333 A.D. as ninth miles from Milan on the Lambro, is dominated by the Medici Castle, born as a "receptum" in 1243, fortified by the Visconti and transformed since 1532 by Gian Giacomo Medici, with frescoed rooms in the mid-500s and the civic collection Don Cesare Amelli; in the center the minor basilica of San Giovanni Battista preserves part of a altarpiece of Bergognone, and the city is known for the Fair of Forgiveness of Holy Thursday, linked to the bull of Pius IV of 1563.

Caves dug into the tuff where the tomb of a Sannite warrior was found, perhaps involved in the battle of the Caudine Forks (321 BC); they are also related to the story of a woman accused of witchcraft.
The majolica of Burgius.

Small museum born in 1973 from a local initiative and expanded in 1981, in the solitary valley of Rodoretto: a hundred objects on the job and daily life in the mountains, with environments such as kitchen, room, cellar and school. Visits to be arranged by telephone.
visits by telephone (tourist site of the Municipality); the MiC card indicates every day closed
The treasure of the Valenzan confraternities.
The reserve where most of the sea salt of Trapani is produced.
A church all of tuff that merges with the gravina.
The lighthouse to the far west.
Church of the 14th century that preserves the statue of Our Lady of the Coroncina and the fresco of Our Lady of the Rose.
Museum in the historic center with the finds of the peucet and Roman necropolis of the territory.
The Civil Antonelli.
Romanesque plain.
A sea of gold.
The Sorrowful Madonna of the Fantoni shop.

Probably erected between 1320 and 1330 on a ridge about 90 meters above sea level, it is one of the few examples of Gothic on the Sorrento Coast; Baroque façade rebuilt between 1773 and 1792, bell tower sixteenth century. Three naves on pillars of tuff, pentagonal apse with ridge vaults, the Annunciation of Giuseppe Bonito (1733) on the high altar, a wooden crucifix of Giotto's school and the urns of Gaetano Filangieri and Bishop Cimino. Cathedral until 1818, reopened in 1995 after the earthquake damage of 1980.

Borgo della Valnerina which preserves intact the medieval structure, with walls and doors of the fourteenth century and towers of the fifteenth century, and the tradition of hemp told by the Museum of Hemp; in the territory the Romanesque abbey of Saints Felice and Mauro at Castel San Felice and the fortified villages of Case and Gavelli.
The viewpoint of the village and the narrowest street in Italy.

Founded by the Sicani, called Batraliah by the Arabs and Petra Heliae by the Normans, the village turns between Piazza Loreto (the highest part, probably the seat of the Sican and then Roman fortification), Piazza San Michele with the circular fountain, Piazza dei Quattro Cannoli with the Baroque marble fountain of Billiemi (the only water source of the village until the eighteenth century) and Porta Seri, last of the six ancient gates, of Norman origin. Three belvedere: Loreto ('u castru') towards Etna, Enna, Caltanissetta and the Impera valley; Carmine towards Palermo; Piazza Duomo towards Gangi and Etna.
The garden of the Dukes of Este next to the center, with the Vigarani Palazzina and the tree-lined avenues.
In winter (1 November-30 March) hole and spas are covered and not visible: call the Antiquarium to know if the covers have been removed
Walk along the grand-ducal arches.

Founded in 1050 as a Benedictine monastery by monks of the abbey of Fruttuaria, from the end of the fourteenth century it was fortified by Del Carretto, then six-seventh-century residence of Della Rovere and Polleri of Genoa, which in 1876 gave it to the Municipality, today owner and with the town hall on the noble floor. The noble floor is home to the Gipsoteca "Edoardo Rubino" with the plasters of the Piedmontese sculptor, the attic temporary exhibitions, the mastic the "Torre dei Cavalieri" on weapons and medieval costumes; in the cellars are aged wines of the Langa Astigiana. In 2026 Sunday openings from May to November: guided tours at 15 and 16 (about 1 hour), theatricalized at 11 and 17 (about 1.5 hours); reduced with subscription Musei Piemonte.
A surprise in the woods.

City of Alto Milanese linked to the battle of 1339, remembered by the church of Sant'Ambrogio della Vittoria, and the cabinetmaker Giuseppe Maggiolini; in the center the square with the parish church from the façade of Piermarini and Villa Maggi Corvini, on the borders the sanctuary of the Madonna of God 'l Sa.

Medieval gate with two arches, also called Torre del Belvedere, is what remains of the ancient fortified complex of the village; the walls, marked by crenellated towers, are still visible. In the walls there is also a second door, the Medieval Gate.
MiC: MUdeF rooms temporarily closed for maintenance of multimedia equipment
Veronese Romanesque church of the XII-XIII century with tripartite façade and rose window that recalls San Zeno Maggiore, three aisles and raised presbytery.
The home of the Cologne Water.
The tools and crafts of the calena countryside.

At the end of the eighteenth century Count Giampietro Annoni bought the land and entrusted the villa to the Genoese Giuseppe Zanoja, also known for the façade of the Duomo of Milan; presumably completed in 1809, since 2007 it hosts the Town Hall after the restoration of the frescoes. The park of 23 hectares, built between 1819 and 1825 as an English country garden, is the second in Lombardy for extension after that of the Villa Reale di Monza: a perspective telescope leads to the Ionic temple erected after 1825 in memory of Count Alessandro Annoni, and along the avenues you will meet the coffee house, the house of the deers, the artificial cave, the pond and the greenhouse-limonaie fifteen arches, with over 160 tree species including cedars of Lebanon of the original plant. The municipality opens it freely (from 25 October to 31 December 2026 every day 9-18.30, closed in case of rain or wind); guided tours with the Cultural Guides Association of Cuggiono.
The starting point of the Right Po cycle path.
The fourteenth-century tower of the Palazzo Pubblico, 88 meters high according to Terre di Siena: you climb on foot, to contingent groups, up to the view over the whole city.
A Roman city still locked in its walls.
different times between sources (SMPP: Mar-Fri morning and Sunday afternoon; ISPRA: every day 9-19 by reservation), house 1 or 11
The Romanesque basilica outside the city towards the sea, marked by Visit Tuscany among the attractions of the territory of Pisa.

The villa of the Pamphilj and then of the Torlonia, residence of the Mussolini family from 1925 to 1943 and today public park with the Casina delle Civette, the Casino Nobile, the Casino of the Princes and the Serra Moresca.

The city of Giacomo Leopardi: the birthplace with the library, the garden of the Infinite reopened by the FAI, the places of poetry and Villa Colloredo Mels with the paintings of Lorenzo Lotto; also the city of tenor Benjamin Gigli.
White sand and sea lilies.

The municipality of the upper Val Borbera on the border with Liguria and Emilia, whose territory coincides with the Natural Park of the Upper Val Borbera (2019): ruins of the castle Malaspina Fieschi Doria on Monte Carmo, abandoned hamlets like Reneuzzi and Casoni and the Ecomuseo dei Sette Ricordi.
The costumes are in miniature.
The Baroque square designed by Bernini.
The caruggio of the Fieschi between arcades and shops.
The Tessa Group explained, free and family-friendly.
Woods and moors a stone's throw from the train, on foot or by bike.
The queen of the Viterbo fountains.
The elevated passage wanted by Cosimo I in 1565, from the Uffizi to Palazzo Pitti above Ponte Vecchio.
The vow against the plague signed by Vittone's school.
A fifteenth-century oratory with its processional crucifix.

Built between 1923 and 1929, long private and adapted to cinema, acquired by the Municipality in 1995: atrium with late Art Nouveau decorations, horseshoe room with three orders of loggias and remains of the decorations of the ceiling and the archo scene.
Visible from the outside are the side rooms of the tepidarium and the calidarium; the octagonal room with niches for the cold baths is partly collapsed due to the instability of the ground.
Walk in the covered passages above the walls.

Medieval cathedral, bishop's seat, in the historic center; from the sacred area under the cathedral are the Roman finds of the civic museum. On August 14th it is the starting point of the great procession where sixty bearers hold the statue of the Assumption on top of a 16 meters high tower.
The Garda from the most elegant shore.
Malatesta and Rizzi in the parish church of the village.
Ancient residence of the Knights of Malta in Piazza Plebiscito, now home to the civic museum and, at times, an art gallery.

Municipality of the Upper Maira Valley, in the Middle Ages the capital of Ugonotti: in the hamlet Villa the seventeenth-century church of the Annunziata with the Museum of Sacred Art in the Confraternita, in Chialvetta the ethnographic museum La Misoun d'en bot and, towards the French border, the springs of the Maira, Chiappera, the Provençal Rocca and the waterfalls of Stroppia.
The oldest part of Finale, a medieval village still surrounded by the walls with towers and doors, now known for its artisan workshops.
Among the oldest beech trees in Europe, a human heritage.

Founded in 1956 by Gruppo Grotte Gavardo and then sold to the Municipality, it occupies a fifteenth-century building in the historic center and tells about the Valley Sand and the western Garda area from the Middle Paleolithic to the post-Renaissance age, with fossils and a section of paleontology. Among the finds are the skeleton of a bear of the caves of the Hollow of the Friar, materials of the pile of the Lucon of Polpenazze (part of a UNESCO site) and the Roman necropolis of the Lugon of Salò. The exhibition itinerary is being reviewed.

Romanesque church on a low hill about two kilometers from the village, near the thermal baths and a Roman amphitheatre, built around 1100 by the monks Vittorini on a early Christian crypt; the murestenes around are animated by novenanti for the festival of late August.
The Abruzzo suede from the viewpoint of the village.
At the end of the sixteenth century, a nave with octagonal coffered vault and seventeenth-century altar in polychrome marble.

Monumental complex of villas and park among the most representative 18th-century villas of Lombardy: the current aspect is due to the architect Giuseppe Piermarini, in a style close to the Reggia of Monza; in the nineteenth century it was restored Pelagio Palagi and at the beginning of the twentieth century Luca Beltrami performed minor interventions. There were guests Ferdinand IV of Naples and Umberto I. On the first floor sculptures and drawings by Giuseppe Scalvini; in summer, since 2012, the park hosts the festival Â"Parco TittoniÂ" . The park has been a candidate for the FAI census on several occasions.

Romanesque cathedral with mosaic in façade, rebuilt at the end of the 13th century: in the apse the Stories of the Virgin frescoed by Filippo Lippi between 1467 and 1469, inside the bronze bust of Urban VIII of Bernini and the painted Cross of Alberto Sotio of the 12th century.
Walled village of Valdichiana Aretina, extraordinary example of medieval urbanism with concentric rings.
Walking and cycling path on the old railway of Asiago, from the Millepini Park to Tresché Conca, with views of the villages of the plateau.
The Romanesque at the entrance of the city.
The porticoed square of Gaetano Koch with the gardens of 1888, the Trofei di Mario and the Porta Magica, the seventeenth-century remains of Villa Palombara linked to a legend.
19th century theater entitled to Yves Montand (Ivo Livi), born in Monsummano.
In the Palazzo Mercantile, seat of the merchant magistrate established in 1635 the museum documenting the history of the fairs of Bolzano.
A shrine in the pine trees.

Fortified complex (VI-XVIII centuries) on a hill overlooking the Tagliamento valley, with crenellated walls, mast and towers; after the earthquake of 1976 it was restored again the last phase, of the seventeenth century. The church of St. Peter (1246) is annexed, where the archaeological excavations with the phases of the building are visible. Free admission without reservation according to the Superintendence.

Cittadina dei Monti Prenestini was born from the medieval Castrum Cavarum, linked to the sculptor Lorenzo Ferri, whose civic museum preserves the gipsoteca and the Monumental Nativity with statues of over 4 meters; outside the village the Sanctuary of the Madonna del Campo and the Park of Villa Clementi with the Fountain of Santo Stefano.

Established in 2009 in the Cilento National Park: posidonia prairies, the flysch of Cilento with stratified and colored rocks that host groupers, moray eels and lobsters, and an underwater archaeological heritage. In San Marco, the Roman breakwater submerged in the ancient Greek-Roman port is visible at the modern port; off Punta Licosa the remains of a maritime villa and the cargo of a Roman ship sunk in the first century BC, with more than one hundred vinarian amphorae.
"A fortress and two churches," according to Umberto Eco: the Fort on a cliff at 639 meters where Cagliostro, the Pieve and the Romanesque Cathedral died.

Church of the XIII century at the cemetery, Romanesque plant with Gothic elements added later: a frescoed bezel with Our Lady, St. John the Baptist and Jesus and, in the apse, a cycle of frescoes with a Last Supper.

Monotorre del Bronzo medio (XV-XIV century B.C.) in the old part of the village, between the houses: trunk-conic, 12 m of diameter and about 10 m of residual height, in blocks of shale with false dome; a corridor of 4 m leads to the circular chamber, with a cistern in a cell, and a staircase of 17 steps rises to the terrace. Reused as a burial in Byzantine times, it dominates the valley of the Flumendosa with a view up to Gennargentu. It is accessed from the ethnographic museum.
The tables of the Bagetti on the Napoleonic countryside of 1796, in a castle with views.
Walk through the ruins of the castles of the foothills.

The museum is set up in the fourteenth-century parish church of Saints Peter and Paul, in an elevated position, with terracotta portal and travertine rosette. It houses a large fifteenth-century fresco of the Last Judgement, a wooden statue of St. Peter of the second half of the fourteenth century and the reliquary-ostensory of the Holy Cross in golden silver, chiselled in 1488 by the goldsmith ascolano Pietro Vannini; in the crypt of the Addolorata, perhaps of Farfense era, traces of frescoes attributed to Vincenzo Pagani and Vittore Crivelli. Opening on request outside the scheduled periods: €4 per person with guided tour.

Built in 1772 on a project by Domenico Schiavi and completed in the following century, with frescoes by Antonio Schiavi and paintings by Francesco Pillizzotti, follower of Nicola Grassi; the main altar in white marble was donated by Jacopo Linussio in 1747.
Village life carved into stone.
The Gothic in a village.
Historical center of remarkable artistic and architectural value; along Via Roma follow the forms of the Lecce Baroque and in the center stands the eighteenth-century Palazzo Baronale Capece.

Villa of 1715, known as "Villa dei Monstri" (Villa dei Monstri) and already the Grand Tour in the eighteenth century: the walls are decorated with statues of monsters, dragons and caricatures carved in Aspra stone; inside the Hall of Mirrors and rooms with mythological frescoes. Times indicated by the source: 1 April-31 October 9-13 and 16-19, 1 November-31 March 9-13 and 15.30-17.30, every day.
The Gonzaghesque parish church with the seventeenth-century cantoria.
The nature of Frignano inside the castle.

A neoclassical church built between 1853 and 1858 on a project by Alessandro Antonelli, with four granite columns pronao and dome on the main altar; decorations by Luigi Morgari (dome and apse, 1898) and polychrome windows by Giovanni Da Re (1927-1943), including the It preserves an Immaculate Morazzone and a altarpiece of the Madonna enthroned attributed to Bernardino Lanino.
The Saluzzo Renaissance.

Pieve of medieval origin on a site rich in Roman finds, almost overhanging the Dora along a stretch of the Via Francigena. The Romanesque façade probably dates back to the second half of the twelfth century; the building was later renovated in Gothic forms, with the semicircular apse replaced by a square. Next to it, the chapel of San Biagio preserves traces of frescoes. Opening on request at the cultural office (tel. 011 9670217) or the UNECON association.

Municipality of Sarrabus, autonomous since 1986, born around the penal agricultural colony founded in 1875 and today museum; 13 kilometers of coast with beaches like Cala Pira, Cala Sinzias, Marina di San Pietro and Costa Rei, and behind the Oasis of the Seven Brothers with the Arch of the Angel.
The farmhouse brianzola in scale 1:10, up to the details.
Our Lady of Mercy of Pagani.

Scenographic church on the square, funded by the heirs of the Prince of Butera and completed only at the end of the nineteenth century, with a monumental facade with overlapping orders and typical crowning of the Sicilian baroque.
The summer palace of the dukes of Parma.
The lion of San Marco in Alto Molise.
Hypogeal tombs of the necropolis canosine, stage of the archeotrekking routes together with the necropolis of Pietracastuta.
A hunt for the towers.
It brings together places, objects and events related to the exile of Levi: guided tours, itineraries in the places described in his writings, shows, exhibitions and the literary prize.
The archaeological history of Trino.
The little theater.
The village of the ax masters.
Monday closed; daily hours on the site of the Civic Museums
Dedicated to a woman of humble origin who in the postwar period gave burial to over 700 victims of the war.

The path Karol Wojtyla starts from Pisoniano and climbs to the Sanctuary of Mentorella; along the route you will find the eighteenth-century church of Our Lady of the Snow, which houses an image inspired by the Salus Populi Romani, celebrated on August 5.
Franciscan spirituality with sea view.
Inaugurated in 1977, it houses the painting "The Miracle of St. Pantaleo" by Andrea Lusso (1595), already altarpiece of St. Pantaleo, and the statue of the Dormitio Virginis of the 14th century.
Perfumes and products that are not found elsewhere.
Two great Sienese churches, marked by Terre di Siena among the places of worship of the city, along with San Domenico and the Baptistery.
Frescoes from the Vissana school.

Above the country, recovery aviaries and settings with veterinary surgery for injured birds: four cages for specimens no longer liberable and a large aviary where those healed train before release, often public. You can see from close up the royal eagle, buzzard, pilgrim falcon, kestrel, scatter, astore and allocco; they must be approached in silence without touching the nets.
A Gothic cathedral made of live trees at the height.
Palazzo del XVIIIcento, now home to the town hall, with Baroque decorations and halls frescoed by Mozzoni.
The cathedral next to the Papal Palace.

18th century neoclassical building with a T-shaped plan, with a private chapel dedicated to Our Lady of Loreto and a dining room with French wallpaper from the early 19th century of the Lefevre paper mill of Isola del Liri.
Already of the monks of Sant'Antonio Abate, consecrated in 1467 by Piero del Carretto; marble saintly waterworks of 1484 and a baroque crucifix of the Margliano school.
The Museum of the "Cittadella nicolaiana" is the complex of the Basilica of St. Nicholas, which contains works and documents related to the history of the basilica and the worship of the saint.
The whole story of Chioggia and its lagoon in one museum.
The Renaissance frescoes of Pellegrino da San Daniele.
work on recovery and restoration, access by reservation (tel. 0981 68088)
A stop in the historic center.
Art and archaeology next to Giotto.
Dunes 12 meters above sea level.

The old town, called "Sciscola" is a name of probable Arab origin meaning maze, is an intricate of tuff and white facades. The village, in a privileged position on the valley of Ofanto, on the Park of Alta Murgia and on the nearby Basilicata, is called the "balcony of Puglia" (Puglia), according to the tradition part of the name derives from a temple of Minerva on which the village arose.
Holy art and ancient books in the cloister.
Stories of departures from Lucchesia.
The villa that preserves the Teatro delle Acque di Carlo Maderno.
The shape that dominates the Santa Valley.
Four monumental tombs in a row under Gennargentu.
The findings of Ozieri's culture.
Salts and workshops linked to traditional puppets, with the Carolingian cycle and stories of saints and brigands.
Fifteen centuries of underground history.

Borgo dell'Alto Monferrato near Ovada, fief of the count Gentile since 1498 and 1745 of the Pinelli Gentile, who still live in the castle. The castle, with its 10th century tower and wine cellars that have been making wine for five centuries, dominates the medieval village with its ancient churches.
Observatory run by volunteers who follow migrations: 312 species of birds have been recorded in the area, with days dedicated to birdwatchers and natural photographers.

It was first mentioned in 1037, and was entrusted to the Benedictines of Cavour Abbey until 1315 and to the Augustinians from 1529 to 1802. On the façade there is an ancient sculpture of the Lamb with the Cross, perhaps from the 11th century.
Set in an ancient mill, it is dedicated to olive oil, one of the main products of the area.

The museum occupies the first floor of the villa, built between 1718 and 1724 by the de Brandis, family documented in Cividale since 1226, and donated to the municipality with all the furnishings by the countess Catherine, last descendant, died in 1984. The picture gallery has about seventy paintings from the fourteenth to the nineteenth century, with names like Jacopo da Bassano, the Domenichino, Francesco Solimena and Pietro Longhi, next to wooden and furnishings from the sixteenth to the nineteenth century, about thirty eighteenth-century prints, landscape frescoes attributed to Antonio Picco and grotesques of the late nineteenth century; library and family archives are in the adjacent Civic Library. Visit by appointment, reservation required (tel. 0432 939590).
A bath in an ice lake in the hills.

Small lake fed by springs at the foot of Mount Cairo, which for centuries refurbished the ancient Aquinum; in the sixteenth century the Boncompagni princes regulated its waters (the Aquinas Forms) to reclaim the plain. About 3 hectares of wetland, since 2017 part of the Natural Monument of Aquinum established by the Lazio Region; also accessible to people with reduced mobility, with some more difficult points.
the MiC card indicates it temporarily closed to the public, works to be re-arranged in new headquarters
The headland of the Roman fleet.
The 17th century door carved and the Annunciation.

Naturalistic Museum of the Pollino National Park which presents the characteristics of the UNESCO Geopark, with paleontological finds of the ancient local lake basin (Elephas antiquus, rhinoceros, hippopotamus, hyena); it was born from the Il Nibbio association, founded in 1998 to recover the abandoned houses of the historic center.

About one hundred works by Italian and foreign artists, including sculptures by Giorgio De Chirico and Francesco Messina and stained glass windows by Aligi Sassu and Remo Brindisi; it hosts exhibitions, presentations and conferences.
Sienese painting outside the city.

On the banks of the Mingardo in the Devil's Gola, under San Severino, you can bathe at the foot of the railway viaduct made of red bricks of 1928, with eight arches, in service until 1965; the upper viaduct is walkable.
One of the most beautiful panoramic points of the Terre di Faenza.
Inside the dome.

Founded in 1611 by the inhabitants with the patronage of Prince Vincenzo Capano, it has the cloister, a frescoed refectory and a single nave church with four altars on its side, three with the Capano coat of arms; the paintings of the ceiling are attributed to Nicola Malinconico, of the school of Luca Giordano, the wooden chest of drawers is by Giuseppe Marrocco da Celso and the stucco by Pietro Sernicola. On July 2 the statue of Our Lady of Graces comes out in procession.
Starting point for all museums.
In the ancient heart of the city.
The treasure saved from the earthquake.

In the deconsecrated church of San Domenico (1571), part of a Dominican monastery known as "su cunventu" , tells the linen from the cultivation to the fabric: ceremonial male and female clothes, festivities, daily newspapers, for mourning and for children, and in the side chapel and in plowing sacristy, gramole, combs, spindles, warps and frames; the path closes with local linens and embroidery. Organizes laboratories to pass on the skills related to linen.
Laste's Gothic Alpine.
It's a long-winding cycle.
A founding city of 1939 to read on foot.

Labyrinth of caves and galleries connected, for tens of kilometers, dug from the Middle Ages in the pepper under the historic center to obtain building material; for centuries there were preserved barrels of wine and in war served as anti-aircraft shelters. Some galleries have been cleaned up and transformed into an exhibition path with the finds of the restorations; visible the walls with the eruptive phases of the Lazio volcano. Guided tours all year round on weekends, by reservation at Archeoclub Colli Albani.
The Gothic-Aragonese mother church of the country.
The Roman Tortona in a palace in the center.
The memory of the work on Trasimeno.

In Rabbi Fonti, about 1,200 m in the Stelvio Park, around the Antica Fonte that flows at about 9 °C: carbonate-alcalino-ferruginous carbon water known in Europe already in the seventeenth century for digestion, circulation and anemia; in the nineteenth century the plant expanded and attracted the Habsburg nobility. Today hydropinic treatments, baths, inhalations, mud, Kneipp route in thermal water, sauna and alpine sauna outdoors, with itineraries of the "Terme e Natura" and forest bathing. Open in summer (2027: from May 28th to September 19th), treatments by reservation.
A fairy tale neighborhood.

The church of the Confraternity of the Trinity was rebuilt in 1576 on a fifteenth-century structure; in 1591 it was granted to the Hermits of Sant'Agostino, whose former convent preserves the cloister and a small crypt for mummification with masonry channels and decorations, restored in 2000.
In the fifteenth-century villa of the Guinigi the history of Lucca among Etruscan finds, medieval sculptures and Renaissance paintings.
The sunset on the roundabout of the pier.
The 17th century parish church of the village.

In the former sacristy, the Robbian temple of the late fifteenth century rebuilt as it was in the church, the relief of the Della Robbia with the delivery of the relic, processional crosses of the sixteenth century (one by Piero di Martino Spigliati, one attributed to the workshop of Benvenuto Cellini), the seventeenth-century reliquary of the Holy Milk and illuminated codes.
He tells of Leonardo's lost fresco.

Borgo on a hill at the eastern entrance of the Matese National Park, with the Norman castle built on polygonal walls Sannite, the convent where Padre Pio made the novitiate and Casa Sania, cultural center with garden and outdoor theater; in early January the living nativity scene.

In the Fortress of Cassero, a fortress built by the Sienese between 1382 and 1384 and attributed to Bartolo di Bartolo, with the Porta Fiorentina. Established in 1989 and reopened with a renovated itinerary from July 1, 2025, documents the country's ceramic tradition: ceramics of daily use of the Seven and Nineteenth Century (broaks, scaldini, pots for pasta) and productions of the local factories Giotto, Lapucci and Aretini; also exhibits a wooden crucifix from the fourteenth century, the Marzocco in serene stone of 1506, sixteenth century sculptures, finds of the excavations of the Fortress and the picture gallery of the Mercy with paintings of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
The church on the hill.
Municipal Museum recognized by the Lazio Region, dedicated to engraving and medal art.
The historic curtain.
Goethe described it as a clean, lively town.

The castle is mentioned for the first time in a Longobard document of the tenth century and was certainly a fortified building in Norman age. Today it houses the Historical and Archaeological Museum of the Civilization of Oil and Wine.
Deep gorge dug in a rocky jump upstream of the stone bridge of Betenda, reachable by a walk near the Tornalla.
The arched portals of the village of the ora.
River forests and over 200 species of birds along the Orba.

Built in 1330 by the Anguissola, as evidenced by a plaque on the main tower, then summer residence of the Landi marquis: rectangular plan with front to the east, two large towers with alternate corners and a massive angular tower, well preserved. It is private and can be seen only from the outside; the seventeenth-century chapel opens only on special occasions.
The Ligurian peasant life of a time.

Founded in 2001 by the artists Vittorio Amadio and Marisa Marconi, who have recovered part of the former Sacet complex, collects paintings, graphics, sculptures, ceramics and photographs of local, regional, national and international artists; it also hosts exhibitions, concerts, conferences, poetry readings, projections and dance performances.

On the hill of Pulsano, on rocks of more than 200 meters, founded in the sixth century according to the tradition of St. Gregory the Great; 24 hermitages depend on it dug into the rock, connected by paths and steps. Opened to worship in 1997.
The district of Riborgo established as a ghetto in 1696 and opened in 1784, today with antique shops along the Beccherie street; in via del Monte the museum of the Jewish community.
The Moretto and the Calegari in a large church of the eighteenth century.
One of the richest campaigns in prehistory.

The building takes up the façade of the first Ford Italia headquarters in Trieste (1923) and inside reproduces the assembly line of the Ford model T. It exhibits vintage cars, including a Cleveland type A of 1897 and an Oldsmobile of 1902, motorcycles, bicycles and about a thousand objects, from measuring instruments to transceivers, including the full radio station of a Soviet ship. Open all year on request.
Medieval house in Runaz, today exhibition venue.
Our Lady of the monastery and the memory of Newman.
The card of the Municipality indicates the access as "Closed": it is seen only from the outside
The two red municipal towers next to the bell tower of the cathedral, the thirteenth-century tower of Casa Cazzulini and the tower of Palazzo Vecchio, symbol of the city.
the MiC card (Add. 2021) indicates closed every day: check opening with the Municipality
Built in the 15th century in memory of the presence of St. Francis in Cannara and the foundation, according to tradition, of the Third Order in 1221.
Sacred art in an 18th century church.
The façade has a large central rose window that illuminates the interior, where there is a suggestive mosaic.

Small town of Astigiano, born in 1416 around the castle of Pelletta, which preserves medieval walls of the 14th-XV century; on the nearby hill stands the church of San Pietro in Vincoli, rebuilt in 1709 and a long pilgrimage sanctuary.
The symbolic place of the rebirth of the Italian army in 1943.
The devotional heart of the upper Seriana Valley.

Borgo with porticoed streets paved with pebbles, tower, square and churches, linked to the Marquis Morozzo della Rocca: the castle was born as a fortress and transformed into a palace in the seventeenth century hosts the Provincial Historical and Ethnographic Museum "Augusto Doro" on the peasant civilization.

Coastal Lake of the Circeo National Park, of biological, naturalistic and archaeological interest, inhabited by herons and garzettes: calm waters for kayak and stand up paddle, boat trips, nature trails and birdwatching.
The intact rural landscape of the valley.
Large green area of about 53 hectares, indicated by the Abruzzo Region among the places to visit.

An inscription dated 1497 the present form, which replaced an older structure; a stone column with cross bears the date 1096 and the pulpit, work of local craftsmanship, is from 1880. Two aisles, the largest divided by arches to the sixth and vaulted with fragments of frescoes, including a Deposition, putti in stucco and altar major in marble; the most precious works are no longer in the church.
The ceiling was carved and gilded at the beginning of the seventeenth century by the French sculptor Leonardo Scaglia.
The porticoes of the medieval market.

In the great sacristy of the church of Santa Croce, originally a hospital, the furnishings of the procession of the Dead Christ of Good Friday: the coffin of 1626, the base of the Addolorata, the white cross of Santa Croce, two eighteenth-century street lamps and a sixteenth-century table of Sant'Egidio Abate.
Medieval ruins and a Tiarini in parish.
Remains of a small hermitic sanctuary where in the 10th century St. Nile of Rossano retired in prayer, on a steep slope near the stream St. Elijah, about 1 km from the church of St. Adriano.
A rocky site that is a typical necropolis with a sicule grotticelle, important evidence of the prehistoric attendance of the territory.
A rare place of contemporary art.
The octagonal dome.

Historical and Ethnological Museum of over 30,000 m2 with 15 pavilions on bridge reclamation, landing of Anzio and battle of Cassino, in two routes (War and Agriculture) with a pavilion of vintage toys.
The ace museum house was born in Lugo, with its aircraft and relics of the Great War.
The most visited mural of the Spanish Quarter in via Emanuele De Deo, in the heart of Largo Maradona.

Under the castle, the square hosts the sculpture in travertine and bronze by Gabriele Jagnocco inaugurated in 2011, dedicated to St. Thomas and the miracle of herring, with its symbols: herring, olive branch, books and the profile of the castle.
The Medma terracotta, the pride of the Magnogrec choroplasty.
Three valleys in one look.

Castle of the 11th century, documented with certainty from the second half of the thirteenth century, when it was subject to Perugia; it was for centuries seat of the Visconty, the county and the municipality, passed to the Trinci di Foligno, then in 1495 to Perugia and from 1560 to 1616 to the Bentivoglio counts of Gubbio. It remained the municipal seat until 1867, when with the opening of the railway station the administration moved to Valtopina. The well-preserved tower, which housed the town hall, Mount Frumentario, the guard body and the prison, the walls and the castle church, lies below the village called Casa Coccia.
Sacred art of the village collected in a restored church.
The three surviving towers of the castle on the Po.

Volcanic massif of 270 km2 between eleven municipalities, with the peaks of Trebina Longa (812 m) and Trebina Lada (795 m), woods of holm oak and cork, Mediterranean maquis, wild boars, foxes and deer and re-introduced deers. Pau rises about 300 metres on its western side. Free entrance.

Museo dell'Arciconfraternita di Maria Santissima del Monte Carmelo, in two sections: sacred art, with liturgical furnishings and vestments of Messinian and Neapolitan workshops of the 18th and 19th centuries, and archaeology, with finds from the Eneolithic to the Byzantine-Norman age.

Opened in 2003 in a former mill near the rocky settlement, it gathers about 3,000 objects of the peasant and rocky life of Zungri, in sections dedicated to the home, to the work of the fields, to traditional crafts, to the weaving and production of wine; a room is furnished as a vintage bedroom, with devotional images, daily men's and women's clothes and wedding costumes.

Castle built in the fourteenth century by the Dal Verme family, who ruled the territory; around it develop the houses of the village. The original complex remains the tower and a sandstone building with a 19th century portal; today it houses the town hall.
At the intersection of the Roman roads.

Opened in 1999 in a building dating back to the early nineteenth century next to Villa Faina, the museum has four rooms on the geology of local eruptions: Venanzite, lava rock with almost unique composition, a dinosaur egg from China and the skull of Elephas southernis found in the surroundings. The open-air park is about 2 km long on the large venanzite casting, partly emptied in the 1970s, between cones, craters, casts, rare minerals and the remains of a millstone quarry.

Building of the late eighteenth century born as a convent of the Clarisses and then became town hall. On the ground floor, obtained from the inner chapel of the former convent, the small horseshoe theatre with the audience and gallery designed in 1834 by Fausto Gozzano, father of the poet Guido; was inaugurated on 16 October 1864 by the Philodramatic Amateurs.
It preserves the Last Judgment painted by the brothers Torresani between 1552 and 1554, extended on three walls until the time and restored in 2026.
The symbol of Castel di Tora on the lake.
The peasant frescoes of Biancolini.
The nineteenth-century parish church and its painters.
Renaissance-style palace, probably begun in the 16th century, with frescoed rooms in the mid-18th century and Italian garden. Visit by appointment.
The Great Synagogue, one of the four active in the 12th century, transformed into a church under the Angevins (later Sant'Anna), now a section of Jewish art of the Diocesan Museum.
Art from the nineteenth century to today.

The town of Varesotto sul Ticino, dominated by the Visconti Castle of San Vito, inhabited by the Visconti and rich in collections; in its territory there are also Volandia, the park and museum of the flight, the Dams of the Panperdute on the Ticino and the paths of the Brughiera del Vigano in the Ticino Park.
Monferrato eras.

Municipality of the lower north-eastern Reggiana, from the fifteenth century to 1776 small autonomous manor of the Sixes; between the eighteenth and twentieth centuries it was known for the inlaid furniture, the 'roleini', documented today by the Museum of Tarsia, while the center is gathered along the portico of Corso Repubblica with the church of San Zenone.
Two public gardens overlooking the lake.
The museum in Enzo Ferrari's birthplace, with the yellow hooded gallery showing racing and road cars and telling the life of the founder.
The tower that preserves the last trace of the castle of Frederick II.

The imposing manor dates back to the first half of the thirteenth century (Visit Cuneese indicates 1241, at the behest of Thomas I of Saluzzo); destroyed in the wars of 1357-1363, it was rebuilt by the Marquises of Saluzzo between 1363 and 1378. In 1604 he passed to the Solaro di Moretta, who took the title of Counts of Monasterolo, and in the seventeenth century the salons were painted and decorated. Massif building adorned with turrets and interrupted by a large tower, it is of the Municipality since 1928 and hosts the municipal offices; it is visited by reservation.
The hydraulic work of the Emperor Claudio.
Chamois and waterfalls in the heart of the Park.

Mountain village whose castle was destroyed in 1502 by the troops of Vitellozzo Vitelli; the church of Santa Maria houses a Madonna with Child in glazed terracotta of the fifteenth century. Good starting point for summer excursions.
A Romanesque church on the roof of the plateau.
Sacred art and music.

Baroque three-nave church of the architect Giacomo Del Sole, built between 1726 and 1760. The main altar decorated in pure gold preserves the relics of the patron Saint Honorius; it preserves frescoes attributed to the Cavalier d'Arpino and a sacristy with wooden sculptures.
The cathedral on the sea.
The medieval quarter of the bridge houses is joined by covered passages and reached by external stairs called "profferli" (profferli) and Via San Pellegrino is a stretch of the Via Francigena.
The Clarisse and the Solimena.
The rite of the most felt fire of the Amiata.

Active since 1978 thanks to the building offered by the Morandi Bonacossi family and the private collection of GioBatta Meneguzzo, it is a permanent museum of contemporary graphics from the 1960s to the 1990s: over 1200 works by 700 artists including drawings, art prints and multiples, from the Informale to the Trans avant-garde through Pop Art, kinetic art, Nouveau Réalisme, conceptual and poor art, American graffiti artists and German neo-expressionism. Audio guides, guided tours and bookshops.

Designed by Lorenzo Porciatti in neo-Gothic style, with pointed arches, double-fores and triple-fores on the facade, a small tower and double-ceiling roof; it stands on the foundations of the previous Palazzo di Giustizia. It hosts the City and the tourist information office.
The park of the dukes.

Theatre housed in an ancient abbey renovated from 1847 on a project by G. Perreau, with decorations by the painter Bertolotti; inaugurated on October 8, 1853 with the Attila di Verdi, was named after the composer in 1901 and reopened in 2006 after decades of closure. It has horseshoe stalls, three orders of stages and loggia, for 330 seats; it is visited during the theater season.
The altar tied to the biscuit of the abbess.
Probably built on the ruins of an Etruscan temple, with its facade and rose window.
some rooms, including the frescoed chapel, which can be visited only by appointment

Samnites to Longobards.

Small ski resort of the Upper Val Sangone with snow-making programmed: descent (2 red and 1 black slopes, 3 lifts) and cross-country (2 blue slopes), plus snowshoes, bobs and sled trips suitable for all ages, with equipment rental.

Ancient parish between the moat to the west of Castel Tirol and the Grabbach, on the hill already inhabited in prehistoric age; the legend wants the church built by a people of dwarves and on the churchyard stood one of the oldest baptisteries in the area. Inside Romanesque frescoes and paintings pray.

Marble group of the Genoese Bernardo Mantero on the promenade, erected as a sign of gratitude to the king who granted the island to the tabarchins: the central statue was inaugurated on 16 July 1786, the two lateral additions in 1788 for the fifty years of the foundation.

The ancient Signia, Volsca and then Latina, on the Lepini Mountains about 60 km from Rome, twinned with Mycena for its cyclopean walls: the Saracen Gate, the church of San Pietro on the podium of the temple of Juno, the Nymphaeum of Quinto Muzio and the Archaeological Museum compose the urban archaeological Park \Segni Città-Museo Â .
Real caves in the woods.

In the Palazzo degli Agostiniani, in a single room that was the lower church of San Nicola di Bari, the association Â"Pozzo della PolentaÂ" exhibits about one hundred pieces: instruments for weaves and rows, 38 reproductions of Renaissance costumes, alabards, banners and palios of the Contesa. It's part of the Cultural Places card.

Documented since 1309, with first pastoral visit in 1511; in 1692 it had 11 altars. He kept the icon on the table of Our Lady of Graces, 1428, attributed to the Salerno school of Andrea Sabatino, crowned after the request of 1795 to the Vatican Chapter; at the entrance two ancient paintings with the Last Supper and the Madonna of Carmine. The bell tower, about 47 meters high, is attributed to the Vanvitellian school; on the first Sunday of July the statue of the Madonna goes in procession.
Guinigi's 45-metre tower, lords of Lucca, the only private tower that remains intact: 230 steps to the hanging garden of holm oaks on top.

Mill of 1806 in the valley of the Sorna, among the few traditional mills still working in the region: a large wheel with boxes and a smaller one in iron, used to grind feed for poultry farming. It offers educational and demonstration visits.
The small 19th century theatre in the centre of the village called the barn of the Malatesta.
18th century parish church, with a 51-metre-high bell tower, the highest of the diocese of Tortona.

The most populous municipality of the Valle d'Itria, known mainly for its Baroque architecture: from the Doge's Palace you enter the center from the Porta di Santo Stefano and walk along Corso Vittorio Emanuele to the Basilica of San Martino and the semicircular Piazza Maria Immaculate; in July it hosts the Festival of the Valle d'Itria.
The crypt on one ancient column.
Ancient books in a castle.

Village on the Molise hills of Lombard origin, with a historic center remained intact and set up as an open-air museum of Molise peasant memory, between murals and bronze statues. Outside the village the Badiale Sanctuary of Our Lady of the Annunciation and woods with views of Montago and Matese.

Salzano, where Giuseppe Sarto was parish priest from 1867 to 1875 before becoming Pope Pius X, houses the Museo San Pio X, the Filanda Romanin-Jacur of 1872 with its multimedia museum, the romantic Roman-Jacur Park and the nineteenth-century church of San Bartolomeo.

Itinerary easy from Pianosinatico, 7 km round-trip in about 1 and a half hours, for Le Voltate, Campetti, Cioppeto and Pian degli Ontani up to the summit; along the road a beech called "tree of fortune" is called.
On the hill of Quart, it preserves remains of the first human settlements of the Aosta Valley.
The polyptych of Giovenone and the Romanesque bell tower.

The old town, with alleys and elegant shops, overlooks the sea; the beaches are spacious and spacious and there is no shortage of rocky coves for those who love a more wild sea. On the promenade bars and restaurants offer pesto and stuffed anchovies, and in the center the freshly baked focaccia. IAT office in Lungomare Kennedy 10 (tel. 010 9127581).
Built after 1218 on a small square of Corso Garibaldi.
The walls and towers of the Malatesta castle in the center of the village.
The marbles attributed to Pietro Bernini.
An entire country that tells the work of the fields.

Granite relief covered by a centuries-old holm oak, Faunistic oasis with mouflons and panoramic summit. At about 700 meters rises the large nuragic complex of Sa Dom'e sa nì (the house in the snow) with towers, walls and circular structures, then used to preserve the ice; under the eastern ridge there is the nuragic village of Arcu 'e sa Tuppa.
The history of Prato textiles between frames and turbines.
The Roman city under the library.
Autumn browns and ancient songs.
Twenty workshops to review the crafts of the past.

Wanted by Francesco Gonzaga as a former vote for the end of the plague, designed by Bartolino da Novara (architect of the Castle of San Giorgio in Mantua), started in 1399 and consecrated on 15 August 1406; basilica minor since 1907. The Gothic-Lombard interior with a single nave houses a wooden frame with 53 polymaterical statues in niches, numerous ex-vote, the mummified crocodile hanging at a time and, in the first chapel on the right, the mausoleum of Baldassarre Castiglione by Giulio Romano. Bertolucci shot a scene of ... nine hundred.

The promenade along the lakefront, partly suspended on the water, runs along the old houses of the old town and the Liberty villas and from the embarcadero reaches almost to the Swiss border; it offers views over two branches of the lake and the mountains around. Just outside the station, the railroad's railroad-traveling iron pier is preserved on the water, reminiscent of the first line with electric trains in Italy. From the boat start the boats for the tour of the lake, also with themed cruises; dogs allowed on the leash.
A church linked to the plague of 1575.
closed for the winter break from 1 November 2026 to 15 March 2027, reopens on 16 March 2027
The other hot cave.
Single ticket to be verified; annual subscription €16 with unlimited entrances; in the Firenze Card
A city of Magna Grecia to travel.

Baroque Church of the Confraternity of Death and Prayer, which buried the abandoned dead, built since 1693 (a project attributed to Mattia de Rossi or Carlo Fontana) and survived the bombings. Greek cross plan with elliptical hall, stuccoes from 1699-1703, wooden statues from the seventeenth century, the dome frescoed by Giuseppe Errante (1786-1788), a balustrade of the organ obtained from the prison of St. Peter of the Battle of Lepanto and the neo-Gothic chapel Guglielmi with monument of Giulio Tadolini.
The hill that houses the great golden statue of Christ the King.
The monumental oak under Mount Ascension.
The covered market of the old town, marked on the official map of the city next to Piazza del Popolo.
The Romanesque with the matrons.
A 17th-century mill still working.
7th century BC archaeological site inside the Canalazzo Forest Park, suitable for hiking and cycling.

Set up at the Sanctuary, it exhibits reproductions and preparatory cartoons of the works realized in the various editions of the Meeting of Our Lady. Open Friday 15-18, Saturday and Sunday 10:30-12:30 and 15-18; other days by reservation (tel. The Commission shall adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 3 of this Regulation.

Parish established in 1415; the new church, built between 1720 and 1732 and consecrated in 1760, was born from a project by Guarino Guarini (the wooden model of 1691 is in the museum) modified by Filippo Juvarra. The vault of the choir is frescoed by Carlo Borsetti (1727) and that of the nave by Giovanni Milocco; in the presbytery five great paintings by Lorenzo and Giuseppe Avondo (1839) on the life of San Giacomo, a marble altar of 1809 designed by Giovanni Molino and organ of the early seventeenth century. Bell tower of 1595 of the masons of Alagna. Visits by reservation with the association    \Campertogno, art and culture Â (tel. 366 3719002).
An eighteenth-century palace for exhibitions.
Looking at the stars on a confiscated asset.

In an olive grove, hundreds of faces carved in the rock and trees by Filippo Bentivegna (1888-1967), who lived there in hermitage for about half a century; it is among the most visited sites in the province after the Valley of the Temples.

A 15th-century church that, with the monastery and the crypt, forms a complex of historical, artistic and architectural interest, declared a national good of archaeological interest; it rises in the homonymous hamlet, lower than Casamale.

The fishing village made famous by the Malavoglia di Giovanni Verga preserves its marina identity in the marina with colored boats and nets, with the seafront between clubs and terraces on the sea, the Baroque church of San Giovanni Battista and the fish market; for the patron is held the feast "U pisci a mari" (Pisci a Mari), which recalls the fishing of the swordfish.
Wooded area that extends also in the municipalities of Calitri, Bisaccia and Monteverde, Site of Community Interest pursuant to the Habitat Directive.

About a thousand finds divided into a naturalistic section (mineralology, zoology, paleontology) and an archaeological-ethnographic one, with 780 prehistoric lithic artifacts coming almost all from the Saharan area.
The old glass.
In the forest visitor centre: the naturalistic museum, a house of the rebuilt lumberjack and the enclosures of deers and mouflons, with 14 marked paths.

A small town on the Tyrrhenian coast dominated by the sixteenth-century castle of the Spadafora family, also known as Castello Samonà, now restored by the Region and used for cultural events; on the hill the village of San Martino, of ancient origins, with its churches.

On the hill of the same name, 571 meters, about 30 minutes from the center, at an ancient castle: built in the fourteenth century, enlarged in 1506, with a single nave with protyrus and polygonal apse. The oldest nave contains fourteenth-century frescoes by artists of the Venetian, pre-Jotan and Giotto school; the apse is frescoed by a Renaissance Friulian painter from the school of Domenico da Tolmezzo. Visits in the summer on scheduled days and times.
An unusual visit inside the castle.
The temple of speed.

Set up in the nineteenth century Palazzo Comunale, it exhibits finds of the territory from the end of the third millennium BC to the high Middle Ages; the main nucleus is dedicated to the culture of Golasecca, of which the museum has one of the most complete collections, with materials of the Gallic, Roman and Altomedieval era and fragments of the Benedictine church of San Donato (first half of the IX century). Since 1994 Pliocene fossils of Cheglio di Taino have also been exhibited. The municipality indicates opening from Monday to Thursday 9-12 and 14-17, Friday 9-12, Sunday 15-18 (with guide on Sunday afternoons and holidays), Saturday closed.
Gothic castle reachable with a hike.

Monastery commissioned in the seventeenth century by Cristina di Francia on the pre-existing Palazzo di Bernardino (1614), on a project by Maurizio Valperga; the eighteenth-century extension and the portal are by Filippo Juvarra. The main cloister, of 1719, measures 70 by 54 meters and has a portico of 112 columns in stone of Chianocco on which the fifteen cells of the monks opened; on the whole also the church of the SS. Annunziata con le Tombe dei Cavalieri e l'Aula Hospitalis. From 1856 psychiatric hospital (the one of the "memorato" of Collegno) until 1978, it is now restored and houses offices, university classrooms and events such as Follia in Fiore.
River area along the Rhine.
Designed by Rodolfo Vantini, with white marble facade of Carrara.

Built by Cosimo I between 1561 and 1564 as a defensive outpost and residence for visits to the marble quarries, in a valley with the Apuans in the background: UNESCO heritage with the other Medici villas.

Second necropolis of the Pantalian type of Sicily, with 288 grotticella tombs dug in the rock, used in the IX century BC and reused in archaic age (VI century BC); excavated in 1949-50 by Luigi Bernabò Brea, the finds are at the Museum Paolo Orsi of Syracuse. It remains a stretch of the ancient paved road.
The fifteenth-century building of Trivento's accounts.

Eighteen centuries under the floor.
Built in the eighteenth century according to the design of the architect Francesco Maria Preti, it preserves paintings from the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries on the life of the saint.

Municipality of the Pollino National Park not far from Diamante and the Riviera dei Cedri, known for its medieval stone town of Grisolia, with its houses leaning against each other, and for the beaches where the rare sea lily blooms.

Birthplace of Peter Mitterhofer, inventor of the typewriter, at the gates of Merano: the museum dedicated to him, the waterfall of almost 100 meters in the Natural Park Tessa Group, the Royal and Imperial Museum of Bad Egart in Tel and the World train of Rablà.

Built in Norman age, perhaps on a Byzantine structure, on the hill overlooking the village. In 1255 it was defended on behalf of Pietro Ruffo; an angioin garrison since 1275, a document dated 1276 describes its towers, a wall of about 80 meters, three cisterns and the churches of St. Nicholas and St. Catherine. In 1313 he resisted the Aragonese attack for a long time before being punished together with the country.
The island of the trap, to walk.
The altarpiece of the Bottani.

Walk on the water.

The museum, commissioned by Bishop Vito De Gristis and inaugurated on July 6, 2005, is set up in the rooms below the Cathedral of Santa Maria Assunta, once a burial place, and exhibits works of the Cathedral and the churches of the diocese, considered among the oldest in southern Italy.

The ancient Rocca Bertalda, twin Rocchettine on the other side of the gorge, still inhabited by a few residents: door of 1601, stone palaces, excavated alleys and houses leaning on the medieval walls; open all year round.

In the village there are workshops of wrought iron processing and restoration of antique furniture.
Monument with scenes of the Passion of Christ decorated with shells and colored ceramics of different eras.
Climbing Monte Porrara offers a magnificent view; Palena is known as the village of the orchids, with 64 species reported in the municipal territory.
The fourteenth-century Crucifix by Pietro da Rimini.
A medieval abbey with crypt.
The loggia of the sixteenth century.
