The Montecuccoli Dovehouse.

City between the Vesuvius and the Gulf of Naples dominated by the Reggia commissioned by Carlo di Borbone in 1738, today home of the Department of Agriculture of the University Federico II, with the large park, the botanical garden and the museum center MUSA.
The Gothic Town Hall.
Tiziano and the pavilion of the pope.
The Visconti fortress with the Bramantino Museums.
Rocca, museum and panorama on one visit.
The Gallura peasanta before tourism.

The village, of about 350 inhabitants, consists of three medieval districts and historically lives of shepherds, timber and charcoal; until the First World War it was a place of trade with Austria. On weekends, Vico's trattorias, including the Trattoria Bianca (since 1901), offer the "capovallese spiedo" cooked with coal and wood fire; in the shops there are local products such as Tombea cheese.

The centre of Alta Irpinia of Lombard origin, collected around the ducal castle, which was the residence of Giovan Battista Manso, friend of Torquato Tasso, and today houses the Civic Archaeological Museum with the Iron Age equipment of the hill of Cemetery Vecchio.
The main church of the village.
Walking on the streets of Picentia.

Founded by Don Pier Cesare De Vecchi, it preserves about 500 items listed: paintings, golden and painted wooden sculptures, furnishings, liturgical objects and sacred goldsmithery, mostly from the oldest parish, including a wooden pyramid altar of 1660. A painting by Melchiorre D'Enrico with the votive procession of the Confraternities of Campertogno at the Sacred Mount of Varallo stands out, after the plague that killed 28 people. Visits only by reservation (tel. 366 3719002).
The Foresi collections.
In the hamlets: the church of Tresilico contains a marble statue of the Madonna del Pilar (XVI-XVII century), that of Castellace a Madonna of Loreto in marble by G. B. Mazzolo dated 1542.
Perhaps the oldest portrait of Urban V.
Hiking trails on the summit and access to the historical park of Monte Sole da Vado.
The nature of the Alpago collected in a single didactic museum.
Natural amphitheatre at the foot of Monte Rosa, for moments of relaxation in contact with nature.
The residence of Spanish viceroys in the 16th and 17th centuries, in Piazza Hero dei Due Mondi, surmounted by the Clock Tower.
Panoramic road that crosses the Pennes Pass at 2,211 meters; from mid-June to mid-July the blooming of the rhododendrons transforms the steep pastures on the sides of the road into a red sea.

On the upper floor of the communicating Palazzo del Popolo and Palazzo del Capitano, from pre-Roman to modern times; there is the Coronation of the Virgin of Spain, already in the monastery of Montesanto.

It is located in the premises of the former Officine Moncenisio and exhibits relics, finds and photographic and graphic material donated by private and institutions, including documents on workshops during the war and on the arrival of the Allies. Library and media library preserve the audiovisual archive of the competition Historical Memory of the Valsusa Filmfest and the maps of the "Sentieri della memoria" on the mountain of Condove. Opening by reservation.
The theater of the square.
A few tens of meters from the Bàsura, a 50 meters gallery with a large side hall, not open to ordinary public.

In a restored former convent, it traces the territory from the eruptions of the Somma-Vesuvius and from the Bronze Age to the origins of Nola, to the Sannites with the painted tombs and the reproduction of the Knight's Tomb, to the Roman age with the statue of Dionysus with panther from the Villa of Somma Vesuviana, to the basilicas of Cimitile.
The medieval roots of the city of pasta, between water and mills.

Housed in Palazzo Bugliari, a building in the middle of the nineteenth century also seat of the Town Hall, it exhibits a complete reconstruction of the women's clothing arbëreshë: daily dresses, festive dresses, wedding ceremony and mourning.
A bakery that stayed the way it was.

Born from the fusion of the Diocesan Museum and the Civic Archaeological Museum, it is housed in the former monastery of Santa Maria del Popolo. The most important pieces are polychrome marbles illegally excavated in the territory in the seventies and returned to Italy in 2007 by the Getty Museum of Los Angeles: the masterpiece is the Trapezophoros (325-300 B.C.), support of a ritual canteen with two grifos that cling a deer, next to an archaic marble Apollo of the first century AD. Free admission; from Tuesday to Sunday 10-12 and 16.30-18.30 (times subject to change).

At the entrance of the village, the sculpture depicts a winged genius with pickaxes that light a fuse, in homage to the workers who brought in the water of the springs of Carpinello, some of whom died using explosives to break the rock.
The ruins of an imperial manor with views of the valley.

Set up in 1991 next to Villa Regina, it illustrates with educational tools the life and environment of the Vesuvian countryside in Roman times, with finds from houses of Pompeii and the rustic villas of Boscoreale (Villa della Pisanella, villa of Numerius Popidius Florus and others). Since the reopening of October 2023 a room is dedicated to the excavations of the villa of Civita Giuliana, with the ceremonial cart found in 2021. Same ticket as Villa Regina.
The remains of the Sannite and Roman city on the Via Appia: thermal baths, walls, public buildings and commercial spaces that tell the role of ancient Aeclanum in the traffics of ancient Italy.

In the Palazzo Malaspina at the top of the village, in front of the Tower of Dante, opened in 2005: over 9,000 books, 600 periodicals and 25,000 manuscript documents collected by Dario Manfredi, with permanent exhibitions on the expedition around the world of the navigator Alessandro Malaspina (born in Mulazzo in 1754), under the command of the Escubierta and Atrevida corvettes from 1789 to 1794. Visitable on request.
An eighteenth-century majolica floor.
Romanesque church of the 11th century with Romanesque-Gothic bell tower, one of the oldest in the city.
The menorahs carved into the rock of the Ibleans.
The Lombard baroque in the heart of Barbagia, with the painted crypt.

The houses of Pieve line up on the edge of the plateau, on top of a cliff excavated by glaciers about 423 meters above the lake. From the churchyard you arrive at Piazza Cozzaglio, with the old town hall and fountain and a wonderful view of the lake and Mount Baldo; in Via Scala Tonda 7 Arturo Cozzaglio was born and on the wall of the municipal archive the lion of San Marco recalls the Venetian domination. Nearby, thrills are suspended 350 meters above the lake.
A Roman aqueduct recently rediscovered.
The old town is enclosed in the walls of the medieval castle; it includes the church of the Assunta and a panoramic viewpoint.
The convent on the summit overlooking Lake Orta.

Municipality of Valle Maira scattered in small stone hamlets, connected by the ring of the Giro between the villages: in Vernetti, seat of the town hall, the ethnographic museum outdoors; in Toulouse and San Sebastiano the frescoes of the itinerant painter Giors Boneto (1807-1808); in Brieis the tower called "casa d'avoucat" .
Four-five-century frescoes in an isolated abbey.

Spa complex of late nineteenth century engineer Nicola Cianelli, rethought between 1950 and 1954 by Ignazio Gardella: the Ionic colonnade becomes an abstract diaphragm, a rose body connects to the historical facade and an air bridge combines thermal baths and hotels; inside remain the double-height atrium and a Neapolitan majolica floor.
A little church in the rock.

Elea was founded around 540 BC by exiles of Focea and was the seat of the Eleatic school of Parmenide and Zenone; the ruins, between Mediterranean maquis and olive groves, include the walls of about 5 km of the 6th century BC, Porta Marina Sud, the Porta Rosa (one of the oldest arches in the entire west), the Adriatic thermal baths with the mosaic of animals and marine monsters, the agorò today read as sanctuary of Asclepius and the Augustan cryptopic. On the acropolis the Roman theatre, an Ionian temple, the Angevin tower, the Palatine chapel and the church of Santa Maria, antiquarium sites. Open every day 8:30-19:30, last entry 18:30.
The Alps with the five senses.
The city seen from the foundations.

12th century church in the medieval square of Castiglione della Valle, a village known in ancient times as Castrum Leonis Vallis Sicilianae that in 1499 would host Lucrezia Borgia and Alfonso d'Aragona. It has a sailing bell tower with four bells and a two-door façade, the first with frescoed bezel and monolithic architrave; the interior with two naves (the left added in the unknown period) preserves Baroque decorations, eighteenth-century frescoes, a wooden ceiling and an organ of 1797. Opening hours not indicated: reference to the parish priest (tel. 328 1494172) or Pro Loco.
The millenarian olive trees and the 17th century church.
The noble residence of the 13th and 17th centuries; the chapel has a dome and the coats of arms of the Anguillara, Chigi and Farnese families. It is private but open to visitors.
From Entreves to Col de la Seigne: narrow and wild at the entrance, then a flat basin; in front of the glacier the lake of Miage.
Borgo Bandiera Arancione del Monferrato degli infernot, linked to the painter Angelo Morbelli, with the giant bench among the vineyards.
Dunes, basins and ravines between sea and olive groves.
Castle wanted and built by Gennaro Della Monica, indicated by the Abruzzo Region among the places to visit.
The alpine village in stone and wood.

Taste the nougat where it is born.

Established in 1884 in the Temple of St. John the Sepulchre and opened in 1958, it collects the civic collection and the findings emerged in the historical center and province.
From Casona to Monte Belvedere.
The 18th-century Town Hall, on the main square, houses a gallery with works by Claudio Ridolfi, including the altarpiece of the Coronation of the Virgin and saints dated 1630.

Walk under the arcades.
It tells the local culture and the processing of sea linen, the sea silk.

Established in 2013 in the house of the family Caira-Vitti, it preserves photographs, postcards and sketches of the late nineteenth and early twentieth century of the Académie Vitti, Paris' private art studio active until 1914.

Vetriolo, a spa resort at altitude, is the starting point for excursions to Panarotta, Monte Fravort and the Lagorai chain; in winter the Panarotta offers alpine skiing, cross-country skiing, snowshoeing and ski touring.

In the neoclassical palace wanted by Count Luigi Tadini and built between 1821 and 1824 on a project by Sebastiano Salimbeni, with the windows on the lake and the ceilings painted by Luigi Dell'Era; the Academy, established in 1829, is one of the oldest museums in Lombardy. In 23 rooms: the Religion and the Tadini Stele by Antonio Canova, paintings by Jacopo Bellini, Antonio and Bartolomeo Vivarini, Paris Bordon, Giacomo Ceruti and three paintings by Francesco Hayez, as well as porcelain by Meissen, Sèvres and Naples.
The walk between palm trees and pinewoods on the sea.
A villa of brianzola delight with the nymphaeum of Neptune in the park.

On the Valentine's Day of Above: up to 53 spectators and a "Cosmos Simulator" for virtual trips around the Earth, between the rings of Saturn and deep space; regular shows in German and Italian, by reservation.

Part of Monte Albo belongs to Irgoli: paths through the woods towards the white peak of sos Aspros, habitat of muflon and royal eagle, along the path the pinnettos, circular huts of the shepherds in stone and wood. The wood of ancient oaks of Talache is recommended.
Vercelli's art gallery.

Land of the upper Garda Brescia gathered around the port, with the municipal palace of the end of the sixteenth century that preserves in the lake wall the balls of cannon fired by an Austrian ship in 1866, the church of San Giacomo of the twelfth century, Villa Feltrinelli, Villa Bettoni in Bogliaco and the lemon trees, cultivated here since the thirteenth century.
The family home of the founder of Bank of America.
The church of Blessed Egidio.

On a sunny hill, built before the year 1000, it has one of the oldest facades of Cuneo and is frescoed by the brothers Biazaci, painters of Buschesi who in the fifteenth century realized more than thirty fresco works and on table in the territory.

The parish church dominates the But valley from above and is the final stage of the Carnic section of Romea Strata da Cercivento. The Zuglio Museum displays the furnishings of a first basilica dating from the 6th to the 9th century and the sculptures of the altar of Domenico da Tolmezzo.
The silver bust of Saint Philip Neri.
A tour of the center between castle and mother church.
On the first floor of the Bishop's Palace, inaugurated in 1984 by the Curia.

On the Lattari Mountains, Gragnano is the city of pasta: the Valle dei Mulini, a thirteenth-century hydraulic complex that ground the wheat, the nineteenth-century square of the historic pasta factories, the large church of Corpus Domini with works by Luca Giordano and Domenico Morelli, and in the hamlet of Castello the church of Santa Maria Assunta, a national monument since 1927.
The oldest fountain in the country.
The walk through porticos and painted palaces.

The village can be reached only on foot through a door and winds through alleys and small steps; it is one of the few historical centers of Italy entirely pedestrian and preserves towers, walkways, rivets, wounds and medieval casematte. An order of 1397 sentenced to death those who opened a gap as wide as a person in the walls. The Porta di Santa Maria (Porta Reatina) has a clock that still marks the hours according to the medieval system.

Urban-rustic villa that touched the maximum splendor between the I and II century AD, with mosaics, service environments and an area of ecological rebalancing around.
Among the streams Resco and Ciuffenna the formations of sand and clay carved by the erosion that inspired Leonardo.

Basin born from the artificial barrier of the river Lete, between the lake of Gallo and the village, in a well preserved natural landscape; on the lake there is an information point (the "Kioschetto").

Narrow streets and houses in live stone or tuff with external stairs and stone walls, sometimes open on small squares full of votive newsstands. In the main square, Piazza Umberto I, overlook the Clock Tower, the church of the Immaculate One called "Foresi" (the Foresi), the entrance arch of the castle and a refined newsstand decorated with stucco; along Via Oberdan there is the ancient ornamental fountain of the Testuggini (the Testuggini). The refuge of Lucrezia d'Alagno, then Totò.

On the hill at 890 meters, a castle perhaps Longobard (mid IX century), of Norman-Svevo plant, rebuilt by the Aragonese nobility; in 1556 Luigi Carafa of Stigliano bought Volturara and added a chapel of San Michele. Ruined by the earthquakes of 1561, 1688 and 1694, the mast remains, a quadrangular court of about 25 by 30 meters and four corner towers up to 12 meters high; the earthquake of 23 November 1980 destroyed much of the church of San Michele Arcangelo, of which remains the skeleton.
Golenal forest along the Rhine with a visit route and summer exits for fireflies.

In Palazzo Olginati, dating back to the fifteenth century, donated to the Municipality by the last heir of the family, provided that a museum dedicated to Garibaldi, which stayed there in 1866; inaugurated in 1932, currently reported in temporary closing.

Borgo del Molise centrale known for the Grano Festival, which every July 26th for over two centuries brings in procession in honor of Sant'Anna the 'traglie', wagons without wheels decorated with braided ears; the tradition is told in the Museo della Traglia, in the former church of Piazza Chiesa Madre, and in the Museo di Comunità hosted in the Convento di Santa Maria delle Grazie.
Pebble beach from the green sea with a pool of sulphur water from a natural spring, linked to the proximity of Vesuvius; on the state road 145, to the north, the Scraio Thermal Baths founded in 1895.

It preserves the Holy Face, a very fine and transparent veil of about 17 x 24 cm with the image of a face of man, arrived at Manoppello according to tradition in 1506, and preserved in a silver reliquary of Neapolitan eighteenth century on the main altar in polychrome marble (1914). The complex, rebuilt between 1848 and 1965 with a façade in white and pink stone, preserves of the seventeenth century phase only the chapel of 1686; annexed to the "treoro" with a wooden tabernacle and a seventeenth-century painting of the Emilian school.
Tower of the historic center, today privately owned, with very thick walls in black stone. During World War II it was used as a refuge from the bombings.

Borgo Bandiera Arancione on the Lepini Mountains overlooking the Pontina Plain, dominated by the Caetani Castle of the 13th century and closed by Renaissance walls; at the foot of Mount Corvino the Cistercian Abbey of Valvisciolo, linked to the legend of the Templars.
The oldest church of Montefeltro and the Romanesque Cathedral with its bell tower: the "campo dei miracoli" of Romagna.
Lake Maggiore of the literary holiday of the nineteenth century.

Borgo del Canavese at the gates of Ivrea, dominated by the castle of the Bishops of Ivrea that Alfredo d'Andrade bought in 1885 and restored in medieval style: around the stone shelter, the churches of Sant'Andrea, San Rocco and Madonna delle Grazie, the chapel of San Grato with frescoes of Giacomo di Ivrea and the paths of the Paraj Auta on the Morenic Amphitheatre.

Country 339 meters at the confluence of the Biscubio in the Candigliano, under Mount Nerone and Montiego, feud of the Brancaleoni counts that transformed the medieval fortress in the great Castle Brancaleoni, now home of the Civic Museum; surroundings of gorges, canyons and paths.
The parish church of the capital, with a canvas of Veronese.

In the historic center a plaque marks the house where, on July 7, 1901, the actor and director Vittorio De Sica, author of films such as "Ieri," today and tomorrow, "La Ciociara" and "Pane," love and...

Medieval village overlooking the sea, linked to the Allied landing on 22 January 1944: the Fort Sangallo with the Museum of Landing and the Antiquarium, the American Cemetery, the sanctuary of Santa Maria Goretti, the village with Palazzo Doria-Pamphilj and, to the south, the castle of Torre Astura.

Outdoor museum in Punta Navaccia, designed by Pietro Cascella: a spiral of 27 columns-sculpture in local stone, about 4.5 meters high, leading to a central table with a solar symbol; the works were realized between 1985 and 1989 by Italian and foreign artists, including Mauro Staccioli, Joe Tilson and Leo Lionni.
€2 (free residents and children up to 5 years)

A complex spread in the historic centre, active since 2004, using the mineral water ferruginous of the Fonte Sant'Antonio, praised as early as 1635 by the prince bishop Carlo Emanuele Madruzzo: inhalations, balneotherapy, hydropinic treatments, wellness area with sauna, Turkish bath and salt cave, outdoor swimming pool and in summer Kneipp routes along the Sarca. Seasonal opening from spring to November 30.
The majolica of a 20th century sculptor in a town of the Serre.
An imposing work, rich in symbols and of great craftsmanship according to the tourist portal of Reggiano.
Church dating back to the year about 1000 which preserves some original frescoes.
€3 whole; free of charge and first Sunday of the month
Church of 1616 that preserves a wooden choir and remains of the ancient local ceramic flooring.
The largest ancient theatre in Campania.

The oldest nucleus, of medieval plant, rises on the top of a mountain, with the morconi of Lauro rocks to strengthen its slopes and the Morconi of San Tommaso rocks to act as a scenery to the parish church. The Church of St. Nicholas is cited as a testimony to the ancient times of the country.
The great exhibitions in the heart of the Contrada.

The large council hall of the Town Hall, in Villa Piovene, hosts a permanent exhibition of archaeological finds of the territory, mostly ceramics, from the Bronze Age to the late imperial age, arranged in four large windows. Free entrance during the opening hours of the Town Hall.
Stone portals and carved balconies.
A Nativity at the bottom of the lake.
The three-legged bell tower, unique in the Langa.
It rises in the hamlet Blessed Virgin of Ono Degno, in memory of a miracle of 1601, when the little Catherine Dusi saw tears come down from the eyes of a painted image of the Virgin.

On the piazza d'armi overlook the governor's palace, the pavilion of the officers and the church; inside three military quarters, the powder keg of St. Ignatius and a royal door. This is where the covered staircase starts.

The centre of the Belice Valley is dominated by the Gryfeo Castle, one of the best preserved medieval fortresses in western Sicily, home to the Museum of the prehistory of Belice; in June the historic centre is covered with the Infiorata flower carpets.

Beach of almost 2 km of gravel and clear sand under Mount Sant'Elia, with beaches and free stretches and waters suitable for snorkeling and diving; in front, accessible by swimming, the rock with a spontaneous olive tree of over 400 years, symbol of the coast.

The family foundry has been producing bells for about a millennium with traditional methods: craftsmen prepare models, guide molten metal and shape bells, and in 1924 Pius XI granted her the papal coat of arms. The museum, founded in 1999 and named after John Paul II (visiting Agnone in 1995), exhibits sacred bronzes including a bell of the year about 1000, tools, documents and a Dutch edition of 1664 of De tintinnabulis; in the workshop you can see ovens and melting pits and you can watch a bell concert.
The cippi of the Claudia Augusta street.
The iron fountain.

In the hamlet of Raffo, about 2 km from the village, a large still active salt mine produces the 'salte di Sicilia': the deposit, among the richest in Europe, covers about 2 km2 with thicknesses up to 250 meters. Inside the mine, the Museum of Salt exhibits sculptures of artists' rooms from all over the world; access is provided with protective measures.
A forest towards the valley of Virgilio.

City on the Strait of Messina, rebuilt after the earthquake of 1908 on roads parallel to the sea: the National Archaeological Museum with the Bronzes of Riace, the Lungomare Falcomatà with the Greek walls and the Roman baths, the Aragonese Castle, the Church of the Ottimati and the Duomo.
The sculptures of Castro, the missing city.
The alpine forest-memorial.
The relic at the center of the devotion of the country.

Built in the fourteenth century by the Confraternita dei Disciplini Bianchi, enlarged in the fifteenth century and dedicated to Saint Bernardino in 1452. On the east façade the frescoes of 1485 by Giacomo Borlone de Buschis: at the top the Triumph of Death with the encounter of the three living and the three dead, at the center the Dance Macabra with people of every class led by skeletons. Inside the Stories of Jesus in 42 squares on three bands (31 visible) and a Crucifixion over the arch of the presbytery.

In the castle, the Museo dell'Opera rises on an archaeological area linked to the early cathedral of Sant'Antonino of the 11th century and preserves architectural, sculptural and archaeological remains, including Byzantine finds; the Museum of Emigration and Rural Civilization collects about 200 objects on the emigration and agricultural life of the Irpini. Visits by reservation.
The 17th century forge along the King's Vase, today's museum, where you can watch the iron work with the hammer moved by water, know handed down by the Frear family.

Three-nave church built in the town of Scozola, where the bishop of Pavia Liutardo (841-864) established a monastic community; in 1535 monastery and lands passed to the Major Hospital of Milan. The present building is a Romanesque reconstruction with apses and bell tower; inside the Disputa di santa Caterina d'Alessandria (1503) by Bernardino Zenale, the Last Supper of Tarillo da Curia (1581), eighteenth-century frescoes by Bellotti and a wooden crucifix.

Also known as the Purgatory, where once the walls were finished under the Monterosso hill: interior covered with different marbles (white, peach flower, Medici breach, portor) and marble portal of the workshop of Carlo Finelli.

On the ancient acropolis of Kroton, at the highest point of the city, between the sea and the countryside: rebuilt in the current forms since 1541 by the Viceroy Pedro de Toledo on a project by Giangiacomo D'Acaja and Giovanni Maria Buzzacarino, a polygonal plan with the bastions of San Giacomo and Santa Caterina; it houses the Civic Museum and the Municipal Library.

In the Town Hall the Dante Room with the Majesty of Lippo Memmi, the Podestà Room with the frescoes of Azzo di Masetto (1290) and the Pinacoteca with Filippino Lippi, Benozzo Gozzoli and Pinturicchio; from the same entrance you climb on the Grossa Tower, 54 meters, built in 1311.
The remains of the castle on the highest hill.
History and environment of the valley in a palace of Garibaldi.

City founded by the Ausoni and Roman colony from 334 BC, crossed today by the Autostrada del Sole: there are still walls with six doors (some sections of the 5th century BC), the passage in rock of the Ponte delle Monache, the amphitheatre of the 1st century BC, the central thermal baths with stuccoes and the northern ones on three levels along the cardo that follows the Via Latina, a temple on podium, probably Capitolium. The theatre, perhaps from the 2nd century B.C. and enlarged in the Augustan age, has the cavea on double arc galleries in cross-linked work, without more steps.

Façade with two overlapping orders; it houses burials of noble families, wooden statues and marbles of St. Anne of the mid seventeenth century and the Madonna of the Audience of the mid sixteenth century attributed to the Gagini.

Piceno village dominated by the Rocca degli Acquaviva, with a cylindrical mast of 22 meters from which the look ranges from the Adriatic to the Sibillini; in the historical center the Gothic Gate, the Civic Tower and churches like San Rocco, the oldest in the country, and outside the walls the Franciscan monastery.
A walk in the woods for families.
A large Marian shrine recently built in the hamlet of Fontanelle, in eclectic style with a large dome; in the garden the chapel of the Addolorata, a cave of Lourdes and the monument to the Fallen.

Borgo at the foot of the Laga Mountains, in the National Park of Gran Sasso and Monti della Laga, almost completely destroyed by the earthquake of 24 August 2016: today you can visit the temporary civic museum "Floriana Svizzeretto" with the works saved and restored, the Laboratory Renaissance and the Polo del Gusto, as well as Lake Scandarello, Oasi Orie Terme and Conca Amatriciana, home of the spaghetti to the Amatriciana STG.

The centre, at the foot of the castle, conserves historic buildings: among the most interesting are the eighteenth-century Palazzo Molinari, known for its stonework, and then Palazzo De Rogatis, Palazzo Del Buono and Palazzo Donatelli, with numerous churches including those of Monte Carmelo, the Presentation of Maria and San Rocco.
Medieval castle recognizable for the two imposing side towers; in the village the church of Sant'Andrea Corsini preserves paintings attributed to the Polinori.
Benedictine-Norman Abbey with a large Renaissance cloister, today seat of the Faculty of Architecture; according to the MiC a section of the Diocesan Museum is being set up.
Next to the castle.
A corner of Far West in Valcuvia, also loved by schoolchildren.

Pre-Roman center of the Frentani and then Roman town hall, Larinum was abandoned in the 9th century for Saracen raids. The amphitheatre of flavia age (69-96 A.D.), oval of almost 100 for 80 meters and capable according to italia.it of about 5,000 spectators, preserves arena, podium, the lower cavea and corridors of the first level; next, thermal buildings with geometric mosaics, marine and fantastic animals, a paved road with shops and houses (the iconic of the kantharos) and a mosaic with groupers and octopus from a domus of Republican age. Open from Tuesday to Saturday 9-13, other visits by reservation (0874 822787).
The symbol of the judicial city.

Tarcento, between mountains and plains along the river Torre, is known for its liberty villas and the remains of ancient castles; in the 17th-17th century Palazzo Frangipane is home to the Natural Archaeological Museum, with one of the most important European collections of trilobites, while on the hill of Coja dominates the neo-Gothic Villa Moretti with its park.
visits by reservation (prolocosangemini@gmail.com)
Giotto Pass €20 whole, €7 from 7 to 14 years; Ghiberti Pass (without Bell Tower) €15 and €5
A Renaissance chapel returned to the life of the country.
The room of the lovers.
Free shores; paid bathing services

About 86 km2 of sea between Capo Boi and the island of Serpentara, divided into two bays from the cape of Capo Carbonara: granite pinnacles with sea daisies and red gorgonies, posidonia prairies and the pinna nobilis, barracuda to the Variglioni, groupers and breams to the dry of Cala Caterina and wrecks including a Roman jail, a 15th century Aragonese sailboat and the steamboat Egle (1943). Forbidden fishing, year-round diving with authorized diving; a path in the spot connects the head to Porto Giunco.
A venerated Byzantine icon in the heart of Este.
Visitable by reservation (Pro Loco, tel. 0827 44060 / 0827 44147)

In Li Parisi, on the border with Trinità d'Agultu and Vignola: a basin of rounded granite boulders, some with human or animal shapes, with tafoni used as shelters, cork oaks and arbutes; hiking trails, mountain biking and horse riding and a viewpoint on the provincial road 74. Set of the movie "The Free Prince" (2018).
An isolated little church above the Gulf of Lacona.
One of the oldest mechanical nativity scenes in Italy; a small museum nearby preserves historical pieces, including the engine of a 1937 representation, and a photo gallery.
International route between the Stura Valley and France, with a hairpin road very loved by motorcyclists; on top, on a prairie, the Lake of Maddalena opens.
The Norman mother church.
A village on the water, between walls, carruggi and harps.
The 16th century frescoes of San Rocco.
Postcard landscapes.
The ascolan theatre season.
The burials of the children's necropolis.
The daily museum, objects like works of art.

It tells of the birth of telecommunications, from the first remote communication systems to the telegraph of Samuel Morse, with 81 exhibits, the oldest a telegraph of 1870 in the rooms of a historical building; the route includes a film on the history of the telegraph and an interactive game to write in Morse code with the button of a telegraphic station reconstructed in 3D printing. Timetable indicated by the Museum Network: Wednesday, Thursday and Friday 10.30-12 and 16-18.

Bagnara is considered to be the capital of the swordfish, and its symbol is the "bagnarota" with a basket in the head from which the sword of the fish comes; the Torrone di Bagnara IGP is still handmade with traditional ingredients, and the area produces the Costa Viola IGT wine.
open to the public only on special occasions (FAI)

Special protection zone for birds of about 800 hectares between wetlands, ponds, meadows and woods, birdwatcher destination. At the gates of the valleys, south of San Martino Spino, the Barchessone Vecchio, a singular sixteen-sided building born as a stopover station of horses (the boats were the host of the army horses until 1861), of municipal property: open Saturday and Sunday 15.30-19.30 with free bike rental on weekends. The nearby Barchessone Portovecchio, with a collection of equestrian and rural traditions, is visited on the second Sunday of the month.

Rural seat of the Teutonic Order: a hospice was built there in 1200, when the crossing road passed on the Renon, to accommodate the travelers, change the horses and cure the sick. The current building, a large walled cube with a pavilion roof, dates back to about 1650; in the majolica stove rooms and stucco ceilings and upholstery with biblical scenes and the history of the Order. Today Renon's cultural centre with concerts and events; visits in season, included in the RittenCard.

Of medieval origin, in the thirteenth century depended on the abbey of Rambona and in 1215 hosted Saint Francis on his way to Loreto; a cloister connects her to the Teatro Verdi. It houses frescoes and a altarpiece with Sant'Antonio da Padova on a gold background by Lorenzo d'Alessandro da San Severino.
The Romanesque of Sabina.

A multipurpose cultural centre founded in 1998 in a former steel mill, with the contribution of the European Union and its citizens; it is part of the Parco della Fantasia (Fantasia Park) Gianni Rodari. On two floors he exhibits home objects of the local companies (Alessi, Bialetti, Lagostina, Girmi, Calderoni and others) and tells the industrial history from the nineteenth century to the present day, with temporary exhibitions.

He kept the Holy Spina, which tradition attributed to the crown of Christ and which according to the chronicles was reddened in 1693 and on February 3, 1710; a notary act of August 3, 1805 recalls another episode during a penitential procession, repeated again every August 3.
The 19th century living room.
The viewpoint on the ternan basin.
A medieval village with views from the sea to Majella.
In the villages of Triatel and Étirol, between raccard, grandze and grenier, tells the history, work and social organization of this small ancient world; the visit ends at the mill on the stream.
The seventeenth-century mother church and the memory of the fallen of the country.

The headquarters of the David Maria Turoldo Study Centre, founded in 2019 by an association founded in 1992, which takes care of its restoration and guided tours; it is an example of a Friulian rural house with courtyard, porch, kitchen on the ground floor, two bedrooms on the first floor and attic with conference room and small library, with walls in cobbles of the Tagliamento and fragments of terracotta. The two rooms of the Turoldo family retain the original structure. Open Saturday and Sunday 9-18, only by reservation by email.
The fortress on the red jasper overlooking the Ceno valley.
One of Montiferru's most spectacular waterfalls.
In front of the church and the square, it collects finds from prehistory to the Roman era found in the area and fossils preserved in the layers of sedimentary stone on which the village stands.

Built a few years after the earthquake of 1783 on the initiative of Maria Antonia Grimaldi Serra; in the Chapel of the Immaculate Mary Teresa Grimaldi's remains have been resting since 1793 and died in the earthquake.
The oldest of the bridges that connect the two villages of the village on the Marmore stream.
The handmade paper in a paper mill of the eighteenth century.
A break in the shade of secular trees in the center.

Romanesque church of the XII century, enriched in the fourteenth century and with a nineteenth-century portico, built on foundations of the IX century still visible in the lower part of the stone walls, pebbles and bricks.
The Latin altars, in the place of the myth of Enea.
Art exhibitions in a neo-Gothic castle surrounded by a historical park.
Next to the Duomo, it preserves three exultets, scrolls illustrated in parchment of Benedictine production, around the thousand, used in medieval religious functions.
The large church of the high city.
Nobile villas and you will suck over the lake.
In the former Carmelino church, awards and memories of the great Mantua pilot.
The walls on the Cesenade hill.
Several paths link the coast to the mountains, from the sea to the woods.

Borgo della Ciociaria built in dark basalt, gathered around the Baronale Castle of the Column and the 36-metre Clock Tower, with access from the ancient doors of the Melangolo and the Olive Tree; it houses the Prehistoric Civic Museum        • Pietro Fedele • which houses the cranial cap of the Man of Ceprano called Argil.
A dazzle of cobbled alleys with noble palaces of the sixteenth century, the Baroque churches of Sant'Angelo and San Domenico and the Clock Tower of 1604.
The neo-Gothic church on the square.
A noble palace to visit.
The honorary arch erected in 27 BC at the end of the Via Flaminia, the oldest preserved Roman arch.

The first beach of Abruzzo is part, with Alba Adriatica and Tortoreto Lido, 13 kilometers of uninterrupted beaches with Blue Flag; in summer in the evening you can enjoy establishments, beach bars and lounge bars with music.
The 14th-century cathedral on the square of the ancient Roman forum; from the right aisle you enter the Christian Museum.

Founded between 1321 and 1327 by Aquilina di Monteserico, lady of Genzano, on the ruins of a manor of the twelfth century, it was inhabited by the Clarisses until 1905 and then used for civil functions. It was opened on the FAI Days of Spring and Autumn 2025.
The pilgrimage of Pentecost with a view of the Coast.
Built between 1672 and 1682 by the Duke Antonio Maria Ceva Grimaldi, feudalist of Solopaca, who settled there with the family.

The village, destroyed by the earthquake of 1783 and rebuilt, preserves houses with carved granite portals, wooden loggias and wrought iron railings, work of the craftsmen called for in the centuries by the presence of the Certosa. The axis is Corso Umberto I, paved in granite in the second half of the nineteenth century and flanked by late Baroque churches.

Fortified village on a spur of Mount Letegge, contested in the thirteenth century between Camerino and San Severino and fortified by Camerino at the beginning of the fourteenth century; there are the church of San Lorenzo and, downstream, the church of Madonna del Ponte.

Borgo della Valnerina was born around the castle of the Arroni, with the upper part of the Terra and the district of Santa Maria with the collegiate frescoed in 1516; in the territory of Casteldilago, the sanctuary of the Madonna dello Scoglio and the Black River Park.

Church excavated in tuff in the 10th century in the Lagnoni district, enlarged between the Three and the fifteenth century: it preserves the frescoes of the Inventio Crucis with the history of Elena in search of the Cross, a rare subject in Puglia.
In the historic centre, designed by the architect Luigi Maria Valadier.
The opera in Rome.
Monumental tree just outside the village; the name comes from the tradition that in the Middle Ages women accused of witchcraft met secretly.
The fourteenth-century church with façade rebuilt since 1621; it houses the Golden Chapel (or Golden Grotto), decorated in wood and pure gold, and the codes of the Amanuense monks.

Mining complex between Arbus and Guspini, part of the Park Geominerario of Sardinia: the first concession was given in 1848 to Giovanni Antonio Sanna and the activity lasted until the final closure of 1991; in 1865 it was the most important mine of the Kingdom with 1,100 workers. Four itineraries of visit: the Palazzina of the direction (1870-77) with the blue room and the church of Santa Barbara, the well Sant'Antonio, the workshops with the foundry of 1885 and the Piccalinna route with the winch of the late nineteenth century.
Church of the historic center marked by the Abruzzo Region among the main stages of the visit.
€3,50, reduced €3, family €7
The collegiate church of the XII-XIII centuries houses, on the left side of the nave, the Baglioni Chapel frescoed in 1501 by Bernardino di Betto called the Pinturicchio.

Fortification of the XIII-XIV centuries of about 13,000 square meters with about 200 small rural houses, four round towers at the corners and a large tower-door to the south; shelter in war and warehouse of grapes, wine and wheat in peace, with rue cobbled in slope.
Public beaches with pinewoods behind, suitable for families and snorkeling; the promenade is a meeting point with summer events.
Where the bees ran.
The fifteenth-century church on the lake.
Seat of the Scuola di Alto Musicale Foundation.
Three-nave church with frescoes on the central cap, on the plumes and in the presbytery; in the choir the great altarpiece of San Giorgio painted by Felice Campi in 1795.
the MiC card indicates visits only by reservation required at least one week before
Panoramic point of the old town with a view of the surrounding villages; the name comes from the Latin .

Museum distributed in three locations: Casa Pirinu with the naturalistic and fauna section, the former Montegranatico with minerals and fossils (managed by the mineralogical association Domusnovae) and the exhibition room of the municipal library with archaeological finds. Casa Pirinu and the library are visited on request to the Municipality; the former Montegranatico opens in winter from 17 to 19 and in summer from 18 to 20.

The municipality of Valle Trompia is linked to the tradition of iron, with the Museum "I Magli" in the sixteenth-century forge, the 17th-century parish church of Santi Faustino e Giovita, Palazzo Avogadro in Zanano with frescoes between the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, a stretch of the Roman aqueduct of Brixia and the sanctuary of Sant'Emiliano that dominates the middle valley.
From the Neolithic to the twentieth century in a Renaissance palace.
The diamond-pointed façade of the sanctuary.
A Greek village clinging to the rock above the river.
Castles is at the edge of the park: excursions to Monte Camicia (2,750 m) and the plateau of Campo Imperatore.

Three waterfalls formed by the stream San Giulio in a wooded environment, between 324 and 474 meters above sea level, where the watercourse goes down to curves with sudden jumps before the village. Only the first is reachable, with a path that starts from the ancient part of the village following the signs from Via Pianella and that requires a lot of attention.
The town square of the village.
An open-air museum of 140 engraved rocks.
About 500 cavities dug by fishermen from the mid-nineteenth century to the sixties to store nets and boats, with colored doors and recovery materials.

The sanctuary is located near the remains of a nuragic village and the necropolis of the end of the III-IV century AD, which has returned funerary furnishings and stems decorated today at the Archaeological Museum; in the church of San Leonardo the simulacrum of San Giovanni Evangelista is kept.

The largest architectural complex of the village, built on an ancient castle: Cardinal Ennio Filonardi had it transformed, around 1530 and on a project attributed to Jacopo Barozzi called the Vignola (his Renaissance portal), into a summer residence of the papal court, dedicated to Paul III in 1532. It preserves mullioned windows, monumental staircases and the floor of a salon with heraldic engravings of the Farnese and Della Rovere.
The great neo-Gothic on the castle square.

A fifteenth-century complex renovated in the seventeenth century, with frescoes from the early eighteenth century in the nave and the seventeenth century in the cloister. It is located to the south-west of the village, on the road to Mount Santa Trinità (411 m), from which you can enjoy a beautiful view.
The Liberty Theatre of the City of Care.
In the former Dominican convent, the Pinacoteca civica, with the Ebe by Antonio Canova, and the great art exhibitions of national breath.
Calanchi, chestnuts and karstism on the plateau.
The prehistoric monument that gave the name to the municipality.
In the former convent of the Augustinians there are 1,300 objects and tools of daily peasant life.
A romantic park around a neoclassical villa.
Entirely frescoed by Gaudenzio Ferrari and his circle, with the cycle of the Life of the Virgin by Julius Cesare Luini (1542).
Templar church with counter-facade frescoes, including the "Nablus Clash."
The village among the vineyards.
One of the less known archaeological sites of the Florentine area, reported by Visit Tuscany among the five to discover.
Cultural center of African ethnography in the Sommariva Village, with a collection of masks, fetishes, weapons, paintings and statues.
The city of cotton told by his cars.
Two churches side by side on the highest point of the village.

The inhabited nucleus, once called Villa, preserves its steep alleys; the eighteenth-century parish church of San Pietro in Vincoli, with a separate bell tower overlooking the centre, stands in front of a belvedere. From the village, at 836 meters, the panorama embraces the Ivrea Moraine Serra and its five lakes.

18th century church built on a plot donated by the Bernasconi family, with a single nave with a small bell tower. The baroque façade alternates concavity and convexity; on the portal a fresco of the Adoration of the Magi and a half bust in stone of Christ blessing. It preserves relics of the Magi, partly from the Basilica of Sant'Eustorgio in Milan, and inside trompe-l'œil decorations and eighteenth-century paintings.

Country of the Po golena, feud of the Pallavicino since 1413, with the fifteenth-century fortress that houses the chapel frescoed by Bonifacio Bembo and the Aquarium and Ethnographic Museum of the Po, the collegiate church of San Lorenzo and the oasis along the river.
In Palazzo Pompei, designed by Sanmicheli, sixteen rooms dedicated to rocks and minerals, paleontology and zoology, with a collection of fossils of particular importance.

On the north side of Piazza Luini, in the complex Casa parrocchiale - Teatro comunale that was of the Scuola Maggiore dei Laici (active from the fifteenth to the eighteenth century), exhibits valuable furnishings from the churches of Ponte; one room was the ancient Oratorio dei Disciplini and preserves frescoes of Fermo Stella.
The January fires.

Built in 1931-32 with the work of the inhabitants, who brought sand and gravel from the Rio Verde; in the apse the triptych of Jacopino Longo with the Madonna and Child and the Saints Giacomo and Donato (1546), stolen in 1997 and returned by the Carabinieri in 2000. The organ is by Antonio Mola (1898); on the same square remains the old parish church of the late seventeenth-early eighteenth century.
The finds of Santu Antine.

Medieval village at about 342 meters in the Peligna basin, at the foot of the western slope of Mount Morrone. The name "Pratola" first appeared in 997 in a agricultural contract of the Chronicon Volturnense; fief of Charles II of Anjou, in 1294 was assigned to the abbot of the monastery of Holy Spirit al Morrone, and since then his history is linked to Celestine V and his monks. In the territory there are still local beans (bread and ... Gentile) and red garlic of Sulmona.

The ancient heart of the village gathers the Mother Church of St. Nicholas, already existing at the beginning of the 14th century, rebuilt in the 16th and rebuilt in the fifties of the twentieth century after the collapse of the roof, with some altars remained intact; the Church of the SS. Rosario, built in 1562 in Renaissance style, with rosette and crowning tooth; the chapel of the Crucifix next to the Norman castle, the Palazzo Marchesale, the Church of St. Joseph and the Civic Museum.
Walk to the village.

Itinerary in the woods along the Rio stream leading to one of the major ancient sites of production of gunpowder, obtained by mixing sulphur and salter; along the path the "pillo" is a hole in the sandstone used as a mortar, and the "mazzapicchio" is a wooden instrument moved by the force of water.
The Walser village.
The indigenous city discovered by its registered tiles.

A search covers more common together, limited to the right official website (e.g. Emilia Romagna Turismo, Ravenna Turismo), and the results are immediately saved in the notes: no page is searched twice.
The square dominated by the great altar of the country in white marble and the fifteenth-century Palazzo Venezia; from the terraces of the Vittoriano a wide panorama.

A circular village of 70 metres in diameter of the medium bronze (1450-1400 BC), founded on almost five thousand poles; UNESCO site since 2011 among the prehistoric palafittic sites of the Alps. You don't visit: it is only approached by boat without engine and an installation is on the opposite side, near Viverone.

Villa Almerico Capra Valmarana, inspired by the Pantheon with four identical facades and the central circular hall under the dome, model for the White House; open all year round, in winter only with guided tours by reservation on Saturday morning.

Made by Enrico Scrovegni in 1303-1305 and frescoed by Giotto in 855 days: 38 stories of the Virgin and Christ on a thousand square meters, the Virtues and the Vizi, the universal Judgment and the starry sky; it stands on the area of the Roman amphitheatre.
